title: [epic] Wave 2026-09-29 out-of-territory findings
body:
### Wave

2026-09-29

### Where these findings came from

The final security review of PR #259 (publish-path hardening) at 4cb6729, 2026-09-29. Its verdict was MERGE, and these are its minors. The owner decided the same day to file them here. Each finding is one comment below.

### Recorded elsewhere, deliberately not duplicated here

- The forge token sent to any host by the clone and the publish probe: #307 (S0).
- Rewritable step specs: #342 (S0).

title: The agent runtime image leaves out tofu, tflint and trivy until a release of each passes the HIGH CVE scan
body:
### What happened

The agent-runtime-base image from #435 (wave 1, B6) ships 8 of the 11 CLI tools the build spec asks for: gh, gcloud, kubectl, terraform, checkov, shellcheck, make and docker. **tofu, tflint and trivy are left out.** When #435 was built (2026-10-01), every published release of each of those three carried a fixable HIGH CVE. The release image scan refuses that, as it should.

### What you expected

All 11 tools in the image, with the image scan passing and no waiver.

### Decision

Owner, 2026-10-01: ship the 8 now. Add the 3 when a release of each passes the scan. No `.trivyignore` waiver.

### To close

For each of tofu, tflint and trivy, check the latest release against the image scan. Add the tool once its release is clean, and say in the PR which release and scan run showed it clean.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Check 2026-10-07 (lane C4E, task_32a78c63af6e4582b9de). No change made; stays open.**

Scan: `trivy 0.75.0 rootfs --scanners vuln --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed`, DB 2026-10-07T00:53Z, each artifact sha256-matched to the Dockerfile pin.

| tool | latest release | result |
|---|---|---|
| trivy | v0.75.0 (2026-10-01) | **0 findings, already in the image on main** (`TRIVY_VERSION=0.75.0`, unconditional install) |
| tofu | v1.13.1 (2026-10-01) | 3 fixable HIGH: x/mod 0.39.0 (CVE-2026-56864, CVE-2026-56865, fixed 0.40.0), grpc 1.83.1 (CVE-2026-84445, fixed 1.83.2) |
| tflint | v0.64.0 (2026-07-17, newest) | 17 fixable HIGH: Go stdlib 1.26.3 (11, fixed 1.26.6), x/crypto 0.53.0 (CVE-2026-56854), x/mod 0.37.0 (2), grpc 1.82.0 (CVE-2026-84304, CVE-2026-84445, GHSA-hrxh-6v49-42gf) |

Control: an unexecutable extracted tflint scanned empty (trivy's Go-binary analyzer skips files without the exec bit); after `chmod +x` it showed the 17. An empty scan is not a clean binary.

Left: flip `INSTALL_TOFU_TFLINT` to 1 when both tools ship clean releases (recheck on the next release of either). If one clears first, split that shared argument so it ships alone, as trivy did. Re-scan, update pins, checksums and `SCANNED_FAILING`/`MAY_BE_HELD` in `tests/unit/scripts/test_agent_toolbox_image.py`.

comments.body:
<!-- swarmcloud-issue-run:run_af622a00f5ed4160b28f:plan -->
### SwarmCloud plan for #442

**Approved** by bogdan at 2026-10-08T23:57:06 UTC.

**Mode:** workflow · **Estimate:** 2.5 agent-hours (plus waiting for upstream releases if neither tool is clean at run time) · **Revision:** 1 · **Digest:** `sha256:2446ba7190646a9deb2ab95284490f92854f5f9dc5caf56283109ee9b3ad4def`

Issue #442 asks for all 11 build-spec tools in agent-runtime-base, with the image scan passing and no .trivyignore waiver. trivy is already done: 0.75.0 scanned clean and is installed unconditionally on main. tofu and tflint are still held. Both sit behind the single default-off INSTALL_TOFU_TFLINT build argument because every release of each had a fixable HIGH CVE. I read the GitHub releases API on 2026-10-08 and the newest releases are unchanged since the 2026-10-07 check: tofu v1.13.1 (2026-10-01; 3 fixable HIGH: x/mod 0.39.0, grpc 1.83.1) and tflint v0.64.0 (2026-07-17; 17 fixable HIGH). So the issue cannot be closed today. The plan has two steps. Step one is work that is not blocked: split the shared hold argument into INSTALL_TOFU and INSTALL_TFLINT, so that whichever vendor ships a clean release first can go into the image alone, the way trivy did. Step two runs at execution time: re-check the newest release of each tool with the promote gate's filter (`trivy rootfs --scanners vuln --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed`, run on the executable binary after a sha256 match). A tool whose release scans clean gets its pin, checksum, default flag, test sets and docs updated, and the PR names the release and the scan. A tool that still fails gets the scan recorded and stays held. The PR says `refs #442` only if both tofu and tflint are in the default build. Otherwise it says `part of #442`.

#### Requirements
1. The agent-runtime-base image carries all 11 build-spec tools (gh, gcloud, kubectl, terraform, tofu, tflint, checkov, trivy, shellcheck, make, docker) in its default build.
2. For each of tofu, tflint and trivy, the latest release is checked against the image scan (the promote gate's HIGH/CRITICAL, ignore-unfixed filter).
3. A tool is added to the default build only once its release scans clean; a release with a fixable HIGH/CRITICAL is never shipped.
4. No .trivyignore waiver or other scan exception is added.
5. The image scan passes with every added tool installed.
6. The PR states, for each tool added, which release and which scan run showed it clean.

#### Overlaps with open work
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#625](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/issues/625) (issue): Cloud Run Job container start time grew. Turning tofu and tflint on adds about 52 MB to agent-runtime-base (docs/worker-images.md), which may add a little pull time. No files are shared. The plan records the size change in docs/worker-images.md and does nothing else about #625.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#911](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/911) (pull request): Edits images/agent-runtime-indexer/, a different image from images/agent-runtime-base/Dockerfile. No shared files.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#897](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/897) (pull request): Edits CLAUDE.md, docs/ci.md, workflows and acceptance scripts, but not the image Dockerfile, docs/versions.md, docs/worker-images.md, docs/BUILD_PROMPT_V2.md or the toolbox test. No shared files.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#476](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/issues/476) (issue): The deferred security-pass epic. This plan adds no waiver and changes no scan configuration, so nothing here needs to go into it.

#### Steps
1. **Split INSTALL_TOFU_TFLINT into INSTALL_TOFU and INSTALL_TFLINT so each tool can leave the hold on its own** (`split-hold`) — 1 agent-hour
   - files: `images/agent-runtime-base/Dockerfile`, `tests/unit/scripts/test_agent_toolbox_image.py`, `docs/versions.md`, `docs/worker-images.md`, `docs/BUILD_PROMPT_V2.md`
   - tests, written first:
     - test_every_held_install_sits_behind_its_own_hold_argument (tofu only under INSTALL_TOFU, tflint only under INSTALL_TFLINT)
     - test_the_smoke_step_adds_each_held_tool_under_its_own_argument
     - test_each_hold_defaults_off_while_its_tool_has_no_clean_release
     - test_the_combined_hold_argument_is_gone_from_the_dockerfile_and_docs
     - smoke-execution cases for INSTALL_TOFU=1/INSTALL_TFLINT=0 and the reverse, asserting the printed tool count

   <details><summary>Instructions</summary>

   Context: issue #442. agent-runtime-base must carry all 11 build-spec tools. tofu and tflint are held behind ONE default-off build argument, INSTALL_TOFU_TFLINT (images/agent-runtime-base/Dockerfile, around lines 590-650, plus the toolbox smoke step around line 754). Because the hold is shared, one tool cannot ship without the other. The 2026-10-07 issue comment asks for the argument to be split so whichever tool clears the scan first ships alone, as trivy did.

   Write the tests first, in tests/unit/scripts/test_agent_toolbox_image.py:
   (a) Replace HOLD_ARG with a per-tool map HOLD_ARG_OF = {'tofu': 'INSTALL_TOFU', 'tflint': 'INSTALL_TFLINT'}.
   (b) Generalise _held_blocks to take the argument name.
   (c) Change test_every_held_install_sits_behind_the_hold_argument so each held tool's `/usr/local/bin/<tool>` install sits inside ITS OWN argument's `if [ "${ARG}" = "1" ]; then ... fi` block, and NOT inside the other tool's block.
   (d) Change _smoke_tool_lists and test_only_the_tools_without_a_clean_release_are_held so the smoke step adds each held tool under its own argument.
   (e) Change test_the_hold_default_is_off_while_any_held_tool_has_no_clean_release so it checks each tool's own argument against SCANNED_FAILING. The rule: a tool pinned at a failing release must default to 0. A tool whose pin is not in SCANNED_FAILING may default to 1.
   (f) Change the smoke-execution tests (_run_smoke and its callers) to pass both arguments, and keep the assertion on the printed count of tools visited.
   (g) Add a test that the old INSTALL_TOFU_TFLINT name appears nowhere in the Dockerfile, docs/versions.md, docs/worker-images.md or docs/BUILD_PROMPT_V2.md.
   Push the tests alone first (red), then the fix.

   Then make the change in images/agent-runtime-base/Dockerfile:
   - Declare ARG INSTALL_TOFU=0 and ARG INSTALL_TFLINT=0.
   - Turn the one guarded block into two independent `if ...; then ...; fi` blocks: tofu's download, sha256 check, extract and install in one; tflint's in the other.
   - Make the smoke step add `tofu` and `tflint` separately, each under its own argument.
   - Keep the explanatory comment and the scan record. Reword it to describe two arguments, and keep the reason each default is 0.
   Update every mention of INSTALL_TOFU_TFLINT in docs/versions.md (line ~87), docs/worker-images.md (lines ~9 and ~119) and docs/BUILD_PROMPT_V2.md (line ~687) to the new names.

   Do not change pins, checksums or defaults in this step.

   Invariants: this changes no runtime behaviour (both default to 0), adds no waiver, and touches nothing under apps/common/swarm_common/.

   Before finishing, run `uv run pytest tests/unit/scripts/test_agent_toolbox_image.py -q`, then scripts/changed-guards.sh, then scripts/publish-scan.sh.

   </details>

2. **Re-check the newest tofu and tflint releases with the promote gate's filter; add each one that is clean, record each one that is not** (`rescan-and-add`) — 1.5 agent-hours
   - files: `images/agent-runtime-base/Dockerfile`, `tests/unit/scripts/test_agent_toolbox_image.py`, `docs/versions.md`, `docs/worker-images.md`, `docs/BUILD_PROMPT_V2.md`
   - tests, written first:
     - test_<tool>_is_in_the_default_build_and_its_install_is_unconditional for each tool that scanned clean (modelled on the trivy test)
     - SCANNED_FAILING extended with every newly scanned failing release, so test_no_default_tool_is_pinned_at_a_release_the_scan_failed refuses them
     - test_versions_doc_lists_the_image_toolbox_at_the_pinned_versions kept green against the new pins

   <details><summary>Instructions</summary>

   Context: issue #442. The owner's decision (2026-10-01) is to add tofu and tflint only once a release of each passes the image scan, with NO .trivyignore waiver. trivy 0.75.0 already ships (it scanned clean on 2026-10-06). As of 2026-10-08 the newest releases were tofu v1.13.1 and tflint v0.64.0, and both FAIL the scan (see the comment in the Dockerfile above INSTALL_TOFU/INSTALL_TFLINT).

   1. Read the newest non-prerelease of each tool now: `curl -s https://api.github.com/repos/opentofu/opentofu/releases?per_page=5` and the same for terraform-linters/tflint. Also read the newest trivy (aquasecurity/trivy). If trivy has moved past 0.75.0, leave the pin alone; this issue only needs it in the image, and it is. Write down when you read each.

   2. For each of tofu and tflint at its newest release:
   - download the linux_amd64 asset named by the Dockerfile's URL template;
   - check it against the vendor's checksum file (tofu_<v>_SHA256SUMS, or tflint checksums.txt);
   - extract the binary and `chmod +x` it. Trivy's Go-binary analyzer skips files without the exec bit, so an unexecutable binary scans empty, and an empty scan is not a clean scan;
   - run the promote gate's filter, `trivy rootfs --scanners vuln --severity HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed <dir>`, with the newest trivy and a freshly updated DB. Record the trivy version and the DB timestamp;
   - as a control, run the same scan on the previously recorded failing release and confirm it still reports findings.
   If the newest tofu 1.13.x still fails, also check the newest release of the 1.12 line.

   3. Write tests first in tests/unit/scripts/test_agent_toolbox_image.py:
   - For a tool that is now CLEAN: remove it from MAY_BE_HELD. Add an assertion like test_trivy_is_in_the_default_build_and_its_install_is_unconditional: the tool is in the smoke step's always-list, it is installed by an unconditional RUN, and its pin is not in SCANNED_FAILING. Add every release the scan failed to SCANNED_FAILING.
   - For a tool that STILL FAILS: add the newly scanned release to SCANNED_FAILING, if it is new.
   Update the module docstring's dated sentence about which tools are held.

   4. Then change images/agent-runtime-base/Dockerfile.
   - For a clean tool: bump its VERSION and SHA256 ARGs. Move its install out of the hold block into an unconditional install, and delete that tool's hold argument altogether: a hold with nothing behind it is dead code. Add it to the smoke step's always-list. Above the pin, write the scan you ran (release, date, trivy version, DB timestamp, result) and the checksum source URL.
   - For a failing tool: keep it held, update the dated scan record in the comment, and bump its pin only if a newer release exists.
   If BOTH are clean, delete MAY_BE_HELD, the hold machinery and the hold-related tests. All 11 tools then sit in the always-list. test_the_smoke_step_names_every_required_tool must still pass.

   5. Update docs/versions.md (the agent image toolbox table: version, clean yes/no, and the 'installed onl…

   </details>

### SwarmCloud: not ready

- **Run:** `run_03d7e658de8c4b569f4a` (NOT_READY)
- **Verdict:** blocked by other work

**Why:** The owner decided on 2026-10-09 (issue comment, 07:39Z) that #442 becomes a Schedules job: a weekly 'image-tool-rescan' schedule will re-scan the newest tofu and tflint releases with the promote gate's filter and add each one that scans clean, with no waiver. #442 closes in favour of that schedule once it exists, and the comment ties that to the Schedules types from #892, lane S6 or later. That schedule does not exist yet on main (960c36f). apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/scheduletypes.py lists no 'image-tool-rescan' type. Its closest entry is DependencyCveRefreshParams. There is no apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/schedtypes/ executor directory, and the schedule tick is still the open PR #964 (S2, part of #892). The parts of the old plan that could be done now are already on main. images/agent-runtime-base/Dockerfile splits the hold into INSTALL_TOFU=0 and INSTALL_TFLINT=0 (lines 634-635, 646, 653, 767-768) and records a re-scan dated 2026-10-09. That scan used trivy 0.75.0 with the DB of 2026-10-08T19:05Z, and the releases API was read 2026-10-09T00:01Z. It found no newer tofu than 1.13.1 and no newer tflint than 0.64.0, and both still have fixable HIGH CVEs. trivy 0.75.0 is already installed unconditionally (TRIVY_VERSION=0.75.0, line 681). So no tool can be added today without a waiver, and the owner has ruled waivers out. The issue's remaining work is the schedule the owner described.

**Needs:**
- depends on #892: the Schedules types must ship (PR #964, the S2 schedule tick, and the type lanes S6 or later that add executor modules under apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/schedtypes/)
- an 'image-tool-rescan' schedule type: the owner names it but nothing in scheduletypes.py describes it yet; it has to be added to the catalogue (docs/schedules.md §3) in a #892 lane, or the owner has to say it should be planned as its own issue
- or: a clean release of tofu (newer than 1.13.1) or tflint (newer than 0.64.0) appears before the schedule exists, and the owner says #442 should take that one-off add (flip INSTALL_TOFU / INSTALL_TFLINT) instead of waiting for the schedule

_The issue is planned again only after it is edited or commented on._

title: A new person's personal workspace (tenant, identity, namespace) is created during onboarding, and no task or workflow starts before it exists
body:
### Problem

A new person gets nothing to run in when they first use SwarmCloud. Each person's isolated space has to be registered by an operator: a personal tenant with its own service account, secrets access, storage prefix and GKE namespace. Today that is a `dev.tfvars` entry plus a release, or `scripts/register-tenant.sh`. Namespaces are also not applied by releases, because `APPLY_TENANT_NAMESPACES` is off.

On 2026-10-07 the owner's own personal tenant, `u-bogdan`, had no GKE namespace until it was created by hand. Any of its tasks dispatched to GKE would have failed to start.

### What the owner wants (2026-10-08)

> "it would be great for personal namespaces to be onboarded at the time of onboarding a new user in swarmcloud. Maybe part of github app onboarding and it should block starting any task or workflow before this exists. We need to have a way to create this via the UI and potentially via the plugin if that is possible"

- **Onboarding creates the space.** The personal space (tenant, identity, secrets access, storage prefix, namespace) is created during onboarding, next to the GitHub App connection step (#780).
- **Nothing runs before it exists.** Submitting a task or a workflow before the space exists is refused with a clear, actionable message. Example: `403 WORKSPACE_NOT_READY: finish setup — create your workspace`.
- **Two ways to start it.** The space can be created from the console's setup checklist and from the plugin (`/sc:setup`, `sc setup`).

### What you expected instead

A person who signs in and completes onboarding can run work with no operator involved, and they can never run work in a space that does not exist yet.

### Constraints

- **Invariant 9:** every tenant has its own GSA, secrets, GCS prefix and namespace.
- **Rule 2:** nothing may touch the other team's resources in `saga-agents-staging`.
- **swarm-api runs with narrow permissions today.** Creating service accounts and IAM bindings is deployer-level power, so who holds it is the core design decision.
- **The release gates IAM changes** behind the owner's approval (`dev-iam`).

### Area

`apps/swarm-api` (onboarding, submission), `apps/swarm-ui` (setup checklist), `apps/swarm-mcp`/`plugin` (`sc setup`), `terraform/` (identity and provisioning), `kubernetes/` (namespace render), `scripts/register-tenant.sh`.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
Owner decisions, 2026-10-08:
- **Who creates the workspace:** a separate, locked-down provisioner, triggered by the person's click in the console or in `/sc:setup`. swarm-api only records and authorizes the request, and keeps no power to create identities or change IAM. The provisioner runs the same steps as `register-tenant.sh` (identity, grants, storage prefix, namespace, tenant document and pool), and the console shows its progress.
- **Before the workspace is ready:** the person can sign in, connect GitHub, choose repositories and look around. Every task or workflow submission (console, API, plugin) is refused with `403 WORKSPACE_NOT_READY` and a link to the setup step.
- **Next:** a short design (docs/), then implementation lanes.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
<!-- swarmcloud-issue-run:run_380620509c984da092e2:plan -->
### SwarmCloud plan for #847

**Approved** by bogdan at 2026-10-08T17:59:45 UTC.

**Mode:** workflow · **Estimate:** 14 agent-hours, plus the owner's one-time steps (W0 verification, Cloud Build repository connection, W4 bootstrap apply and dev-iam, W5 policy apply, W9 apply and plan check, the first real approval) · **Revision:** 1 · **Digest:** `sha256:92ed0ab45424e2eae3fb51e27807d83f173985e210f29a7daf9192c12b5555d2`

Most of #847 is built or in flight. On main: the design (docs/workspaces.md), admin roles in Firestore (W2), the call guard (W3), the workspace deployer's cluster RBAC and scope policy (W5), and register-tenant.sh --workspace with its Cloud Build file (W6, #869). In open PRs: the workspace record, routes, onboarding steps and submission gate plus the People/approval API (W1+W7, #868, which supersedes #861), and the Terraform for the deployer identity, Pub/Sub trigger and restricted logs (W4, #871). This plan delivers what is left. The console gets the workspace and Claude-account steps in the setup checklist with live provisioning progress, WORKSPACE_NOT_READY/NO_CLAUDE_ACCOUNT banners on every Submit screen, and the Admin › People pane (W8). The plugin gets swarm_setup_workspace, the two steps in sc setup and /sc:setup, and the refusal printed with its next command (W8). u-bogdan moves out of Terraform state with a plan that destroys nothing (W9). WORKSPACE_GATE is wired through Terraform, shipped off, with the docs W10 names. Finally the gate is turned on in dev, but only after the owner records the first real approval end to end (W10, WD8). After that, a new person's request is approved with one admin click, a guarded Cloud Build job creates their tenant, identity, grants, storage prefix and namespace, and no task or workflow of theirs starts before it is ready. The steps that use #868's or #871's code must not start until those PRs merge. W0 (live verification in the shared project) and the owner's one-time applies are not agent work; see questions.json.

#### Requirements
1. During onboarding, each new person gets a personal space: their own tenant, service account, secrets access, GCS storage prefix and GKE namespace (invariant 9).
2. The workspace step sits in onboarding next to the GitHub App connection step (#780).
3. Submitting a task or a workflow (console, API or plugin) before the person's workspace is ready is refused with 403 WORKSPACE_NOT_READY, a clear actionable message and a link to the setup step.
4. The workspace can be requested from the console's setup checklist.
5. The workspace can be requested from the plugin, through /sc:setup and sc setup.
6. A separate, locked-down provisioner creates the workspace, triggered by the person's request (approved by an admin, per the design). swarm-api only records and authorizes the request and holds no power to create identities or change IAM.
7. The provisioner runs the same steps as register-tenant.sh: identity, grants, storage prefix, namespace, tenant document and pool.
8. The console shows the provisioner's progress.
9. Before the workspace is ready, the person can still sign in, connect GitHub, choose repositories and look around.
10. A person who signs in and completes onboarding can run work with no operator involved.
11. Nothing touches the other team's resources in saga-agents-staging (rule 2).
12. IAM changes stay behind the owner's dev-iam approval.
13. A short design is written in docs/ before implementation (docs/workspaces.md, on main).
14. u-bogdan, the owner's personal tenant whose namespace was made by hand, becomes a workspace record outside Terraform without destroying anything.

#### Overlaps with open work
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#868](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/868) (pull request): W1+W7: the workspace record, GET/POST /v1/workspace, the loan request, the onboarding steps, WorkspaceNotReady/NoClaudeAccount, the gate behind WORKSPACE_GATE=off, and the People/approve/deny/limits/loan routes with the Pub/Sub publish. This plan does not redo any of it. console-workspace, admin-people, plugin-setup and gate-switch-and-docs call its routes and must start only after it merges. The owner or reviewer must land #868 first.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#861](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/861) (pull request): W1 alone. Every file it changes is also changed by #868, which carries W1 plus W7, so merging both will conflict. The owner should refs #861 as superseded by #868, or merge #861 first and rebase #868. **Incident, read 2026-10-10 ~02:10Z: an approved workspace request waits forever and nobody is told.** w-752763 was approved 2026-10-09T07:09Z and still reads `approved`, with `steps: {}` and `dispatch: null`.

- WS-WIRE (wf_fbcc9726): a 10-minute sweep scheduler, the `workspace_apply_publish` switch, and an alert on `workspace_stuck`.

The owner's own workspace is unblocked through W9 (962 merged), which needs no Cloud Build pipeline. **PR 936 (W10, WORKSPACE_GATE on) must not merge until provisioning works**, or no task starts for anyone without a workspace.

comments.body: **Owner decision 2026-10-10: WD2 is re-decided. A person's workspace setup runs as a Cloud Run job, not a Cloud Build trigger.** The reason: a generic, easy-to-install SwarmCloud. Cloud Build makes every install add a repository connection (OAuth plus Google's GitHub App), a Secret Manager grant to Google's Cloud Build agent, and possibly a private pool, and none of those can be done by `terraform apply`. A Cloud Run job runs the image the release already builds from `main` (pinned by digest), as `swarm-workspace-deployer`, under the same call guard. Its logs stay private in Cloud Logging, and it needs no forge connection, so it works for any forge. It is installed by Terraform alone. The design amendment comes first (lane WD2-CRJ); then the build. Once the job ships, the `swarm-github` Cloud Build connection and its two grants (PRs 993 and 1005) are removed. Until then the connection stays as it is, PENDING_USER_OAUTH, and nothing uses it.

title: The default compute service account holds Editor on the shared project, so anything running as it can act as every swarm account and update or run Cloud Run jobs
body:
### What happened

Read 2026-10-10 ~18:45Z with `gcloud projects get-iam-policy saga-agents-staging`, for W0b item (3) of docs/workspaces.md (#847): the **default compute service account `209012342332-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com` holds `roles/editor` on the whole shared project**. Editor includes `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` and `run.jobs.update` / `run.jobs.runWithOverrides`. So any workload running as the default compute account (a VM, a Cloud Run service or a job deployed without an explicit service account, or a legacy Cloud Build) can:
- update or run the planned `swarm-workspace-apply` Cloud Run job as `swarm-workspace-deployer`, bypassing the job-level IAM policy W4b relies on;
- update any `swarm-job-*` worker job;
- act as every swarm service account.

The rest of the reading is as designed. The Cloud Run dispatch roles are held only by swarm-scheduler (swarmJobDispatcher, plus the conditioned swarmGkeDispatcher), swarm-reconciler (swarmJobReaper, plus the conditioned swarmGkeReaper), swarm-accept (swarmAcceptanceRunner) and swarm-tf-deployer (run.admin). Two human owners hold owner, and one of them also holds run.admin and serviceAccountUser.

### What you expected

No identity outside the platform's own accounts and the owners holds act-as or Cloud Run job update in the project. The default compute account's automatic Editor grant is Google's legacy default, recommended to be removed.

### Where

`saga-agents-staging` project IAM. This project is **shared**: the other team's workloads may run as the default compute account, so the grant **must not be removed or narrowed without them**.

### Severity

S0 class (it bounds tenant isolation and the workspace deployer's blast radius), but there is no exposure today: the Cloud Run job does not exist yet (W4b). The workspace job design records it as a residual risk until this is resolved.

### What would resolve it

Agree with the other team which of their workloads use the default compute account. Move those to dedicated accounts, then remove `roles/editor` from `209012342332-compute` (or narrow it to what those workloads need, with no actAs and no run.* job permissions).

**Why:** The fix this issue asks for is a change to project IAM on the shared project saga-agents-staging: removing or narrowing roles/editor on 209012342332-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com. That account is on this repository's shared-resource deny-list (scripts/lib/common.sh, the SHARED list around line 248), and CLAUDE.md rule 2 says nothing written here may modify it. The issue says the grant 'must not be removed or narrowed without' the other team, and docs/workspaces.md (W0b item 3, around lines 350-356) records it as a residual risk 'to be removed together with that team, never unilaterally'. The first step in 'What would resolve it' is to agree with the other team which of their workloads use the default compute account and move them to dedicated accounts. Neither the issue nor its comments record that agreement, so no code change in this repository can deliver it now. There is also no exposure today, because the swarm-workspace-apply job (W4b) does not exist yet. One related point: SwarmCloud depends on the account too. terraform/bootstrap/wif.tf `deployer_acts_as_cloudbuild` grants swarm-tf-deployer roles/iam.serviceAccountUser on the default compute account, and terraform/bootstrap/deployer_conditions.tf (around line 626) notes that the 20 most recent Cloud Builds all ran as 209012342332-compute@developer. Removing Editor from that account would affect this platform's own `gcloud builds submit` path as well as the other team's workloads.

**Needs:**
- agreement with the other team that owns saga-agents-staging's agents-staging workloads: which of their workloads run as 209012342332-compute@developer, and a date by which they move to dedicated service accounts (recorded on #1020)
- owner decision: after that migration, remove roles/editor from the default compute account entirely, or narrow it to a named set of roles with no iam.serviceAccounts.actAs and no run.jobs.* permissions (and who applies the project IAM change, since it is outside terraform's managed-by=swarm-terraform scope)
- owner decision: should SwarmCloud first move its own Cloud Build runs off the default compute account to a dedicated swarm build service account (replacing terraform/bootstrap/wif.tf deployer_acts_as_cloudbuild)? That is a separable, unblocked preparatory change, and it could be filed as its own issue if wanted

title: Every member's GitHub token slot in a group tenant is readable by the tenant's shared worker identity, so one member's agent can read another's token
body:
### What are you trying to do?
Keep each person's credentials their own inside a shared group tenant.

Measured from docs/onboarding.md on main, 2026-10-11:
- Where repository grants are enforced (dev: `repository_grants_enforced = true`), a person's task already runs as that person. It uses their own GitHub App user token, stored per person as `swarm-tenant-<t>-git-u-<hex>` (with a `-refresh` twin), or their fallback PAT.
- **But the tenant's worker account can read every member's slot.** docs/onboarding.md §"Phase 1" item 4 grants `secretAccessor` on `swarm-tenant-<t>-git-u-*` to the tenant's worker identity, one conditional binding per tenant. Every member of `eng` runs agents as the same `swarm-agent-worker-eng`, so an agent in Bob's task could read Alice's token slot. Only convention and the worker's code choose which slot it reads.
- Service submissions (indexing, schedules, smoke) use the tenant token `swarm-tenant-<t>-git`, which is shared by design.
- Provider keys (`swarm-tenant-<t>-<provider>`) are per tenant.

### What would you like to see?
A design for user-scoped secrets in group tenants, so no member's agent can read another member's credential. Because a group tenant's workers share one identity, IAM alone cannot do this. The design has to choose between:
- a broker (swarm-api releases a person's token only to an attempt whose task `submitted_by` is that person, checked against the signed attempt key and fencing generation, with the worker's direct accessor grant on `-git-u-*` removed);
- per-person worker identities inside a group tenant;
- requiring personal work to run in the person's personal workspace, as the owner chose for browser logins (#1030, LB-7).

Provider keys need the same review: decide which are team credentials and which are personal.

### Where would this live?
Secrets and tenancy: `docs/onboarding.md`, `docs/multi-tenancy.md`, `docs/git-tokens.md`, the tenancy module's conditional binding, the worker's token read, and swarm-api.

### How do you do it today?
As described above: per-person slots, readable by the whole tenant's worker identity.

### How would you know it worked?
A task Alice submits in `eng` pushes as Alice. An attempt of a task Bob submitted in `eng` is refused Alice's slot by IAM or by the broker, shown by a test. No credential appears in any log, Job environment or repository file.

### Constraint check
Owner decision, 2026-10-11: secrets are user-scoped, not tenant-scoped. Browser logins are already scoped to personal workspaces (#1030).

title: The console does not show which GitHub permissions the App or an org is missing, so a merge fails before anyone knows
body:
### What are you trying to do?
Know, before a run fails, whether GitHub lets SwarmCloud do what the run needs on a repository, and fix it from the console.

On 2026-10-11, sagaxyz/ai-studio merges failed with `token_lacks_rights` because the swarmcloud-saga App lacked **Commit statuses: read**. Nothing in the console said so.

### What would you like to see?
The owner chose design 2, "Org cards", from https://claude.ai/artifact/5e2ufvX8APiK3DYfxaTE5P (private to the owner).
- **Work › Setup › GitHub** shows one card per connected org, plus one for the App.
  - A card is collapsed when everything is granted, and open when something is missing.
  - Each missing permission says in plain words what breaks (for example, "merges can't see CI, so they fail").
  - Each gap has a fix button that opens the exact GitHub page:
    - for an org: the installation's permission-update review page;
    - for the App: its permissions settings page, shown to admins only.
- **Work › Repositories** gets a status dot per repository whose tooltip names the problem. A repository's page shows its own org's card.
- SwarmCloud re-checks when the user returns to the tab, and on demand.
- GitHub does not allow SwarmCloud to grant permissions itself, so a fix is always a link.
- Token-backed repositories are probed for what their token can actually do.

### Where would this live?
- swarm-api: a new permissions read, using the App's installations and per-repo probes.
- apps/swarm-ui: the Setup GitHub section, Repositories, and the repository page.

### How do you do it today?
You find out when a merge or step fails, and fix it by hand on GitHub.

### How would you know it worked?
- With an org that has not accepted a requested permission, Setup shows that org's card open with the gap and a working review link.
- The affected repositories show a red dot.
- After accepting on GitHub, a re-check turns the card and the dots green.
- A member who is not an admin never sees the App-level button.

### Constraint check
No credential is stored or requested. Read-only GitHub calls only, with the App's installation tokens and the tenant's existing token.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Cause of today's red acceptance runs, read 2026-10-16:** not code. Every failing group had a claude-code task that started and then parked `quota_exhausted` within seconds. Example: task_4480ce24bb5745078d69 ran at 10:15:11Z, logged quota_exhausted and parked at 10:15:15Z, and was cancelled by the 900 s timeout. The `smoke` tenant borrowed only one account, `eng:team`, which was at 93% of its weekly limit.

**Change, owner decision:** `eng:devops-team`, at 47% weekly, now also lends to `smoke` (applied 18:05Z; `sc accounts` reads `eng:devops-team lends to u-bogdan, u-devops, smoke`). The next acceptance run shows whether this was the whole cause.

### Wave

2026-10-12: the live-browser (#1030) finishing lanes: LB-STREAM, LB-UX1/2/3, LB-V1..V6, LB-R1..R5, LB-KEYRACE, OPS-RELAY, OPS-MIRROR, plus the operator's hand-made PRs (PR 1168, 1171, 1173, 1182, 1184, 1185, 1186, 1191) and the gstack visual QA passes 5–7.

### Where these findings came from

The visual QA passes (scratchpad/lb-vqa/REPORT.md), the release runs on main, CI on PRs 1184 and 1186, and the owner's report of task_23cc2e82178640709a45, whose live browser never started. Each finding is a comment below with the file and call site. Under the repository's rule, this epic closes on its comments, never on its body.

title: Runner git access: platform-held git tools mid-task (push own branch, rebase, private read, pr checks), never raw tokens
body:
## Problem
SwarmCloud runners hold no GitHub credentials, so a lane can only build on a fresh checkout and hand its diff back at the end. On sagaxyz/ai-studio, 2026-10-12, that kept about half the lanes local and caused failures:
- **Lost pushes:** two lanes BUILT their change, but the platform push of the build branch never happened (wf_e55610ded71c4d9d9fae, wf_0260c920acf8414395b2). The review step then failed with "Remote branch swarm/task_… not found", and each had to be rescued from `build.patch` by hand.
- **No git ops on existing branches:** no rebase onto main, no conflict fix on a PR's branch, no catching a stacked branch up after a squash merge. These are the most common follow-ups.
- **No private reads:** a lane can't read a sibling private repo (sagaxyz/agents-backend) at a pinned sha. Pin bumps and upstream-parity work stay local.
- **Can't watch its own CI:** a lane can't check its PR's CI or fix red rows.
- **Status-read 404s:** three workflows returned 404 on status after their build step, although their review and fix steps ran. The coordinator re-ran the review locally, which produced duplicate PRs.

## Proposal: platform-held git tools, mid-task
The runner gets MCP tools that SwarmCloud executes with its own credential. The agent never sees a token.
- `git_push_branch()` pushes the task's own branch (`swarm/<task>` or a declared branch). It is never `main` or another task's branch.
- `git_fetch(ref)` and `git_rebase_onto(ref)` are run against origin by the platform. The result lands in the workspace, with conflicts left for the agent.
- `read_private(repo, path, ref)` is read-only, limited to an allowlist per tenant (e.g. sagaxyz/agents-backend).
- `pr_checks(pr)` is read-only: the CI rows bound to the head sha.
- Every call is logged with the task id. Push is refused for protected branches, and for any branch not created by this task unless it was declared in the spec.

## Fallback, if tools can't land soon
A per-task GitHub App installation token, valid for 1h and scoped to the ONE repo of the task:
- Contents write, with branch protection guarding `main`;
- Pull requests write;
- no admin, Actions or secrets permissions.
A separate read-only installation token covers the allowlisted private dependency. Never a personal access token. Revoke it when the task ends.

## Never on runners
kubectl, gcloud, production clusters, secret creation or rotation, and repo or org settings. These stay with the human or the coordinator's local session.

## Threat model
Agents read untrusted repo, issue and PR text, so a prompt injection could try to exfiltrate or misuse a credential.
- **Platform-held tools:** no token exists in the container, so nothing can be exfiltrated. Misuse is limited to what the tools allow: the task's own branch, and allowlisted reads.
- **Fallback token:** if one leaks, the damage is limited to one repo for one hour with no admin, and protected branches stay safe.

## Acceptance
- A lane can rebase its PR branch onto main, resolve conflicts, push, and read `pr_checks`, all without a token in the environment. Prove it with `env | grep -i token` being empty.
- A lane can read agents-backend at a sha via `read_private`.
- Push to `main` or to another task's branch is refused, with a test for each.
- A failed final push surfaces as an error on the task, never as SUCCEEDED with no branch.

Context: sagaxyz/ai-studio coordinator session, 2026-10-13. The owner chose this approach: "write a proposal for SC and file it as an issue in the repo so it gets done".

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Cause measured (2026-10-22 09:08Z): the gate refuses control because the fixture page is plain http.**

For attempt att_fb7f449a000d41acb9a7 (scheduled run of 2026-10-21 ~22:03Z), the gate's own log lines (namespace swarm-tenant-smoke):

- 22:03:41 `live gate: record=control_refused {"cause": "insecure_connection"}` at the take (relay: `control_taken`);
- 22:03:48 the same refusal at the renew;
- 22:04:05 `live rfb: … closed keys=0 pointer=0 pastes=0 dropped=53`: every input the scripted viewer sent was dropped.

`LIVE_BROWSER_PROMPT` (scripts/acceptance/groups/live-browser.sh) serves the fixture with `python3 -m http.server 8765 --bind 127.0.0.1` and opens `http://127.0.0.1:8765/login.html`. `CdpProxy.take_control` (apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/livegate/cdpproxy.py ~1080) refuses any page whose security state is not `secure` or whose URL is not https (`_https_host`). That rule arrived with QI-GATE (PR 1724, merged 2026-10-20 ~11:56Z); the first red scheduled run is 39466773672 (2026-10-20 17:31Z).

So the earlier "input before the grant" hypothesis is wrong: control is never granted. The product is doing what it was built to do (no hand-off on an insecure page); the acceptance case predates the rule.

Two ways to fix it, both an owner decision (held for the morning):
1. **Serve the fixture over https** from the dedicated public fixture bucket (`swarm-acceptance-fixture-<project>`), as a second static object beside fixture.html. Harness-only; widens the bucket from one public object to two.
2. **Treat loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost) as secure in the gate**, as Chrome does for secure contexts. Changes the hand-off security rule.

Separately (independent of the choice): the run 39727554326 failure (socket close 4503, no relay) is environmental.

title: [epic] Wave 2026-10-14 out-of-territory findings
body:
### Wave

2026-10-14 (CTXQ, EGRESS, JEV, SC plugin, merge-train lanes)

### Where these findings came from

Orchestration of the 2026-10-14 wave, from the SwarmCloud orchestrating session. Read on 2026-10-14 between 20:00Z and 00:45Z (13:00–17:45 PDT). Each finding is one comment below, with the file, the call site and how it was measured.

### Recorded elsewhere, deliberately not duplicated here

- The one-parent merge commits from conflict-fix rounds: issue #1321 (fixed by PR 1322).
- The hung unit shards with no job timeout: PR 1319.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body: - [ ] **The CTXQ-UI lane (PR 1332) built a second code-intelligence backend outside its UI territory, duplicating CTXQ-SET** · `apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/routes/code_intelligence.py` (since deleted) · Found while reconciling PR 1330 on 2026-10-14. The lane brief named only `apps/swarm-ui`; nothing refused the out-of-territory route. A fixer kept CTXQ-SET's `codeintel` as the only implementation (PR 1330). Remaining mechanical fix: the lane brief template should list forbidden paths, or the publish step should refuse a diff outside the named territory.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
- [x] **`swarm_check` keeps flagging `merge_refused` on merge steps whose pull request has since merged** · `apps/swarm-mcp/swarm_mcp/check.py` around line 499 (the `merge_refused` rule) · Measured by `/sc check` at 00:41Z on 2026-10-15: the merge steps for PRs 1328, 1317, 1312 and 1316 were all flagged STUCK `head_moved`, but `gh pr view` showed every one MERGED. The rule reads only the step state; it never reads the PR, so every `head_moved` stays flagged for good.

_Ticked 2026-10-17 00:20Z, verified on main 35f2a61e: 18f40870: check.py:555-572 skips MERGED/CLOSED_

title: Jev's data flow has no record tying each sent-or-never-sent rule to the code and test that enforce it
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Hold, for the security pass (#476), a reviewable record of exactly what leaves the platform when a workspace opts in to Jev for code intelligence. Since PR 1330, `workspace_settings/{tenant}.code_intelligence.jev` decides whether repository excerpts go to an external ranking service. The owner made that setting owner/admin-only and audited on 2026-10-14 because it does. The rules for what may be sent live in docs/design/context-quality.md §5.4, a design document. Nothing yet ties each rule to the code and test that enforce it.

### What would you like to see?

A data-flow record (docs/jev-data-flow.md, or a section of docs/design/context-quality.md) with one row per §5.4 rule. Each row gives the rule, the function that enforces it (once phase 4, CTXQ-JW, builds the Jev call path), the unit test that proves it, and what the audit line records:

1. path deny (`.env*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `*.p12`, `*.tfvars`, `*.tfstate*`, `secrets/`, `credentials/`, `hard_stop_paths`): path name only;
2. a credential-scan hit drops the excerpt (never masks it);
3. `swarm_redaction.rules.redact` applied to every string;
4. the task's registered secrets scrubbed (`agent_worker.redact.scrub_text`);
5. never sent: author identities and emails, another repository's content, in-flight content beyond titles and paths, the agent's transcript, environment variables;
6. per-call audit `{call_id, kind, bytes, input_tokens, ms, outcome}` in `context-pack.json`, with no payload.

Plus: where Jev runs (the worker process, never the agent or swarm-api, §5.1), which key it uses, and which egress path its calls take.

### Where would this live?

docs/ (a decision record), reviewed under the security epic #476

### How do you do it today?

The rules exist only as design prose in §5.4. Lane CTXQ-JW (phase 4) will implement the call path; this record should be written with it and reviewed before Jev is turned on for any workspace beyond the owner's.

### How would you know it worked?

Every §5.4 rule has a named enforcing function and a test that fails when the rule is removed. The review on #476 signs it off.

### Constraint check

- [X] None of the above, as far as I can tell

title: A workspace secrets store holds any provider credential and grants each one, by checkbox, to specific runner profiles, images and platform components
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Set and manage the API keys and credentials of every provider SwarmCloud uses (TypeSafe first, then others), and decide per secret which part of SwarmCloud may use it. Today the TypeSafe key has its own provider-keys path (docs/provider-keys.md), forge tokens have another (Secret Manager `swarm-tenant-<tenant>-git`, the #1041 redesign), and each new provider would add a third.

Owner, 2026-10-14 ~21:50 PDT, verbatim: "we need to be able to set and manage typesafe and other apis from api providers we use, I think we need a secrets store management solution that will store any credential and based on a set of check boxes, we can enable every secret, one at a time to be used in different scenarios with different components. For example we can store an api key and only allow access to it for a specific runtime job type and image like jev-browser or claude-code-browser. All these secrets will be in the workspace of the user and it will provide a way to grant access to specific secrets in different components of the swarmcloud and runner profiles"

### What would you like to see?

A workspace secrets store:
- any credential stored once, in the user's workspace;
- per secret, a set of checkboxes granting it to specific consumers: a runner profile (claude-code-browser), a runtime image or tool (jev-browser), or a platform component (the judge, the merge step);
- each grant enabled one at a time;
- a consumer that is not granted a secret can never read it.

### Where would this live?

Settings › Workspace › Secrets (new), swarm-api, the worker's secret delivery, Secret Manager and IAM.

### How do you do it today?

Per-feature paths: the provider-keys record for TypeSafe; `scripts/create-secrets.sh --stdin` for forge tokens and platform secrets; the worker reads each through its own code.

### How would you know it worked?

A TypeSafe key stored once and granted only to claude-code-browser + jev-browser is readable by a jev-browser task, and refused (and audited) for every other profile. The grant is changed from the console without a deploy.

### Constraint check

- [X] Touching the other team's resources in the shared project `saga-agents-staging` — must not (deny-list)
- [X] A change to the frozen contract in `apps/common/swarm_common/` — likely: runner profiles may need to declare the secret slots they consume. That is a request, not a code change.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Owner decision, 2026-10-14 ~22:40 PDT: user-signed submissions as phase 2.**

- **Phase 1** is the release design in docs/design/workspace-secrets.md §3.3. The worker signs the release with its per-attempt Ed25519 key, and swarm-api checks the attempt, the generation fence, the workspace and the grants, all from the signed task spec.
- **Phase 2** adds per-person signing keys (a console passkey, or a key the sc plugin keeps in the OS keychain).
  - Every submission is signed, building on #342's signed step specs.
  - A personal secret is released only to a task whose spec carries a valid signature from the secret's owner; a group-workspace secret needs a current member's signature.
  - Headless jobs (schedules, issue runs, CI-fix rounds) use owner-signed standing grants.
  - The point: a compromised scheduler or database, or another member of a group, cannot create a task that pulls someone's personal secrets.

Still open: the design's §9 questions (enforcement option, the release route, personal secrets in group workspaces, who manages group secrets, rotation, audit retention, provider keys, inject mode, default grants).

comments.body:

- **Q2 the release route:** allowed. It follows from Q1: `POST /v1/attempts/{id}/secrets:release` is the one route that serves credential material, and the no-read-path test is amended to name it.
- **Q3 personal secrets in group workspaces:** opt-in per secret, and only on the owner's own submissions.
- **Q4 group workspace secrets:** platform admins only add, rotate and grant.

Q5–Q9 are still open.

- **Q6 audit:** release rows kept 90 days by TTL.
- **Q7 provider keys and pool accounts:** listed read-only, not moved.
- **Q8 inject mode:** a TypeSafe forwarder in the first build.
- **Q9 default grants:** migrated TypeSafe keys start with jev-browser and judge ticked.

Q1–Q4 are in the previous comment, and user-signed submissions are phase 2.

title: One in eight claude-code-browser attempts started its agent with no live browser: Playwright MCP absent or SWARM_CDP_ENDPOINT empty
body:
### What happened

In benchmark batch `devb-1015` (u-bogdan, 60 `claude-code-browser` tasks submitted within 18 s at 2026-10-15 09:17:37–09:17:56Z), 8 of 60 runs (13%) started with no live browser:
- 4 runs that were told to use Playwright MCP found no Playwright MCP tools. Each agent then launched its own headless Chromium through the image's Python Playwright, which bypasses the live browser and the "no hidden browser" stub.
- 4 runs that were told to use dev-browser found `SWARM_CDP_ENDPOINT` empty, so the dev-browser wrapper had no live browser to attach to. It correctly refused to launch one of its own.

The helper's `live_browser` column agrees: 25/30 Playwright and 26/30 dev-browser runs used the live browser.

### Severity

S2

### Where you saw it

Agents: live browser

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), release of 2026-10-15 ~08:50Z (main 3b2479bc), profile claude-code-browser, GKE.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `scripts/browser-bench.sh --batch <name>` (or submit 60 `claude-code-browser` tasks at once).
2. Read each answer. Some say the browser tools "weren't available in this session" or that `SWARM_CDP_ENDPOINT` is empty.

### What you expected instead

Every `claude-code-browser` attempt either gets its live browser (sidecar ready, `SWARM_CDP_ENDPOINT` set, Playwright MCP registered) before the agent starts, or does not start: it waits or parks without holding capacity. It never runs an agent with no browser. The control: 52 of the 60 runs in the same batch, same profile and same minute did get the live browser, so the measurement could have come out clean.

### Identifiers

- Task id: task_cf08f28bc5ee4b2bab48, task_606e81bb3082452485b6, task_f2b37f10f135442ab91d, task_ac510920e4804c78831f (Playwright MCP missing); task_611f22e81e4d49ccbe26, task_0e7d8129cc51450eaa30, task_28e588f9d96542b785e2, task_7b5831d1120e451eae59 (SWARM_CDP_ENDPOINT empty)
- Release or CI run id: benchmark batch devb-1015

### Screenshots, errors, logs

~/.swarm/browser-bench/devb-1015/results.tsv (`live_browser` column). Answer excerpt: "The dev-browser CLI ... finds that browser through the SWARM_CDP_ENDPOINT setting, which is empty in this session."

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Cause, measured 2026-10-15 ~11:10Z from the pods' container logs (k8s_container, swarm-tenant-u-bogdan):** in every no-browser run checked (task_0e7d8129, task_ac510920, task_cf08f28b, task_28e588f9), the display sidecar's live gate came up normally: "chromium up; CDP proxy on 127.0.0.1:9222", "live gate: ready", "worker registered". About 4 s later it logged `record=tunnel_refused {"cause": "relay unreachable: gaierror"}`, a DNS resolution failure for the relay. The worker then logged **`no live path for this attempt`** and started the agent with no `SWARM_CDP_ENDPOINT` and no Playwright MCP, although the local CDP proxy was up. 11 pods logged `tunnel_refused` in the 6 h before the reading. All 60 benchmark tasks started within the same ~2 minutes.

So there are two defects:
1. The relay hostname does not resolve under a burst of pod starts. This looks like DNS: a gaierror, not a refusal.
2. The agent's browser is made to depend on the viewer tunnel. A failed tunnel removes the agent's local CDP endpoint as well as the human view.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Close sweep 2026-10-16, still open.**

Status, read 2026-10-16 ~13:00Z. PR 1372 is on main and released in 85114dbf (2026-10-15 23:39Z). The agent's browser now depends only on the gate being ready: a refused viewer tunnel costs the human view, not the agent's CDP endpoint, and is retried for the whole attempt, and a gate that is not ready fails the attempt retryably (live_gate_unavailable) with its lease and capacity released, so an agent is no longer started without a browser. Since that release, QA batch post-1015 had the live browser on 34 of 35 agent runs (the 35th inconclusive because its actions read returned 404), and tenant pod logs show no tunnel_refused and no 'no live path' lines, against 21 and 9 in the two hours around the devb-1015 burst. Two things keep this open: no 60-task burst has run since, and the relay name failing to resolve under a burst has no cause or fix yet; the gate now logs EAI_AGAIN or EAI_NONAME, which will say which. Next step: re-run scripts/browser-bench.sh with 60 tasks and expect 60 of 60 with the live browser.

title: A parked live-browser attempt does not carry IndexedDB to the resumed attempt; build it when a task is measured losing state
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Resume a parked live-browser task and find the web app exactly as it was left. PR 1365 (QA-RESUME, part of #1362) carries the parked attempt's tabs in every workspace, and their cookies and localStorage in a personal workspace. It does not carry IndexedDB, so an app that keeps its state there starts empty after a park.

### What would you like to see?

At park, the JSON-safe contents of each open origin's IndexedDB are exported (through an isolated-world script). On resume, each tab is loaded once with page scripts held, the stores are written, and the tab is reloaded. Values that are not JSON (Blobs, Dates, ArrayBuffers) are dropped. The size counts against the same 56 KiB Secret Manager jar as cookies and localStorage.

**Owner decision 2026-10-15 (~03:40 PDT): build this only once a real task is measured losing IndexedDB state across a park.** Until then this issue records the gap and the design.

### Where would this live?

Agents: live browser (apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/livegate/tabs.py, from PR 1365)

### How do you do it today?

You don't. A task that needs it must redo the work after a resume. Nothing in QA scenario S5-resume used IndexedDB.

### How would you know it worked?

A QA scenario writes an IndexedDB record in part one, parks, and reads the same record in part two without navigating.

### Constraint check

No caller input selects anything (invariant 10). A parked task holds no capacity (invariant 1). The restore costs one extra page load per restored tab.

title: The internal Jev URL is plain http to a Service that only passes TLS on 443, so no internal judgment can reach the decision API
body:
### What happened

The internal Jev backends call `http://decision-api.swarm-system.svc.cluster.local/{jev,laya}/v1/decide`, and that URL cannot reach the decision API. The tailnet egress Service `decision-api` listens only on **443** and passes **raw TLS** through to `decision-api-staging.taile0bda9.ts.net:443`, whose certificate is issued for the tailnet name.

Measured 2026-10-15 ~19:55Z from a `swarm-judge: internal` pod in `swarm-tenant-eng`, with the egress Running and joined to the tailnet (node `swarmcloud-decision-api`):

| URL | result |
|---|---|
| `http://decision-api.swarm-system.svc.cluster.local/jev/v1/decide` (what the code sends) | curl exit 28, timeout (no port 80 on the Service) |
| `https://decision-api.swarm-system.svc.cluster.local/jev/v1/decide` | curl exit 35, TLS failure (certificate name mismatch) |
| `https://decision-api-staging.taile0bda9.ts.net/jev/v1/decide` with `--connect-to …:443:decision-api.swarm-system.svc.cluster.local:443` | HTTP 400 from the API (the path works) |

Control: the same request from an **unlabelled** pod returned `000` after 10 s, so the NetworkPolicy holds.

### What you expected

With `internal_decision_api_enabled = true`, a live-browser pod whose workspace chose Internal Jev or Internal Laya reaches the decision API. Today, turning the switch on would make every internal judgment fail, and the wrapper would report Jev as unavailable.

### Where

- `apps/scheduler/scheduler/judgment.py` `INTERNAL_DECISION_SERVICE`
- `apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/judgment.py` `INTERNAL_DECISION_SERVICE`
- `images/agent-runtime-browser/jev-browser/bin/jev-browser-mcp` `DECISION_SERVICE`
- `terraform/infra/locals.tf` `internal_decision_api_url`
- `kubernetes/swarm-system/tailscale-egress.yaml` (Service: 443 only, raw TLS)

### Also

The runbook's probe pod (`docs/runbooks/tailscale-egress.md`, "Verify") is refused in a tenant namespace three ways:
- the LimitRange minimum is 250m / 512Mi;
- `swarm-worker-pod-hardening` requires `automountServiceAccountToken: false`;
- the namespace's default 20Gi ephemeral storage is over Autopilot's 10Gi cap, so the probe needs an explicit `ephemeral-storage`.

The fix is decided with the owner before it is built: `internal_decision_api_enabled` stays off until then.

title: Every agent runtime reads the code graph from one shared, cached graph service instead of a per-pod snapshot, kept in sync by push-triggered indexing
body:
### What it is

Every agent runtime gets the repository's code graph and index (call graphs, impact, tests_for, territory, the whole index on request) from **one shared, multi-tenant graph service**, instead of copying a snapshot into each pod. It is injected into the context at start (the context pack) and available as a tool for the rest of the task, for planning, implementation, review, tests and merge decisions.

### Owner decisions (2026-10-15 ~17:15 PDT)

1. **Shape: a shared service plus a local shim.**
   - A read-only `swarm-graph` Deployment in `swarm-system` serves the graph tools over MCP/HTTP to every runtime (claude-code, codex, claude-code-browser).
   - Each request carries an attempt ticket minted by swarm-api (tenant, repo, generation; the egress and TypeSafe ticket pattern).
   - A tiny stdio shim in each pod, installed and registered in every runtime's MCP config by the worker, forwards queries and adds the `stale` marks from the agent's own working tree (one `git status` per answer).
   - Nothing is copied into a pod, so this adds no per-agent storage or start-up time.
2. **Trigger: push webhook plus a poll fallback.**
   - GitHub App push events on a registered repository's default branch enqueue an incremental index job.
   - A 5-minute poll enqueues one whenever the head is past the indexed commit, catching any missed webhook.
   - The scheduled full re-index stays as the safety net.
3. **Sharing: never across workspaces.**
   - Every index, cache entry and read is keyed by (tenant, manifest digest). Invariant 9 holds as written, even when two workspaces register the same public repository.

### Caching (as recommended)

- **The index of a commit is immutable**, so cache keys are (tenant, manifest digest) and a new commit is a new key. Nothing needs invalidating, and a hit is always correct for the commit it names.
- **Layers:**
  - decoded shards in an in-memory LRU per replica, warmed on promotion;
  - a query-result cache keyed on (tenant, digest, tool, arguments) for expensive answers such as impact and call-graph expansion;
  - GCS as the store of record, with content-addressed shards shared across commits within a tenant.
- **An agent on another commit** is served from the nearest indexed ancestor, with its changed paths marked `stale`.

### What changes from today

Today `graphstage.py` copies the snapshot to `work/.swarm-context/snapshot/` in every pod, and each agent runs its own `python -m agent_worker.graphmcp` (knowledge-graph.md §5.3: no network, no credential). This replaces that delivery. The no-network property becomes: a network hop to one in-cluster service, gated by a ticket.

### Next

A design doc (`docs/design/graph-service.md`), then a split into lanes: service, shim and worker install, ticket route, push trigger and poll, incremental indexing, context-pack switch, caches, and migration off per-pod staging.

   2. Mint `swarm-graph-ticket-key` with `scripts/create-secrets.sh --graph-ticket-key`.
   3. Set `graph_service.serve = true`, keeping `enabled = false`. Two pods run in swarm-system, and no workspace uses them until its `graph_delivery = service`.

   `serve` lands in a second PR, after the key has a version. A Cloud Run reference to a secret with no version stops swarm-api from starting (GS-INFRA's Q3 deviation).
2. **GS-HOOKS caller identity: reuse the rollup sweeper identity.** The receiver runs as the sweeper service account and calls `POST /v1/admin/repositories/push` as it. No new `GITHUB_HOOKS_USERS` list.

   The owner was shown the trade-off: a public-facing service then holds every sweeper route, for every tenant, so a compromised receiver has that blast radius. The dedicated identity was the recommended option and was declined.

### What happened
A re-run of the exhaustive visual QA of the SwarmCloud console (`apps/swarm-ui`), SwarmCloud workflow wf_44fa99a703dd4daf971a (2026-10-16). It rendered every route in headless Chromium at 1440×900 and 400×800, light and dark, after #1038's 15 fix lanes merged (PRs 1039-1088). It re-checked each of #1038's 152 findings and recorded new ones.

- **#1038's 152:** 111 FIXED, 11 CHANGED but resolved, 22 CHANGED with a defect left, 8 STILL. So **122 are closed and 30 remain**.
- **NEW:** 111 distinct (S1 0 · S2 25 · S3 86). 21 of them are on the Automate routes (`automate/schedules`, `automate/approvals`), which were rendered for the first time.
- **Open now: 141, S1 1 · S2 31 · S3 109** (on 10-11: S1 6 · S2 55 · S3 91).
- The only open S1 is **V002**. A 422 refusal on the Submit forms is still drawn away from the button, under the field (~1,000 px above it at 400 px) or outside `OutcomeSlot`, with no scroll or focus move, and the panel keeps saying "Ready to send".

The full merged report is in the comments below, in parts. Its §3 proposes 17 file-disjoint lanes: R1-R15 in wave 1, and R16-R17 in wave 2 behind hub files.

S1: V002's refusal half; a failed submit can look like nothing happened.

### Where you saw it
Every console section: Overview, Work (Agents, Workflows, Runs, Timeline, Repositories, Setup, Access, Submit), Automate (Schedules, Approvals), Capacity, Admin.

### Environment
SwarmCloud console, fixture mode, headless Chromium (Playwright), on 2026-10-16 against main at the time of the run.

### Steps to reproduce
Open each route at 400×800 and 1440×900, in both themes. Each finding names its route, state and viewport, and has a screenshot in its task's artifacts.

### What you expected instead
- Ids and long tokens wrap or ellipsize inside their cells.
- No inner container scrolls sideways at 400 px.
- A submit's refusal is drawn where the button is.
- The new Automate screens follow the same rules as the rest.

### Identifiers
Workflow wf_44fa99a703dd4daf971a; summary task task_1ad45814650e4e77ad94 (visual-qa-report.md, questions.json); group tasks qa-accounts task_5c4321a1c8b04125b29d, qa-admin task_be4002800bb448fe9555, qa-capacity task_013413f11ce248119b60, qa-runs task_7333d1a0345948db9c08, qa-setup task_1875875014334dbab9b3, qa-submit task_0c3812574bdf4185b6d5, qa-work task_fd01b400704b424bbc79. title: [feat] A task cannot reach its caller's MCP server, because a dispatch can attach neither an MCP server nor a short-lived credential for it
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Run SwarmCloud workflows from an application that holds the knowledge its agents need (an indexed graph of documents, conversations and decisions) behind its own MCP server. Each agent must query that server during its run and write its results back through it, with a credential that is valid for that one run only and expires with it. Today a task's only inputs are its prompt, the one repository it clones, and the inputs its profile declares (`issue` for claude-code). There is no way to give a task an MCP server or a credential for one, so the application must paste context into the prompt and lose everything the agent would have looked up on its own.

### What would you like to see?

- A dispatch (and a workflow step) may name **MCP servers** by URL, from a list the tenant has registered in advance (so a caller cannot point an agent at an arbitrary host).
- A dispatch may carry an **ephemeral credential** per named server: supplied by the caller at dispatch time, delivered to the worker only, injected as the server's auth header, never logged, never written to artifacts, and destroyed when the attempt ends. Redaction treats it like every other secret.
- The worker writes the MCP configuration for Claude Code before the agent starts, so the agent sees the server's tools like any local MCP server.
- Builds on #1347 (workspace secrets store): long-lived secrets come from the store, per-run credentials from the dispatch.

### Where would this live?

API — /v1 (apps/swarm-api); Scheduler — admission and dispatch (apps/scheduler); Worker on GKE (apps/agent-worker); Claude Code plugin or MCP bridge (swarm_dispatch, swarm_workflow gain the fields).

### How do you do it today?

Context is retrieved by the caller and pasted into each step's prompt; results come back only as artifact files. The agent cannot ask a follow-up question of the knowledge it was given.

### How would you know it worked?

- A claude-code task dispatched with a registered MCP server and a credential calls a tool on that server, and the server sees the credential.
- The same dispatch naming an unregistered URL is refused before admission.
- The credential appears in no log route, artifact, checkpoint or event; a test searches all of them for it.
- After the attempt ends, the worker holds no copy of it.

### Constraint check

- [x] A change to the frozen contract in `apps/common/swarm_common/`: new dispatch fields (`mcp_servers`, ephemeral credentials). Needs an entry in `docs/contract-change-requests.md`.
- Invariant 10 holds: the caller names registered servers, never an image, command or resource spec.

title: [feat] A workflow step can read only the one repository its workflow clones, so a step that must understand a product spread across several repositories cannot
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Have one step reason over a product whose code lives in several repositories (API, web app, infrastructure, SDK). The repository is workflow-level, so every step clones the same one; the only way to read the others is one task per repository plus a merge step that sees summaries, not code.

### What would you like to see?

- A step may list **additional repositories**, each with a ref, checked out read-only beside the primary one (e.g. `./repos/<name>`), from repositories the tenant has registered.
- The primary repository stays the only one whose changes are carried back (`collect`, `direct-pr`, `integrate` unchanged).
- Pinning works as for the primary: each additional checkout is pinned to the commit its ref resolved to at submission.

### Where would this live?

API — /v1 (apps/swarm-api); Worker on GKE (apps/agent-worker); Claude Code plugin or MCP bridge.

### How do you do it today?

One indexer task per repository, each writing a summary artifact, then a step that stages all the summaries. Cross-repository questions ("which service owns this endpoint the web app calls?") get answered from summaries, not code.

### How would you know it worked?

- A step with two additional repositories sees all three checkouts at their pinned commits.
- A change made inside an additional checkout is not in the collected patch.
- A repository the tenant has not registered is refused at submission.

### Constraint check

- [x] Frozen contract: new step field. Needs an entry in `docs/contract-change-requests.md`.
- Workspace size: 4 GiB today for claude-code; several checkouts may need a larger named resource class.

title: [feat] Every claude-code step runs the pinned Opus model, so a summarizing or classifying step costs as much as a deep-reasoning one
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Run pipelines in which most steps are deep reasoning (Opus) and some are mechanical: classify feedback, summarize a source, reformat a document. Since #226 every claude-code step runs the pinned `claude-opus-5-5`, and invariant 10 rightly forbids a caller from naming a model.

### What would you like to see?

Model tiers as **profiles**, keeping invariant 10 intact: the caller still picks a profile by name and the profile fixes the model.

- `claude-code` (unchanged): `claude-opus-5-5`
- `claude-code-sonnet`: `claude-sonnet-5-5`
- `claude-code-haiku`: `claude-haiku-5-5`

Each is a catalogue entry with its own `MODEL` in Terraform, visible in `swarm_profiles`.

### Where would this live?

Runner profile catalogue; Terraform (job env per profile); Worker (apps/agent-worker, `--model` already passed since #226).

### How do you do it today?

Every step runs Opus, including steps that only reformat text.

### How would you know it worked?

- `swarm_profiles` lists the two new profiles with their models.
- An attempt on `claude-code-sonnet` records `claude-sonnet-5-5`.
- `input.model` from a caller is still refused (the #226 test still passes).

### Constraint check

- Invariant 10 holds: the model comes from the profile, never from the caller.
