comments.body:
**Finding, 2026-10-20 ~07:50Z:** after a merge from main, `scripts/changed-guards.sh` diffs against the branch's previous head instead of its merge base with main, so a conflict fix selects every file main changed.

- **Measured** by the conflict-fix step on PR 1696 (task_af1a2f10e81d4aeaaf40).
- **The diff base** was `d78d49fc`, the branch head before `origin/main` was merged in.
- **The effect:** the 59 files main had changed since the branch left it counted as "changed", which selected 154 test files. Run in four parts one after another, they hit the 600 s limit in part 3, with no test failing.
- **Expected:** a pre-publish run after a merge selects by the diff against the merge base with main, which is what the pull request will show, not by the branch's own pre-merge head.

GUARDS-DEDUP (PR 1704) touches the same script. If it does not already fix this, it is a small follow-up there.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Finding, 2026-10-20 ~10:40Z:** the platform's CI-fix and conflict-fix steps write a `pr-title.txt` taken from their own commit's headline. If a later publish ever applies it, the lane's real title would be replaced, and that title carries the `(TAG;` the chain watcher matches.

**Seen three times tonight:**
- PR 1704: "test: the QA account-name test imports swarm_api inside the test…";
- PR 1703: "Re-run CI: unit shard 1/4 did not reproduce red on c490b6c";
- PR 1696's CI-fix.

All three PRs still carry their lane titles, read 10:40Z, so nothing has applied the file yet.

**Expected:** a fix step that does not own the PR's title writes no `pr-title.txt`, or the publisher ignores one from a fix round.

title: SwarmCloud serves whether caller MCP servers, await-input and service answers are on for a workspace, so a caller need not guess
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Product Oracle (tenant u-or-9a0792) needs to know whether three SwarmCloud features are on for its workspace before it offers them to its users: caller MCP servers (#1433), the await-input step (#1436), and a service workspace answering its own waits (#1577). SwarmCloud serves none of the three states today. After every Oracle deploy, Oracle cannot tell that MCP is on until a workflow submission confirms it. Its New run form then warns users that agents cannot read Oracle, which is untrue; this was seen 2026-10-20 ~19:00Z. Owner decision, 2026-10-20: build it.

### What would you like to see?

A `features` block on `GET /v1/tenants/me`, per workspace, holding the state the serving process actually uses for each feature:

- `caller_mcp`: swarm-api's `SWARM_MCP_SERVERS` (`mcp_servers.mcp_servers_enabled()`).
- `await_input`: whether the `await-input` runner profile is available (`RUNNER_PROFILES["await-input"].available`, read through the catalogue, never restated).
- `service_answer`: whether this workspace is a service workspace whose own principal may answer its waits (`awaitinput.py`).

Each value is `true`, `false` or `"unknown"`, and `unknown` is never shown as false. The sc bridge's status shows the same three.

### Where would this live?

API (`apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/routes/tenants.py` `@router.get("/me")`, its schema), and the MCP bridge / plugin (`apps/swarm-mcp`).

### How do you do it today?

Oracle learns each state at submit or answer time and persists what it learned as a workaround.

### How would you know it worked?

- With `SWARM_MCP_SERVERS` off, `GET /v1/tenants/me` says `caller_mcp: false`; with it on, `true`.
- The same holds for `await-input` availability.
- A service workspace says `service_answer: true`, and a group or personal workspace says `false`.
- Oracle's status read stops saying "not reported by SwarmCloud".

### Constraint check

Read-only, with no new IAM. It names no image, command or resource (invariant 10). It reads the frozen catalogue without restating it (rule 1).

title: The plugin's check and attach-all stop after 4 pages of running workflows, so older stuck work is never flagged
body:
### What happened

`swarm_check`, `swarm_workflow_launch {attach: "all"}` and `swarm_workflows` read at most 4 pages of 50 running workflows in a tenant, then stop. They report "stopped after 4 pages of 50 running workflows; older ones are not checked" (or "older running workflows, if any, are not listed"). In tenant eng on 2026-10-20 (20:11Z, plugin sc-v0.5.45) every check and attach-all hit the cap. So stuck or stale work older than the newest 200 running workflows is never flagged, and never gets a row. Reported by Product Oracle's session and seen in this session the same day.

### Severity

S2

### Where you saw it

The sc plugin: `/sc check`, `/sc attach --all`, `/sc workflows`.

### Environment

SwarmCloud (dev), tenant eng, sc plugin 0.5.45.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In a tenant with more than 200 running (non-terminal) workflows, run `/sc check`.
2. Read `running_incomplete_because` / `incomplete_because`.

### What you expected instead

The check reads every running workflow it is scoped to. The API should filter on the server (`GET /v1/workflows?state=...&claude_session=<id>&repository=<repo>`), so a session's check reads only its own work in one or two pages and never stops short. That fix is the owner's choice of 2026-10-20 over paging to the end.

### Identifiers

- `apps/swarm-mcp/swarm_mcp/check.py:106` `WORKFLOW_LIST_PAGES = 4`, with the same cap again at `apps/swarm-mcp/swarm_mcp/sc.py:721`.
- `apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/routes/workflows.py:118` `list_workflows()`.

### Does it look like one of these?

The cap is stated twice, in check.py and sc.py, which is the mirrored-copy shape this repository keeps finding.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

`"incomplete_because": "stopped after 4 pages of 50 workflows; older running workflows, if any, are not listed"` (swarm_workflow_launch, 2026-10-20 19:03Z)

### Anything else

Lane CHECK-FILTER (API query parameters plus the bridge's callers). Built after visual-QA wave 1.

title: The verification gate reports five false failures: a jq argument limit, one target's leases read by the next, another tenant's attempts, GKE work it cannot see, and a stale missing-output expectation
body:
### What happened

The verification gate, `make verify-remote` (the swarm-verify Cloud Run job, tenant eng), was run on 2026-10-20 as the baseline for the isolation cutover (#1457). It reported 3 of its 4 targets red: `concurrency-test`, `race-test` and `e2e-test`; smoke-test passed. Read against the platform's own records, every failure is a test defect or one target interfering with the next. None of them is a platform defect:

1. **concurrency-test never sampled.** `scripts/concurrency-test.sh` lines 133 and 150 died with `jq: Argument list too long`: the growing pools/leases/tasks sample is passed as `--argjson` (around `all="$(jq -nc --argjson a "${all}" ...)"`). The script then exited without cancelling its 300 submitted mock tasks (execution swarm-verify-gztsl).
2. **race-test read another target's leases.** It narrowed `runner:mock` to 1 slot and saw `active=40` while it had submitted only 12 tasks. 40 is the pool's normal limit, filled by concurrency-test's leftover backlog. None of race-test's own 12 tasks was leased ("checked 0 task(s) with attempts"), so nothing was admitted past the narrowed limit (execution swarm-verify-7pkc9).
3. **e2e [7] asked for another tenant's attempts.** It scans Firestore attempts and asks the API for each task's attempts. The tasks it reported (e.g. task_dcedd511e54345349960, task_19c440f8627f44548f8c, task_25633ce0bd874d619819) are the **smoke** tenant's, and the gate runs as **eng**, so the 404 is tenant isolation working.
4. **e2e [10] cannot see GKE work.** "No task is holding capacity against an execution that is gone" lists Cloud Run executions only. The 10 tasks it flagged are eng claude-code agents running on GKE Autopilot (e.g. task_cf154a98da3f42bfae36, dispatched as swarm-tenant-eng/swarm-cf154a98da3f42bfae36-1 at 20:10:02Z).
5. **e2e [6] expects the old missing-output behaviour.** The negative control expects the producer that never wrote its promised file to SUCCEED and the consumer to fail. The platform now fails the producer itself (`expected outputs missing`), which acceptance's workflow group asserts ("a missing one fails it before the child runs ... FAILED outputs_missing").

### Severity

S2

### Where you saw it

`make verify-remote` (scripts/verify-remote.sh), job swarm-verify, executions gztsl (concurrency), 7pkc9 (race) and cltfv (e2e), 2026-10-20 ~20:37-20:56Z.

### Environment

SwarmCloud (dev), main at 3252c86a and cc2dedea.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `make verify-remote` with the default targets.
2. Read each execution's log in Cloud Logging (`resource.labels.job_name="swarm-verify"`).

### What you expected instead

- A green gate on a healthy platform, so the isolation cutover has a baseline.
- concurrency-test passes its sample by file or stdin, never as an argument, and always cancels what it submitted, even when it fails.
- race-test refuses to start while its pool already holds leases it did not make, or waits for the pool to drain.
- e2e [7] checks only the calling tenant's tasks.
- e2e [10] reads the attempt's backend and asks GKE for GKE work.
- e2e [6] expects the producer to fail with outputs missing, and the consumer never to run.

### Identifiers

`scripts/concurrency-test.sh` (about 125-155), `scripts/race-test.sh` [2]-[3], `scripts/e2e-test.sh` checks [6], [7] and [10], `scripts/verify-remote.sh` (target order).

### Does it look like one of these?

The isolation design (#1457) asks for this gate before and after the cutover; this is the baseline run.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

```
scripts/concurrency-test.sh: line 133: /usr/bin/jq: Argument list too long
OVER LIMIT: runner:mock active=40 limit=1
Firestore has attempt att_0128e390edcc468d9be0 for task task_dcedd511e54345349960, and the API would not serve that task's attempts (HTTP 404)
task task_cf154a98da3f42bfae36 is RUNNING against execution swarm-cf154a98da3f42bfae36-1-44888, which is not running
FAIL the negative control's producer still succeeds: expected 'SUCCEEDED', got 'FAILED'
```

### Anything else

Lane GATE-FIX fixes the five. The acceptance groups the release ran at the same time also had reds in git-tools (`forge_refused` on a mid-task push, execution 9j7ss) and workflow (await-input revise leased 161 s after the answer, execution mk5l7). Those are acceptance's own reports, not this gate's, and are not covered here.

title: Pre-publish graph-pytest runs from the repository root, so every lane in a repository whose Python projects live in subfolders fails it
body:
### What happened

The worker's pre-publish `graph-pytest` check fails on every lane in a repository whose Python projects are not at the repository root. It runs one `uv run --quiet pytest -q -n auto ... <graph-selected files>` from the repository root (`apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/prepublish.py` `_graph_pytest()`, built by `graph_checks()`). sagaxyz/ai-studio has no root `pyproject.toml`: its projects are `api/` (whose dev group provides pytest) and `runner/`. From the root, uv finds no project and fails in 0.0 s with `error: Failed to spawn: pytest — No such file or directory (os error 2)`. The check is then FAILED, each lane's agent spends its one fix turn proving the code is fine, and the PR body carries a "Pre-publish checks failed" section that is not about the code. Reported by the AI Studio session on 2026-10-20 for PRs 715, 717, 718, 721 and 725 (e.g. task_9792dbf0c28c43f58316, task_c74925202a8b41798165), and confirmed against the code on main.

### Severity

S2

### Where you saw it

The worker's pre-publish checks (`prepublish-checks.md`, and the PR body) on sagaxyz/ai-studio lanes.

### Environment

SwarmCloud (dev), worker image from main 2026-10-20.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a lane on a repository whose Python tests live under a subproject with its own `pyproject.toml` and none at the root.
2. Read the lane's prepublish checks.

### What you expected instead

graph-pytest groups the selected test files by their nearest ancestor directory that holds a `pyproject.toml`, the way the vitest check already groups by package (`_package_root`). It runs `uv run pytest` once per project, from that directory, with paths relative to it. A test file with no project above it, or a repository root that is not a Python project, is reported SKIPPED with a plain note, never FAILED. A "Failed to spawn: pytest" or "no project found" from uv is likewise SKIPPED with that reason.

### Identifiers

`apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/prepublish.py` `_graph_pytest()` and `graph_checks()`.

### Does it look like one of these?

#1605 (pre-publish ran tests that needed a service it did not have) is the same family: a check that cannot run must say so, not fail the lane.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

```
error: Failed to spawn: `pytest`
  Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

### Anything else

Lane PREPUB-PYPROJECT fixes it.

title: A row that nests its answer one level too deep reports a finished step with no excerpt, cost, PR or artifacts
body:
### What happened

A `[SwarmCloud]` row reports a finished step or task with an empty result: the state is right, but `answer_excerpt`, `cost_usd`, `duration_s`, `pr_url` and `last_error` are null and `artifacts` is `[]`. Meanwhile `swarm_result` on the same task shows the full result.

The cause is in `plugin/workflows/run.js` `stepAnswer()`:
- Some sc:step and sc:task rows call `StructuredOutput` with the documented object nested one level too deep: `{"result": {"state": ..., "result": {...every field...}}}` instead of `{"state": ..., "result": {...}}`. `STEP_RESULT` requires nothing and allows any extra property, so StructuredOutput accepts it.
- `stepAnswer()` then reads `answer.result` as the step's fields. It finds only `state` and a nested `result` there, so it returns the state and nulls everything else.

Measured 2026-10-20 ~22:40Z in the journal of the QAFIX2-OVERVIEW attach run (wf_4b9dc2654dce4a43a342, plugin 0.5.45). It has five rows:
- **Nested shape:** the review, fix and merge rows. All three ended null in the run's summary. The review row had returned its full MERGE verdict excerpt, cost and duration. The merge row lost its `last_error` "PARKED on CI_PENDING ... PR #1760".
- **Documented shape:** the re-review row, the control. Its summary kept every field, which shows the reading works when the shape is right.

Also seen:
- PREPUB-PYPROJECT's implement row (task_dbe7094639ca4da88a25, 5 min, $1.13, 7 artifacts per `swarm_result`).
- Product Oracle's session on 2026-10-20: two `attach_tasks` rows, task_2a8fa001a602413086d9 (PR #127, $3.39, 9 artifacts) and task_a8380238991242adadfb (PR #124, $1.72, 7 artifacts). So `taskRow` is affected as well as `followRow`, and the cause is not task length.

### Severity

S2

### Where you saw it

The /workflows panel rows and the run results of `/sc:swarmcloud` (attach and attach_tasks).

### Environment

sc plugin 0.5.45 (main is at 0.5.46 with the same `stepAnswer`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Attach a workflow with `/sc attach <wf_id>` and let its steps finish.
2. Compare each step in the run's result with `swarm_result` on its task.

### What you expected instead

A row's answer, in either shape, reaches the run's result whole. `stepAnswer()` unwraps the doubly nested form. When `answer.result` carries no step fields of its own but holds an object `result`, read that inner object, with the state from it or from the outer level. Every existing shape keeps reading as today: the documented one, the flat pre-0.5.17 one, and `result: null`. A row whose fields are all missing after unwrapping still reads as today.

### Identifiers

`plugin/workflows/run.js` `stepAnswer()`, used by `followRow()` and the task rows.

### Does it look like one of these?

#285 (a relay that retyped its answer lost the state) and ROW-SKIP (#1194) are the same family: the row's answer shape drifting from what the script reads.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

```
Stage 2 {"result": {"state": "str", "result": {"state": "str", "answer_excerpt": "str", "cost_usd": "float", ...}}}   -> summary: all null
Stage 4 {"result": {"state": "str", "answer_excerpt": "str", "duration_s": "float", ...}, "state": "str"}            -> summary: kept
```

### Anything else

Lane PLUGIN-ROW-NEST fixes it.

title: The sc plugin keeps a local, git-ignored build board per project, refreshed as work moves and opened with /sc build-board
body:
### What should change

The sc plugin creates and maintains a **build board for each project**: a local HTML page like the operator's hand-built SwarmCloud Build Board. It shows every lane's state, its PR and what it waits on, grouped by feature, plus a "waiting on someone" list. It is kept current as work is dispatched and progresses, and opened with `/sc build-board`.

### Why

Today the only build board is hand-maintained by one operator session from chain files and `gh` calls. Its claude.ai copy belonged to whichever claudeswitch account published it and froze when the rotation moved on (2026-10-20 ~22:45Z). Every project that dispatches work through the plugin should get the same view for free, with no account or publishing involved.

### Requirements (owner, 2026-10-20)

- Created and maintained by the plugin, per project, looking like the current build board.
- **Always stored locally** and independent of any Claude account or profile (a claudeswitch rotation changes nothing).
- **Never committed**: git-ignored by default, without editing the repository's own `.gitignore`. A `.gitignore` containing `*` inside the board's folder does this, as `.sc-swarmcloud-runs/` already does.
- **Invisible:** the files live at `<project root>/.claude/build-board/`.
- **Updated automatically** when work is dispatched, and as it progresses.
- Opened with **`/sc build-board`**.

### Decisions (owner answers, 2026-10-20 ~23:00Z)

1. **Scope:** every workflow and single task the caller submitted against this project's repository, from any Claude Code session or account. Not only the current session, and not teammates' work.
2. **Grouping:** "By feature" groups lanes by the GitHub issue each workflow names (its `issue` input, else `(#N)` in its title), labelled with the issue's name where SwarmCloud knows it. Workflows naming no issue go under "No issue". There is no hand-kept map.
3. **"Waiting on someone"** lists, from what SwarmCloud knows only (nothing read from GitHub):
   - lanes' owner questions (`questions.json` / `owner_questions`), with the built option marked;
   - steps waiting for a person (AWAITING_INPUT, and HUMAN_REQUIRED parks), each with its `/sc answer` command;
   - failed or refused merges (`checks_failed`, `merge_conflict`, `head_moved`), and CI parks over 90 minutes.

   Failed steps in general are not listed.
4. **History:** finished work stays on the board for 30 days. In-flight work always shows.

### Done when

- After any dispatch or `/sc check` in a project, `.claude/build-board/index.html` exists. It is self-contained (inline CSS and JS, light and dark themes, readable at phone width with no sideways page scroll) and reflects SwarmCloud's state.
- `git status` in that project shows nothing new.
- `/sc build-board` refreshes the page and opens it in the default browser.
- A claudeswitch account switch leaves it working.

### Anything else

Lanes BOARD-CORE (collect, render, write; the `swarm_build_board` tool and `sc build-board`) and BOARD-WIRE (automatic refresh, the `/sc build-board` verb, the session-start refresh, version bump, docs).

title: The merge step reads a cancelled check run as a failure even when a later run of the same check succeeded
body:
### What happened

SwarmCloud's merge step refuses a pull request with `checks_failed` when a check name has a cancelled run at the head, even if a later run of the same check succeeded. On 2026-10-21 the operator cancelled stranded CI runs (the runner dispatcher incident, #1775) and re-ran the newest. VERIFY-GKE-READ-2's merge step (task_b469cda145cc4eaab9e7, PR 1777) then failed with "checkov (terraform + kubernetes) (cancelled, success), secret scan (cancelled, success), trivy (repo) (cancelled, success)". The platform's CI-fix loop also ran two fix rounds (task_c56002cde2dc4a99b770) over checks that had not failed.

### Severity

S2

### Where you saw it

`/sc check` merge_refused flags; the merge profile's refusal message.

### Environment

SwarmCloud, merge profile as deployed 2026-10-21.

### Steps to reproduce

1. On a lane PR waiting at its merge step, cancel one CI run and re-run it so it succeeds.
2. The merge step refuses with checks_failed.

### What you expected instead

The merge step and the CI-fix trigger judge each check name by its latest run at the head (by start time), so a cancelled run superseded by a success is not a failure. A check whose LATEST run is cancelled is still "not green" and waits, rather than failing the merge.

### Identifiers

The merge profile's check evaluation (the code that builds the "(cancelled, success)" message) and the CI-fix trigger that reads the same checks.

### Anything else

Not scheduled. Owner, 2026-10-21 ~02:00Z: the affected PRs are merged by an owner-approved operator rescue watcher (merge on mergeStateStatus CLEAN) instead of a lane for now.

title: [feat] A pull-request run reuses a green swarm/** push run that tested the same tree
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Stop testing the same tree twice on the self-hosted CI VMs. Since LANE CI-EARLY (2026-10-20), a lane's `swarm/**` push runs `application` and `terraform`, and then its pull request runs them again. In the 24 h from 2026-10-20 06:00 to 10-21 06:00 UTC, 166 (workflow, head_sha) pairs ran on the VMs both as a `swarm/**` push and as a `pull_request` run. Counting the smaller run of each pair, that's **51.5 VM-hours a day, 18% of all VM hours**. The push runs alone (133 runs) used more VM time than the PR runs (131). Measured by the ci-runners session's capacity review over 1,287 runs and 13,785 jobs.

### What would you like to see?

Keep CI-EARLY. Let a pull-request run reuse a green push run that tested the **same tree**: ci-gate passes on the recorded green, and the heavy jobs skip.

- Compare **trees, not shas**. A PR tests `refs/pull/N/merge`, whose tree differs from the lane head once main has moved, and then nothing is reused.
- Build on B1 ("Main reuses the tested tree", docs/ci.md). Every non-main run already records `tested-tree-<tree>` (the `record the tested tree` job, `scripts/lib/ci_reuse.py`). Today only main's push run reads a record back (the `changes` job's `reuse` step).
- A cancelled or failed run never records a green. Any doubt or API error means nothing is reused and every job runs.
- A skipped heavy job counts as a pass only through ci-gate's own verdict. The SwarmCloud merge step's `required_check_state`, which reads every run of a required check at the head, accepts a reused green.
- Prior art: sagaxyz/ai-studio `.github/scripts/ci_tree_reuse.py` and its `record-green-tree` job.

### Where would this live?

Release pipeline or CI (.github/workflows)

### How do you do it today?

Each lane's tree is tested twice: once on its `swarm/**` push, once on its PR.

### How would you know it worked?

A day of runs after the change shows the PR run of an up-to-date lane skipping the heavy jobs, with ci-gate green citing the push run it reused, and VM hours down by roughly the 18% above. A PR whose merge tree differs from the push run's tree, or whose push run was cancelled or red, runs everything.

### Constraint check

- [x] None of the above, as far as I can tell

Owner approved 2026-10-21 (FIX 1 of the ci-runners capacity review).

title: [feat] Sub-minute CI checks run as steps of one or two jobs instead of a VM each
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Stop paying a whole VM for jobs that do under a minute of work. In the same 24 h sample (2026-10-20 06:00 to 10-21 06:00 UTC), **3,313 of 7,341 VM jobs (45%) did under 60 s of work, 18.4 h in total**. Each paid a VM create and boot (about 52 s created-to-started at best) and took a cap slot. The most frequent per day: what this change reaches (289), platform policy assertions (272), secret scan (263), swarm-ui typecheck / component tests [name-keeper] (256), ruff check (253), format / unit tests [name-keeper] (253), release workflow wiring (252), ci-gate (252, p50 12 s), kubernetes manifests (245), trivy (238).

### What would you like to see?

Fold the sub-minute checks into one or two jobs as steps, for about 10 fewer VMs per run. Keep every required check name that the ruleset (24160219) and ci-gate read. Where a name must survive, keep a name-keeper job but run it on `ubuntu-24.04`, so it costs no VM. Every check that used to fail a run still fails it.

### Where would this live?

Release pipeline or CI (.github/workflows)

### How do you do it today?

One VM per job, sub-minute ones included. docs/ci.md "Where pull-request CI time goes" has the earlier per-job table.

### How would you know it worked?

A PR run uses about 10 fewer self-hosted VMs. Every required check name still appears on the PR. A deliberately broken input to each folded check still turns the run red.

### Constraint check

- [x] None of the above, as far as I can tell

Owner approved 2026-10-21 (FIX 2 of the ci-runners capacity review). The merge-queue rule was not chosen and stays off.

title: [bug] A GKE worker records its pod hostname as execution_name, so the gate calls live Jobs gone and cancel cannot stop the Job
body:
### What happened

On GKE, a worker records its **pod's hostname** as its attempt's `execution_name` (for example `swarm-918a848f969e406389fd-1-2cq5s`). Every reader expects the dispatcher's `<namespace>/<job>` (`swarm-tenant-eng/swarm-918a848f969e406389fd-1`).

`agent_worker.lifecycle._execution_name()` takes the first of `CLOUD_RUN_EXECUTION`, `K_REVISION`, `JOB_NAME` and `HOSTNAME` that is set. A GKE Job sets none of the first three: it sets `RUNNER_JOB_NAME` (`scheduler/dispatch.py`), so `record_attempt_start` overwrites the dispatcher's record with the pod name.

What that breaks:
- **The verification gate.** e2e [10] (`scripts/e2e-test.sh` `capacity_holder_verdict`) GETs `jobs/<pod name>`, gets 404, and reports a live agent as "RUNNING against GKE Job … is gone". The gate run at 06:45Z 2026-10-21 UTC on release 4c8f6fd9 flagged 7 running tasks this way. Every one has a live Job, `swarm-<task>-<gen>`, and pod.
- **Cancel.** The reconciler's `stopexec` calls `GkeBackend.probe(execution_name)`, which needs `<namespace>/<job>` and answers UNREADABLE "not a <namespace>/<job> name". So cancelling a GKE agent doesn't stop its Job promptly, and it runs until the reconciler's sweep reaches it.

### Severity

S2 — wrong data on screen or in the API (states, counts, capacity, costs, timings) — I can't trust what it says

### Where you saw it

Worker on GKE — browser (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-browser, kubernetes)

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), release 4c8f6fd9, read 07:33Z UTC 2026-10-21.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run any GKE agent (claude-code on GKE_AUTOPILOT) in eng.
2. Read its newest attempt's `execution_name`: the pod name.
3. `make verify-remote`: e2e [10] reports that agent's Job as gone, while `kubectl -n swarm-tenant-eng get job swarm-<task>-<gen>` shows it active.

### What you expected instead

A GKE attempt records `<namespace>/<job>`, the name the dispatcher created and every reader looks up. The gate passes on a live Job, and cancel's probe reads ACTIVE and stops it at once. An attempt recorded under a pod name before the fix is still mapped to its Job (`swarm-<task>-<gen>`, the pod name without its 5-character suffix) by the gate and the reconciler.

### Identifiers

task_918a848f969e406389fd, task_3f3f8e2700ed46f89c17, task_a2b9406305f84f8db249, task_f8688be632da4d5c895e (eng); task_a99a5d6850514e78ac6f, task_cd796fad1206460cbfc8 (u-bogdan). Gate log: e2e-test [10], run at 06:45Z.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

```
[10] No task is holding capacity against an execution that is gone
     task task_918a848f969e406389fd is RUNNING against GKE Job swarm-tenant-eng/swarm-918a848f969e406389fd-1-2cq5s is gone
FAIL tasks holding capacity with no live execution behind them: expected '0', got '7'
```
`kubectl get jobs,pods` in that namespace at the same time: `job.batch/swarm-918a848f969e406389fd-1` and `pod/swarm-918a848f969e406389fd-1-2cq5s`.

### Anything else

The control that shows the gate could have passed: the same run's cluster read succeeded (the grant from PR 1777 is in), and smoke, race and concurrency all passed. Owner decision 2026-10-21: fix it at the source (dispatcher env and worker record), and map legacy pod names in the gate and the reconciler. Lane GKE-EXEC-NAME.

title: [bug] A git-tools continuation's rebase onto main is refused foreign_author, and the refusal does not say which commit
body:
### What happened

In git-tools acceptance, phase 2 (`scripts/acceptance/groups/git-tools.sh`) runs a direct-pr continuation of the lane. It fetches the lane's branch, `git_rebase_onto` main through the planted conflict in `tests/acceptance/fixtures/git-tools/planted.txt`, and pushes. The push is refused by the worker's own authorship check (`agent_worker.gittools.GitTools._check_authorship`) with `foreign_author`, before swarm-api is called ("audited: none"). The refused commit and its author line are not recorded anywhere a reader can see. The task (task_bc8cc08d44a74e08bdb7, workspace smoke) has no `git-answers.jsonl`, and the agent's output doesn't carry the refusal. Check [1] has failed in every dev acceptance run on #1188 since at least 2026-10-20 18:01Z UTC.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Worker on Cloud Run (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-base)

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), acceptance on 136915e8 (2026-10-21 06:41Z UTC); read 07:52Z UTC.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run `accept.yml` (or `scripts/verify-remote.sh acceptance/git-tools`).
2. Phase 2's rebase lane fetches `swarm/<lane task>`, rebases it onto main through the planted conflict and pushes.
3. The tool answers `foreign_author`.

### What you expected instead

A continuation that rebases the lane's own branch onto a main it fetched through the tool can push. Main's commits are among origin's haves, and the lane's commits are this workspace's own work. If one of the rebased commits really is foreign under the rule, the refusal says which commit and which author field, and records it in `git-answers.jsonl`, so acceptance and a person can tell a real refusal from a wrong one. The rule itself (no agent pushes commits authored by someone else) stays.

### Identifiers

task_bc8cc08d44a74e08bdb7 (rebase lane, smoke), PR 445 on bogdan-alexandrescu/swarmcloud-sandbox, #1188.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

```
FAIL git-tools: a lane rebases its pull request's branch onto main through a planted conflict, pushes, and reads pr_checks, with no forge credential in its environment: no push of swarm/task_bc8cc08d44a74e08bdb7 succeeded (audited: none; the agent was answered foreign_author); no pr_checks call succeeded
```

### Anything else

The other git-tools failure, check [5], has a separate, confirmed cause: the smoke workspace's git token gets a 403 from GitHub on the sandbox's branch rules (needs metadata read). The owner is replacing that token with a sandbox-only one. Owner decision 2026-10-21: investigate-and-fix lane GITTOOLS-REBASE-AUTHOR.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body: **Correction to the confirmed-cause line above** (measured 2026-10-22): the git-tools acceptance failure that remains after PR 1807 is not the smoke token lacking "metadata read". GitHub answers the branch-rules read for the private, user-owned sandbox with 403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public", whatever token asks, so a token swap will not fix it. Details and the fix lane (GITTOOLS-PLAN403) are on #1188.

title: [bug] A periodic checkpoint still making progress past 360 s lets the lease lapse, and the reconciler reclaims a live agent
body:
### What happened

task_8cff36540fd44bf7839f (claude-code on GKE, workspace eng, from Product Oracle) failed with `lost_worker` after three attempts, all lost the same way. Read from Cloud Logging at 08:18Z UTC 2026-10-21:

- Gen 1 at 07:41:15Z, gen 3 at 07:59:09Z and gen 5 at 08:11:42Z each logged "stopped heartbeating the lease during a long operation: it outlasted its bound", with `during: "checkpoint (periodic)"` and `bound_seconds: 360`. The reconciler then reclaimed each one ("lease silent for 101-110s (grace 90s)"), and the pod was stopped.
- The checkpoints were growing, and still progressing when the bound hit. Gen 3 restored 102,262 files at 07:44:46Z, then wrote 145 MB (94,693 files) at 07:49:51Z, 194 MB (49,039 files) at 07:53:09Z, and 291 MB (238,819 files) at 08:00:50Z. That last one took about 7.5 min, past the 360 s bound (`heartbeat_meanwhile_max_seconds`, three lease timeouts).
- No OOMKilled and no eviction in the pod events. Peak RSS was 6.2 GB of 8 GB.
- The agent ran Postgres, `pytest -n 3` and a web build, so the work tree kept growing, and so did CPU contention with the archiver.

### Severity

S2 — wrong data on screen or in the API (states, counts, capacity, costs, timings) — I can't trust what it says

### Where you saw it

Worker on GKE — browser (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-browser, kubernetes)

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), release 90a6d2e2.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a claude-code task whose work tree grows to ~200k+ files (a database data dir, test caches, build output).
2. Wait for a periodic checkpoint that takes longer than 360 s.
3. The lease lapses, and the reconciler reclaims a live worker. The retry restores the big tree and repeats.

### What you expected instead

A checkpoint that is still making progress keeps its attempt's lease alive. `_heartbeat_meanwhile` keeps beating while the archive's files and bytes advance, up to a hard ceiling, so a wedged checkpoint still lapses and gets reclaimed as today. Regenerable caches stay out of checkpoints, as `checkpoint.TOOL_CACHES` already does for node_modules, so a retry doesn't restore and re-archive them.

### Identifiers

task_8cff36540fd44bf7839f; attempts att_590bf6a6b1224230aec1 (gen 1), att_08c94a3849014ec2a769 (gen 3), att_37a2dca7c23d4567b0ab (gen 5).

### Screenshots, errors, logs

```
{"during": "checkpoint (periodic)", "bound_seconds": 360, "generation": 5, ...} stopped heartbeating the lease during a long operation: it outlasted its bound, and the lease is left to expire
```

### Anything else

Owner decision 2026-10-21: bug and fix lane CHECKPOINT-PROGRESS. Oracle's stopgap in the meantime: Postgres data outside the workspace, pytest with `-p no:cacheprovider`, and build output cleaned between phases. Invariants 4 and 8 (checkpointing is mandatory and periodic; workers never sleep through a long wait) stay as they are.

title: [feat] A batch with more rows than one Claude Code run can show is attached as several runs, so every row is live at once
body:
### What are you trying to do?

See every row of a big SwarmCloud batch at once in Claude Code. Claude Code runs at most min(16, CPU cores − 2) agents per workflow run, which is 8 on a 10-core machine. Each live row is one agent, so a `/sc:swarmcloud` run attaching 18 tasks shows 8 rows and queues the other 10 until a slot frees. Reported by Product Oracle on 2026-10-21. The plugin's own cap (`max_live_rows`, 100) never comes into play.

### What would you like to see?

When a workflow, or a batch of single tasks, has more unfinished rows than one run can show, `swarm_workflow_launch` writes several titled runs, each within the host's limit (CPU cores − 2, at most 16; read where the bridge runs, the same host as Claude Code). Each run is named for its share: `SC · <name> · N steps · rows 1-8`, `rows 9-16`, and so on. The batch stays ONE SwarmCloud workflow with one console entry. The skill's `attach`, `attach --all` and `check` launch every run the reply lists.

### Where would this live?

Claude Code plugin or MCP bridge — /sc and the swarm_* tools (plugin, apps/swarm-mcp)

### How do you do it today?

Rows past the 8th wait. The only workaround is splitting a batch into several submissions, which gives up the one-workflow console entry.

### How would you know it worked?

Attaching an 18-step workflow on a 10-core machine starts 3 runs whose rows add up to 18, all live at once, with one console entry.

### Constraint check

- [x] None of the above, as far as I can tell

Owner approved 2026-10-21. Lane PLUGIN-ROW-SPLIT.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body: **Owner decision, 2026-10-21 08:23Z UTC, which overrides the design above:** a plugin setting `rows`. `summary` is the default: ONE follower row per SwarmCloud workflow (or per single-task batch), whose line sums up the step counts and changes only when they change. `per-step` gives today's row per step, split over several runs within Claude Code's per-run agent limit. Lane PLUGIN-ROW-SPLIT carries this brief.

title: [bug] The plugin build board lists 1,054 'needs you' items, mostly old questions of lanes that merged weeks ago, many twice
body:
### What happened

The plugin's build board (`swarm_build_board`, sc 0.5.49), written at 08:43Z UTC 2026-10-21 for this repository, reports **1,878 lanes, 47 in flight and 1,054 "needs you"** (`waiting: 1054`). The page is 2.1 MB. The hand-made board for the same work counts 201 lanes and a handful of open items.

"Waiting on someone" is nearly all **owner questions from lanes that finished long ago** (since 2026-10-06), many listed twice:
- **Repeated for every step:** each lane's question appears again for every step that read it.
- **Duplicated as unreadable:** the same question appears again as "Questions that could not be read", because "the worker counted 1 question(s) in questions.json, and the artifact route says absent".

Most of those questions were answered in a Claude Code session, and the lane merged. Nothing recorded the answer on the task (`swarm_task_answer` is new in 0.5.49), so the board treats them as unanswered forever.

### Severity

S2 — wrong data on screen or in the API (states, counts, capacity, costs, timings) — I can't trust what it says

### Where you saw it

Claude Code plugin or MCP bridge — /sc and the swarm_* tools (plugin, apps/swarm-mcp)

### Environment

sc plugin 0.5.49, bridge in this checkout. Read 08:51Z UTC 2026-10-21.

### Steps to reproduce

1. `/sc build-board` (or `swarm_build_board`) in a project with weeks of lanes.
2. Open `.claude/build-board/index.html` and look at "Waiting on someone".

### What you expected instead

"Waiting on someone" lists what actually waits for a person: steps parked for a person, open refused merges, CI parks over 90 min, and owner questions of lanes that are still open. For example, a lane whose PR hasn't merged, or whose workflow is still running. A lane that merged or finished isn't waiting on its old questions. One question appears once.

**This changes what counts as waiting, which the owner defined on 2026-10-20** ("questions lanes ask + steps waiting for a person + failed or refused merges", history 30 days). So it needs the owner's call before a fix lane: needs-owner.

### Identifiers

`.claude/build-board/index.html` written 2026-10-21T08:43:09Z; counts {lanes 1878, done 1579, in_flight 47, queued 0, needs_you 1054}.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

```
Owner Questions that could not be read · C1C · #123 Timeline adds up … 2026-10-06 02:39 UTC · step implement: the worker counted 1 question(s) in questions.json, and the artifact route says absent
```

### Anything else

Until this is fixed, the hourly hand board (cron aa11c053) keeps running. It wasn't retired, because the two boards don't match.

title: git_fetch answers a bare 500 for every bundle over 24 MiB because swarm-api may not create objects under tenants/<t>/attempts/
body:
### What happened

145 of 415 `git_fetch` calls in 48 h (35%) answered 5xx (134 × 500, 11 × 502). All 134 tracebacks end in `storage.objects.create` denied on `swarm-artifacts-saga-agents-staging/objects/tenants/eng/attempts/<attempt>/git/<call>.fetch.bundle`. They occur in 24 of the 48 hours. p95 latency of the failing calls is 24 s, so the agent also pays 10-40 s per failed call.

### Severity

S1 — blocked: I cannot do the thing at all

### Where you saw it

API — /v1, including sign-in and tenant resolution (apps/swarm-api)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run an agent with the runner git tools against a repository whose fetch bundle is over `INLINE_BUNDLE_BYTES` (24 MiB).
2. The agent calls `git_fetch`.
3. swarm-api tries to upload the bundle to `FETCH_OBJECT` and GCS refuses.

### What you expected instead

A large fetch succeeds, or at least fails with a named refusal code instead of a bare 500.

### Identifiers

`apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/gittools.py` `FETCH_OBJECT` (`tenants/{tenant}/attempts/{attempt}/git/{call}.fetch.bundle`), `INLINE_BUNDLE_BYTES = 24 MiB`. swarm-api's conditional grants on the artifact bucket (`terraform/infra/await_input.tf`, `live.tf`) name `tenants/<t>/tasks/<task>/attempts/input-*/artifacts/` and `tenants/.../attempts/<a>/live/` only, never `tenants/<t>/attempts/<a>/git/`.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Request-log analysis: `scratchpad/analysis/api/analysis-48h.txt` (operator's session). Error text: `storage.objects.create` denied for the swarm-api identity.

### Anything else

**Needs the owner (IAM).** The two fixes are: (a) a conditional `objects.create` grant for swarm-api on `tenants/<t>/attempts/<a>/git/*.fetch.bundle` (a dev-iam row), or (b) no bucket at all: stream large fetch bundles in the response body. Either way the 500 should become a named refusal while the bundle cannot be stored. Related: #1225.

Found by the 2026-10-21 system analysis (read-only, 48 h window 2026-10-19 09:00Z to 2026-10-21 09:00Z, plus live snapshots 08:57Z-09:20Z).

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Proposal for BGD, prepared 2026-10-21T16:36Z UTC from read-only research (nothing applied).** Options, costs and the exact change follow; BGD picks one.

## Proposal: fix #1815 (a `git_fetch` over 24 MiB returns a bare 500). Read-only research, 2026-10-21

**1. Cause**

- **Where it fails.** In `apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/gittools.py`, `GitTools._fetch` has an inner `deliver()`. When a bundle is over `INLINE_BUNDLE_BYTES` (24 MiB), `deliver()` calls `GcsBundles.upload()`, which is `blob.upload_from_filename`. It writes `tenants/{t}/attempts/{a}/git/{call}.fetch.bundle` into `swarm-artifacts-saga-agents-staging`.
- **Why it needs IAM.** swarm-api has no permission that allows that create:
  - `api_reader`: objectViewer, in `terraform/modules/iam/bindings.tf`.
  - `api_history_purge_deleter`: delete under `tasks/` and `checkpoints/` only.
  - `api_input_writer`: objectCreator, limited to `attempts/input-*/artifacts/` (`terraform/infra/await_input.tf`).
  - The live project policy gives swarm-api no storage role at project level.
- **Why it shows as a bare 500.** GCS returns 403. `handle()` catches only `GitToolRefused`, `GitExecError` and `ForgeWriteError`, so Google's `Forbidden` escapes as a 500 and no audit row is written.
- **Why the agent keeps paying for it.** The worker's `ChildApi.call` marks any status of 500 or above as retryable. The agent is told "ask again" and repeats the failing call.
- **Push is not affected.** The worker uploads its own push bundle under its own prefix, and swarm-api reads it through objectViewer.
- **Correction to the issue.** The objectCreator grant in `live.tf` belongs to the live relay's Kubernetes service account, not to swarm-api.

**2. Options**

**A: one narrow IAM row (recommended)**
- role `roles/storage.objectCreator`. It can create only: no get, list or delete, so it cannot overwrite an existing object.
- member `serviceAccount:swarm-api@saga-agents-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com`
- resource: the policy of bucket `swarm-artifacts-saga-agents-staging`, never the project's
- condition title `git-fetch-bundles-only`:
```
resource.name.startsWith("projects/_/buckets/swarm-artifacts-saga-agents-staging/objects/tenants/")
&& resource.name.extract("/objects/tenants/{t}/") != ""
&& resource.name.extract("/objects/tenants/{t}/") == resource.name.extract("/objects/tenants/{t}/attempts/")
&& resource.name.extract("/attempts/{a}/") != ""
&& resource.name.extract("/attempts/{a}/") == resource.name.extract("/attempts/{a}/git/")
&& resource.name.endsWith(".fetch.bundle")
```
- **Where it goes.** A new file `terraform/infra/git_tools.tf`, holding a `google_storage_bucket_iam_member` shaped like `api_input_writer`. It names the bucket and member through `module.storage.artifact_bucket_name` and `module.iam.service_account_members["swarm-api"]`. Add `tests/terraform/git_tools_iam.tftest.hcl` with names the condition must admit and refuse. It does not belong in `terraform/bootstrap`: the role is predefined and the grant is bucket-scoped, as in `await_input.tf`.
- **Lint result.** Google's `iamPolicies:lintPolicy` returned `{}` for this expression (446 characters). As a control, a `matches()` expression returned `ConditionCompileCheck ERROR`, so the lint can fail.
- **Repo constraints it follows:**
  - Cloud Storage conditions refuse `matches()`; Google rejected it in release run 38114832799, recorded at the history-purge grant in `bindings.tf`.
  - A per-tenant `startsWith` list does not work, because `var.tenants` leaves out personal tenants created at runtime (same note).
- **Code changes:**
  - Wrap the upload so a failure becomes a named refusal with a status below 500, so the worker does not retry it.
  - Upload with `if_generation_match=0`.
- **Rejected:**
  - Unconditioned objectCreator: swarm-api could create objects in any tenant's `tasks/` artifacts and `verdicts/`, which even workers are denied.
  - Impersonating each tenant's worker service account: that needs TokenCreator on every one of them.

**B: no IAM, stream the bundle**
- Send bundles over 24 MiB in the response body as a chunked `application/x-git-bundle`, with the sha256 in a header. The worker needs a streaming read in `children.py` and `gittools.py`.
- Cloud Run caps an unstreamed HTTP/1 response at 32 MiB; a chunked response is not capped.
- Costs: a larger change in two apps, up to 256 MiB passing through swarm-api, and an amendment to `docs/runner-git-tools.md` §1.3, which says "Fetch bundles come back the same way".

**Under either option:** the named refusal is code only and can ship now, with no IAM.

**3. Tenant isolation (invariant 9)**

One swarm-api serves every tenant, so the condition cannot tie the tenant segment to the caller. Isolation therefore holds in three layers:
- **IAM fixes the path shape.** One tenant segment, then `attempts/<one segment>/git/`, ending `.fetch.bundle`. Never `tasks/`, `verdicts/`, `checkpoints/`, `repos/` or a push `.bundle`. For example, `tenants/a/b/attempts/…` is refused.
- **Code fixes the tenant.** The object key comes from `attempt.tenant_id` in the proven body, whose ID token is that tenant's own worker identity. The request never supplies it.
- **The reader is limited to its own prefix.** The worker refuses any `bundle_object` outside `tenants/<own>/attempts/` and reads with its own-prefix grant. A wrongly named key fails closed with a 403.

Option B writes nothing to the bucket.

**4. Recommendation and the row to approve**

Ship A together with the named refusal. At the `dev-iam` hold, approve only if the plan adds exactly one `google_storage_bucket_iam_member` with the role, member, bucket and condition above, and removes nothing.

**5. Not verified**

- The artifact bucket's live IAM policy: not read, because it is outside the two commands I was allowed.
- Whether a `resource.name` condition admits the create of a resumable upload (every bundle here is over 8 MiB). The `await_input` and live-relay grants use the same pattern, but I did not confirm that either is applied and used.
- Whether the 32 MiB Cloud Run limit applies on the worker's path. If it does, a 24 MiB inline bundle encodes to exactly 32 MiB before the JSON is added, so bundles just under 24 MiB may already fail. That may explain the 11 × 502; unconfirmed.
- Cleanup of fetch bundles. They carry no `custom_time`, so the bucket's `days_since_custom_time` rule never deletes them. I did not check whether the reconciler sweeps them.

title: swarm-api answered every caller 'no available instance' (429) for 96 s at 07:05:57Z on 10-21 while four new instances failed their startup probe
body:
### What happened

From 07:05:57Z to 07:07:33Z on 2026-10-21, Cloud Run answered 429 "no available instance" to every caller of swarm-api, and swarm-scheduler got the same. 4 new swarm-api instances failed their startup probe in that window. CPU was low and only 2 instances were active, so this was not load. A separate read at 09:08Z timed out on the front door (`could not reach https://swarm.saga.xyz: [Errno 60] Operation timed out`). Cause not found yet.

### Severity

S1 — blocked: I cannot do the thing at all

### Where you saw it

API — /v1, including sign-in and tenant resolution (apps/swarm-api)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

Not reproduced. Read the swarm-api request log and the Cloud Run system log for 07:05-07:08Z on 10-21.

### What you expected instead

New instances pass their startup probe, and a client can tell Cloud Run's "no available instance" 429 from the API's own `RateLimited` 429 (today both read as "you are polling too much").

### Identifiers

Service swarm-api (and swarm-scheduler), us-central1, 2026-10-21 07:05:57Z-07:07:33Z.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Cloud Run request log: 429 with Cloud Run's "no available instance" body on every route for 96 s; 4 startup-probe failures.

### Anything else

Possibly related: #1471 (one NAT IP, 655 dropped packets in 7 days). swarm-api is capped at 5 instances of 1 vCPU (`dev.tfvars:209`) and redeploys about 15 times a day straight to 100% traffic. After the isolation cutover (#1457) it becomes every worker's only state path, so an outage like this would stop work, not just the console.

Found by the 2026-10-21 system analysis (read-only, 48 h window 2026-10-19 09:00Z to 2026-10-21 09:00Z, plus live snapshots 08:57Z-09:20Z).

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Investigation, read at 09:47Z UTC 2026-10-21 (Cloud Run logs and revision settings, read-only).**

**Instance starts of swarm-api, 06:00–08:30Z** (from "Starting new instance" to the startup probe's success or failure; per instance id):
- 06:28–06:29: 3 instances, OK in 6.0–7.4 s.
- **07:03:53, 07:05:33, 07:05:42, 07:06:34: 4 instances FAILED at 96 s** ("STARTUP TCP probe failed 12 times consecutively … port 8080. The instance was not started").
- 07:06:40, 07:07:11, 07:07:23: OK, but in 61 s, 29 s and 77 s.
- 07:21–07:50: OK in 5.8–45.7 s (most 6–14 s).

**What it was not:**
- **Not a rollout.** All of these are revision `swarm-api-00378-tdf`, created 06:28:51Z, whose first instances started healthy in 6–7 s. The next revision came at 07:21Z.
- **Not load.** Requests per minute: 07:03 had 104 (24 task submissions), and 07:04–07:07 had 56–86. The real burst came at 07:12–07:13 (227 and 185 a minute, 300 submissions), and it caused no startup failures.
- **Not the NAT, for Google APIs.** The subnet has Private Google Access on.
- **Not the app's code before it listens.** The failed instances logged nothing at all between "Starting new instance" and the probe failure, only one `Connection failed with status DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` line. `create_app` makes no outbound call before it listens. That points at the container or sandbox start (image fetch, Direct VPC interface attach, or CPU), not at swarm-api.

**Why it became an outage:** only 2 instances were serving. Cloud Run's autoscaler wanted more, and every new one failed for about 4 minutes, so callers got "no available instance".

**Settings that make it fragile** (revision 00378):
- startup probe: TCP on 8080, initial delay 5 s, period 5 s, 3 s timeout, 12 failures;
- **startup CPU boost off**;
- Direct VPC egress `all-traffic` on swarm-subnet-us-central1;
- `max_instances = 5`, and (inferred) no minimum above what the autoscaler keeps.

**Candidate fixes, each for the owner** (capacity and cost; see the system review's "API capacity before the isolation cutover"):
1. Keep `min_instances` at 3, so a period of failing starts does not leave too few instances.
2. Turn on startup CPU boost.
3. Raise `max_instances`.
4. A log line at process start and at listen, so the next case separates "the container never started" from "the app started slowly".
5. If it recurs, a Cloud Run support case with the instance ids: 0010dd86074d35e8…, 0010dd86071fc249…, 0010dd8607b813b4…, 0010dd8607aae0b0….

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Proposal for BGD, prepared 2026-10-21T16:36Z UTC from read-only research (nothing applied).** Options, costs and the exact change follow; BGD picks one.

## PROPOSAL: swarm-api start failures (#1816, the swarm-api 429 "no available instance" outage on 10-21)

Read 2026-10-21 16:30Z. Source: origin/main `b3685ae0`. Only `main` was fetched, because the full fetch failed on a ref lock. Cloud Run reads covered swarm-api only and went through `redact`.

### 1. Live settings (revision `swarm-api-00384-vsd`, 100% traffic)
- **Minimum instances: 2.** Every revision since `00366-wc6` (10-20 15:36Z) has had this floor. That includes `00378-tdf`, the revision that was serving during the outage.
- **Maximum instances: 5 per revision.** There is also a service-level annotation `run.googleapis.com/maxScale: 20` that nothing in the Terraform sets.
- **CPU always allocated** (`cpu-throttling: false`).
- **Startup CPU boost off.**
- **Concurrency 80, 1 vCPU, 1 GiB, gen2, Direct VPC `all-traffic`.**
- **Startup probe:** TCP 8080, delay 5 s, period 5 s, timeout 3 s, 12 failures allowed. Liveness probe: `/healthz` every 30 s.
- **Instance starts** (10-19 16:35Z to 10-21 16:30Z, 97 in total):
  - 10-19 (partial day): 8
  - 10-20: 34 (7 rollout, 18 min-instance, 9 autoscaling)
  - 10-21 to 16:30Z: 55 (18 rollout, 14 min-instance, 23 autoscaling)
- **Startup probe results:** 92 succeeded and 5 failed. 81 succeeded within 2 attempts; 4 needed 6 to 10. A healthy instance printed its first line about 21 s after starting.

### 2. Recurrence since 07:07Z
- There was **1 more start failure**, at 15:01:49Z on `00384-vsd`. It was one of four instances started for a deploy, and it failed the same way: nothing logged between "Starting new instance" and the probe failure.
- It had no effect on callers. The other three instances were up within 22 s, and there were **0 Cloud Run 429s from 07:07:34Z to 16:31Z**. As a check, the same query returns 36 of them for 07:05 to 07:07Z.

### Two things in #1816 are wrong
- **The floor was not missing.** The investigation comment infers "no minimum", but the floor was 2. The outage began with a min-instance replacement at 07:03:53 that failed. Cloud Run then shut down warm instance `…cf2f44` anyway (uvicorn "Shutting down" at 07:05:42Z), which left one instance.
- **Not every caller was refused.** That surviving instance, `…6c2fc4`, served 57 requests in 07:05:57 to 07:07:40Z, while 36 got 429.

### 3. Options
Price basis: Cloud Run Tier 1 instance-based billing, $0.000018 per vCPU-second and $0.000002 per GiB-second. With CPU always allocated, an idle minimum instance is billed at that full rate. These prices come from CLD's training knowledge and were not fetched. At 1 vCPU and 1 GiB, one instance running all month costs about **$52.56**.

**(a) Startup CPU boost, about $1 a month** (roughly 35 to 80 starts a day, about 30 boosted vCPU-seconds each). It needs four edits:
- `terraform/modules/cloud_run/variables.tf`: `startup_cpu_boost = optional(bool, false)`
- `terraform/modules/cloud_run/main.tf:105`: `startup_cpu_boost = each.value.startup_cpu_boost`
- `terraform/infra/main.tf` (swarm-api block): `startup_cpu_boost = true`
- `tests/terraform/cloud_run.tftest.hcl:209-215`: change the assertion to "false unless the service sets it"

The module comment and that test both call boost a breach of invariant 7 (requests == limits, no bursting). As amended 10-20, invariant 7 allows CPU burst on GKE only, so this needs BGD's sign-off and probably an entry in `docs/contract-change-requests.md`.

**(b) `min_instances = 1`** at `terraform/infra/main.tf:317`, $52.56 a month. This cuts the floor from today's 2 and reverses owner decision Q6(a) (two warm swarm-api instances, 2026-10-17). Not tenable.

**(c) `min_instances = 2`** is what is live now, at about $105 a month. The doc comment from PR 1484 (ISO-IAM, two warm instances) is true. This setting was in place during the outage.

**(c′) `min_instances = 3`**, at `terraform/infra/main.tf:317`, about $158 a month (≤ $53 more). Losing one instance would still leave two.

**(d) Longer startup window, $0.** Raise `failure_threshold` from 12 to 36 at `terraform/modules/cloud_run/main.tf:144`. Instances that are slow but healthy (some took 61 to 77 s) would pass instead of being killed at 96 s.

**(e) A start-up log line, $0.** In `images/swarm-api/Dockerfile:235`, put `echo` before `exec uvicorn`. The next failure would then show whether the container ever ran.

### 4. Recommendation
- **Do (d) and (e) now.** Both are free and touch no invariant.
- **Do (a) once BGD agrees to the invariant 7 exception.** The roughly 21 s start is mostly Python startup on 1 vCPU.
- **Keep 2 instances for now; move to 3 if failures recur or before the isolation cutover (#1457, when swarm-api becomes every worker's state path).** The failed instances logged nothing at all, which points to a platform-side start problem. Boost does not fix that; only a third instance gives margin against it.

Files CLD would change: `terraform/modules/cloud_run/{main,variables}.tf`, `terraform/infra/main.tf`, `tests/terraform/cloud_run.tftest.hcl`, `images/swarm-api/Dockerfile`, and the comment in `terraform/infra/main.tf` that gives the monthly cost.

### 5. Not verified
- Why the five failed instances produced no output (image fetch, VPC interface attach or sandbox start).
- Why Cloud Run shut down `cf2f44` while its replacement was failing.
- Why one live instance still gave 429s at about 60 requests a minute.
- Which maximum applies: the service-level 20 or the revision's 5.
- Cloud Run's cap on total startup-probe time.
- Boost's exact multiplier for 1 vCPU.
- Current list prices.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body: **BGD decided 2026-10-23 (~17:37Z): turn on option (a), startup CPU boost, for swarm-api only** (~$1/month), recorded as the one exception to invariant 7 for that Cloud Run service. Lane API-CPU-BOOST is building it, with a terraform test that no other service gets the boost.

title: 21 alert policies notify nobody: the project has no notification channel because alert_emails is empty
body:
### What happened

All 21 alert policies in `saga-agents-staging` have an empty channel list, and the project has 0 notification channels, 0 uptime checks and 0 SLOs. At least 4 policies met their condition in the last 7 days, including the 42-minute GKE dispatch outage on 10-20 (19:24-20:06Z, 54 × `gke_create_job_forbidden`, 13 tasks FAILED). Nobody was told. 264 scheduler wakes were dead-lettered in two bursts, and that subscription has no consumer and no alert either.

### Severity

S1 — blocked: I cannot do the thing at all

### Where you saw it

Terraform or infrastructure (terraform)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

`gcloud alpha monitoring channels list --project saga-agents-staging` returns `[]`. `dev.tfvars:491` sets `alert_emails = []`; `modules/monitoring/alerts.tf:23` creates a channel per listed email only.

### What you expected instead

A policy that fires reaches a person, and an empty channel list is a visible error, not a silent default.

### Identifiers

`terraform/environments/dev/dev.tfvars:491`, `terraform/modules/monitoring/alerts.tf:23`.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

7-day metric totals against thresholds: dispatch-failures 61 (fires, 10-20 19:24-20:06Z); pr-stranded 520 (fires continuously); generation-fenced 270 (fires, but 215 are verify-remote's own startup fences); worker-action-ended 70 (fires).

### Anything else

**Needs the owner:** who receives alerts (email, Slack, PagerDuty) and which policies page versus record. Before adding a channel, tune the noisy ones so the channel is not muted on day one: exclude verify and smoke traffic from generation-fenced, give pr-stranded a rate and a duration. Also wanted: an uptime check on swarm.saga.xyz plus an authenticated swarm-api probe, and alerts on dead-lettered wakes, the reconciler pass time, and NAT drops.

Found by the 2026-10-21 system analysis (read-only, 48 h window 2026-10-19 09:00Z to 2026-10-21 09:00Z, plus live snapshots 08:57Z-09:20Z).

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Proposal for BGD, prepared 2026-10-21T16:36Z UTC from read-only research (nothing applied).** Options, costs and the exact change follow; BGD picks one.

## Proposal: send the 21 alert policies to a person (#1817, "alerts reach nobody")

### 1. Live state (read 2026-10-21 16:30Z, project saga-agents-staging)
I read this with `gcloud monitoring policies list` (the alpha group isn't installed, so I used the GA command) and `gcloud beta monitoring channels list`.
- There are **21 alert policies**. All are `swarm-dev-*`, all carry `managed-by=swarm-terraform` and all are enabled. None of the other team's policies appear in the listing.
- **All 21 have zero notification channels.**
- **The project has 0 notification channels** (no email, SMS, Slack or anything else) and **0 uptime checks**.
- By severity: 6 CRITICAL, 8 ERROR, 7 WARNING. Across them there are 25 conditions: 18 threshold, 1 absence, 6 log-match.
- Cause: `dev.tfvars:491` sets `alert_emails = []`, and `alerts.tf:23` only creates a channel for each listed address. `extra_notification_channels` is not set.

### 2. The policies that matter most
I did not read how often they fired: gcloud has no incidents command. The counts below are the issue's 7-day metric totals from the 2026-10-21 09:00Z analysis; I did not re-read them.
- **safety-tick-stopped** (CRITICAL): the one-minute scheduler tick has not been delivered for 10 minutes.
- **dispatch-failing-on-a-backend** (ERROR): one backend has refused every dispatch for 15 minutes. 61 failures; it fired 10-20 19:24–20:06Z during the GKE outage (13 tasks FAILED).
- **scheduler-not-draining** and **wake-messages-dead-lettered** (ERROR): the wake backlog stays above 50, or anything lands on the dead-letter subscription. The issue counts 264 dead-lettered wakes.
- **reconciler-cannot-see-a-backend** (ERROR): leases are held back because the reconciler cannot prove them dead.
- **spec-signature-invalid**, the 4 **workspace-deployer-\*** policies (CRITICAL) and **tenant-namespace-mismatch** (ERROR): isolation and IAM tripwires.
- The noisy ones:
  - **pr-stranded**: 520 events, fires continuously.
  - **generation-fencing**: 270 events, of which 215 are verify-remote's own startup fences.
  - **worker-action-ended**: 70 events.

### 3. Options

**These apply to every option:**
- **IAM:** none. Only `google_monitoring_*` resources change, and `scripts/lib/iam-plan.jq` does not classify those as IAM, so they apply on merge with no dev-iam hold. The CI deployer already holds `roles/monitoring.editor` (`terraform/bootstrap/variables.tf:287`).
- **Cost:** alerting is billed per condition plus points returned, not per notification. The 25 conditions cost the same with or without channels: about $2.50–$8.75 a month at the $0.10–$0.35 per condition per month that Google's pages give. Neither page I read lists a charge for notifications.
- **Personal data:** the repository is public, so an address in `dev.tfvars` is published. The safer route is for BGD to create each channel in the console and for CLD to commit only its ID in `extra_notification_channels`.
  - Setting `TF_VAR_alert_emails` instead does not work: the `-var-file` line overrides it, and any plan run without that variable would delete the channel.
- **Guard:** a `precondition` on `service_errors` would fail the plan when `create_alerts` is true and the channel list is empty. It has to land in the same PR as the first channel ID, or the release plan goes red.

**(a) One email channel for all 21 policies.**
```hcl
extra_notification_channels = ["projects/saga-agents-staging/notificationChannels/<ID>"]
```
- BGD adds an Email channel under Console > Alerting > notification channels and clicks "Send test".
- Email channels have no verification step (docs read today).
- Risk: untuned, pr-stranded alone floods the inbox.

**(b) Severity split.**
- These 14 go to the urgent channel plus email: safety-tick-stopped, spec-signature-invalid, workspace-deployer-{outside-personal-workers, foreign-runtime, front-door-iam, tenant-secret-iam}, control-plane-5xx, dispatch-failing-on-a-backend, reconciler-cannot-see-a-backend, scheduler-not-draining, wake-messages-dead-lettered, tenant-namespace-mismatch, workspace-job-or-dispatch-changed, workspace-job-run-by-another-caller.
- These 7 WARNINGs go to email only: generation-fencing, job-executions-failing, pr-stranded, schedule-needs-attention, tasks-dead-lettered, worker-action-ended, workspace-stuck.
```hcl
variable "urgent_notification_channels" { type = list(string), default = [] }
locals { channels_by_severity = {
  CRITICAL = concat(local.notification_channels, var.urgent_notification_channels)
  ERROR    = concat(local.notification_channels, var.urgent_notification_channels)
  WARNING  = local.notification_channels } }
```
- The urgent channel would be a Cloud console mobile-app push or SMS. SMS needs a verification code, and the phone number never goes in the repo.
- BGD creates both channels; CLD commits their IDs.

**(c) Slack.**
- BGD, as a Slack workspace admin, adds a Slack channel in the console and clicks Allow for "Google Cloud Monitoring". A private Slack channel also needs `/invite @Google Cloud Monitoring`.
- CLD then commits the channel's ID in either list.
- It is not created as a Terraform resource: the Slack type needs `sensitive_labels.auth_token`, which would land in Terraform state, against the repo rule "no secret material in Terraform".

### 4. Recommendation: (b), with email for everything and Slack or mobile push as the urgent channel
- The 10-20 outage was an ERROR-severity alert. At current rates the 7 WARNINGs would bury it in a single inbox.
- In the same PR:
  - pr-stranded gets a `duration` (for example 3600s) and a rate threshold;
  - generation-fencing excludes the verify and smoke `metric.label.tenant_id` values;
  - the empty-channel precondition is added.

Files CLD would change:
- `terraform/modules/monitoring/variables.tf`, `alerts.tf`, `stranded_prs.tf`, `tenant_namespace.tf` and `workspace_alerts.tf`
- `terraform/infra/variables.tf` and `main.tf`
- `terraform/environments/dev/dev.tfvars:491`
- `tests/terraform/observability.tftest.hcl`
- `docs/operations.md`

### 5. Not verified
- Incident history, and the 7-day counts (both are the issue's).
- Whether alerting billing is live, and the current rate: Google's two pages disagree.
- That `roles/monitoring.editor` includes `notificationChannels.create`. I did not re-read the role's permission list.
- The issue says dead-lettered wakes have no alert, but the live policy wake-messages-dead-lettered watches `swarm-scheduler-wake-dlq-sub`. I did not read whether that subscription exists, because Pub/Sub is outside the reads I was allowed.
- Whether SMS is available for BGD's number.
- The issue's other requests (an uptime check, reconciler pass-time alerts, NAT-drop alerts) are not covered here.

title: The live Firestore database has no backup and no delete protection, and the DR doc gives its recovery point as an export that was never taken
body:
### What happened

Firestore `swarm` (the live product's database) has point-in-time recovery for 7 days, but delete protection is OFF, `gcloud firestore backups schedules list` returns `[]`, and `gs://swarm-artifacts-saga-agents-staging/backups/` does not exist. `docs/disaster-recovery.md` §1 gives Firestore's recovery point as "last export" and never mentions point-in-time recovery. Point-in-time versions go with the database if it is deleted.

### Severity

S1 — blocked: I cannot do the thing at all

### Where you saw it

Terraform or infrastructure (terraform)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

Read the database's settings and backup schedules with gcloud; read `docs/disaster-recovery.md` §1.

### What you expected instead

A deleted or corrupted `swarm` database can be restored to a known point, and the DR doc states the recovery point that really exists.

### Identifiers

`terraform/infra/main.tf:132` (`deletion_policy = "ABANDON"`, protects only against terraform destroy); `dev.tfvars:13` (`deletion_protection = false`, "Dev may be torn down and rebuilt"), which `delete_protection` follows.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Dev is production: `prod` has never been deployed (no `infra/prod` state) and `prod.tfvars` sets 31 of dev's 70 variables.

### Anything else

**Needs the owner:** turning on delete protection for the live database, and a backup schedule (for example daily kept 7 days, weekly kept 14 weeks), which costs a little storage. A restore drill must go to a new database id, never `swarm`. The DR doc correction is mechanical and goes in the 2026-10-21 analysis epic.

Found by the 2026-10-21 system analysis (read-only, 48 h window 2026-10-19 09:00Z to 2026-10-21 09:00Z, plus live snapshots 08:57Z-09:20Z).

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Proposal for BGD, prepared 2026-10-21T16:36Z UTC from read-only research (nothing applied).** Options, costs and the exact change follow; BGD picks one.

## #1818 — Firestore `swarm` has no backup and no delete protection: proposal

### 1. Live state, read 2026-10-21 16:30Z (09:30 PDT)

Read with `gcloud firestore databases describe --database=swarm` and `gcloud firestore backups schedules list --database=swarm`.

| | live |
|---|---|
| Point-in-time recovery | **ON**, `versionRetentionPeriod: 604800s` (7 days), earliest version 2026-10-14T16:30Z |
| Delete protection | **OFF** (`DELETE_PROTECTION_DISABLED`) |
| Backup schedules | **none** (`[]`) |
| Location / edition | `us-central1`, FIRESTORE_NATIVE, STANDARD, `freeTier: true` |
| Stored size | **not read.** `describe` has no size field. Size is a Cloud Monitoring metric, and this brief allowed only gcloud Firestore reads. |

The DR doc correction has already merged (PR 1827, DOCS-TRUTH). `docs/disaster-recovery.md` §1 now says "7 days of point-in-time recovery; total loss if deleted".

### 2. Terraform today

* The database is `google_firestore_database.this` in `terraform/modules/firestore/main.tf`.
* It is called from `terraform/infra/main.tf` `module "firestore"` with `delete_protection = var.deletion_protection` and `deletion_policy = "ABANDON"`. `dev.tfvars` sets `deletion_protection = false`.
* Point-in-time recovery is on by the module's default.
* There is no `google_firestore_backup_schedule` anywhere. The pinned google provider is 6.50.0, which has that resource.
* **Terraform-managed, inferred rather than read from state.** Every release applies `terraform/infra`, and the last one succeeded today at 14:06Z. If `swarm` were not in state, that apply would fail trying to create it.
* `var.deletion_protection` also governs the GKE cluster and about 15 Cloud Run services. Flipping it in dev would change all of them, so the plan below adds a separate variable.

### 3. Options

**Pricing basis.** These prices come from CLD's memory (knowledge cutoff June 2026). They are not fetched: the pricing page returned no tables.
* Backup storage: about $0.03/GiB-month.
* Point-in-time recovery storage: about $0.18/GiB-month. It is already being paid.
* Restore: about $0.20/GiB, charged once per restore.

The Firebase pricing doc (fetched) says a backup's size equals the database's size when the backup was taken. Size was not read, so the table uses 1 GiB and 10 GiB. The ceiling column prices backups at $0.18.

| | change | added per month, 1 GiB / 10 GiB | ceiling |
|---|---|---|---|
| (a) | delete protection on; point-in-time recovery stays on | $0 / $0 | $0 |
| (b) | (a) + daily backup, kept 7 days | $0.21 / $2.10 | $1.26 / $12.60 |
| (c) | (b) + weekly backup, kept 14 weeks | $0.63 / $6.30 | $3.78 / $37.80 |

**The Terraform change, in the `terraform/infra` root, not bootstrap.** A schedule is a child of the database that the infra root owns; bootstrap is the IAM root.

* (a): in `terraform/infra/main.tf`, `delete_protection = var.firestore_delete_protection`, a new variable defaulting to `true`. This is an in-place update. `ABANDON` means `make destroy` still leaves the database alone.
* (b): a new `terraform/modules/firestore/backups.tf`:
  ```hcl
  resource "google_firestore_backup_schedule" "daily" {
    project   = var.project_id
    database  = google_firestore_database.this.name
    retention = "604800s"
    daily_recurrence {}
  }
  ```
* (c): add a `weekly` schedule with `retention = "8467200s"` (14 weeks, the maximum) and `weekly_recurrence { day = "SUNDAY" }`.

**IAM: none in any option.** The deployer already holds `roles/datastore.owner` on `swarm`. The plan is non-IAM, so it ships through the release without the `dev-iam` hold. **Merging the PR is the approval.**

**What each option protects:**
* (a) stops an accidental console or `gcloud` delete. Anyone with `datastore.databases.update` can still turn protection off first, and point-in-time versions still die with the database.
* (b) survives a deleted database. The Firestore backups doc says: "Deleting the source database does not automatically delete related backups." After a deletion, at most 24 h of data is lost.
* (c) also recovers corruption noticed up to 14 weeks late. It has a cost beyond money: an offboarded tenant's records stay in the weekly backups for up to 14 weeks. That cuts against BGD's 2026-09-24 offboarding decision ("everything the tenant left is deleted"). Tenant workers cannot restore a backup, but the copies exist.

**Restore, in one paragraph.** A restore never writes into `swarm`. `gcloud firestore databases restore --source-backup=projects/saga-agents-staging/locations/us-central1/backups/<id> --destination-database=swarm-restore-<stamp>` creates a NEW database in `us-central1` holding the data as of that backup. The point-in-time path is the one in DR §4: export at `--snapshot-time`, then import into a new id. Either way, read the new database first. Making it live means importing it into `module.firestore` state and changing `firestore_database`, and nobody has drilled that.

### 4. Recommendation: (b)

* It closes the total-loss case for pennies.
* It needs no IAM change.
* Its 7-day window matches the point-in-time recovery window that already exists, so offboarded data stays no longer than it does today.

Take (c) only if BGD accepts that offboarded tenants' data stays in backups for up to 14 weeks.

**What CLD would build after approval, as one lane, tests pushed red first:**
* `terraform/modules/firestore/backups.tf` (new) and `variables.tf`: retention variables, validated at 8467200s or less.
* `terraform/infra/main.tf` and `variables.tf`: `firestore_delete_protection` and the retention values. `dev.tfvars` stays as it is.
* `scripts/lib/unlabelable-types.json`: add `google_firestore_backup_schedule`, which has no labels attribute.
* `tests/terraform/firestore.tftest.hcl`: a schedule exists on `swarm` and none on `swarm-bench`; protection is on.
* `docs/disaster-recovery.md`: update §1, and add to §4 a "Restore from a scheduled backup" section and a "Restore drill" section.
* `tests/unit/scripts/test_docs_system_truth.py`: it currently asserts "delete protection is off" and dev's `deletion_protection = false`, so those assertions must change.
* `docs/runbooks/tenant-offboarding.md`: add backups to its list of what survives.

After the release, CLD would:
1. Re-read `describe` and the schedule list.
2. The next day, run `gcloud firestore backups list --location=us-central1`.
3. Run a drill restore into `swarm-restore-drill-<date>`, then delete it. This creates a database and bills a restore, so it needs BGD's separate approval.

### 5. Not verified

* Stored size, so every dollar figure is a formula.
* All prices (memory, not fetched).
* That the deployer's conditioned `datastore.owner` lets a backup-schedule create through. Its behaviour on non-database resource types was never measured; it is built to fail open.
* Whether a restore carries indexes and TTL policies with it.
* That the database is in Terraform state (inferred from green releases).

title: The quota broker's secret-version retention has never run: it compares the project number Secret Manager returns with the project id
body:
### What happened

88 ERRORs in 48 h read "a version listed under one secret names another, so nothing was expired", across all 10 `swarm-account-eng--*` secrets. `swarm-account-eng--devops-main` has 132 versions, all ENABLED, and so does its `-refresh` secret; each gains 4-5 versions a day. About 1,300 versions are enabled in all, roughly $80 a month and growing, and every superseded OAuth credential stays readable.

### Severity

S2 — wrong data on screen or in the API (states, counts, capacity, costs, timings) — I can't trust what it says

### Where you saw it

Quota broker (apps/quota-broker)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

List the versions of `swarm-account-eng--devops-main` (metadata only). Version names come back as `projects/209012342332/secrets/...`, with the project NUMBER.

### What you expected instead

Old versions are disabled, then destroyed after a grace period, keeping the newest few.

### Identifiers

`apps/quota-broker/quota_broker/secretstore.py:460` compares that number with the project id, so `_destroy_stale_versions` returns before expiring anything.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Quota-broker log: `a version listed under one secret names another, so nothing was expired` (88 in 48 h).

### Anything else

**Needs the owner (secrets):** the code fix is one comparison, but once deployed it starts disabling and destroying about 1,300 credential versions, which cannot be undone. The owner decides how many to keep (the analysis suggests 3), the grace before destroy (7 days), and whether the first run is a dry run that only lists. Belongs with epic #476.
