title: A platform-side dispatch refusal spends a task's attempts and fails it within about two minutes instead of parking it
body:
### What happened

On 2026-10-20 19:24-20:06Z the cluster's admission policy `swarm-worker-job-constraints` refused every CPU-burst Job ("requests must equal limits") because the scheduler shipped #1689's sizes before the policy allowed them (PR 1747 later corrected that). 54-56 dispatches failed with `gke_create_job_forbidden`, and 11-13 tasks ended FAILED `dispatch_failed`, each within about 2 minutes. 3 merge tasks used 10 of 10 attempts. The same path applies to a Job-quota 403 ("exceeded quota"): each tenant namespace allows 200 Jobs and finished Jobs stay for an hour, eng peaked at 119 Jobs in a rolling hour, and the 201st Job would fail tasks instead of queueing them.

### Severity

S2 — wrong data on screen or in the API (states, counts, capacity, costs, timings) — I can't trust what it says

### Where you saw it

Scheduler — admission and dispatch (apps/scheduler)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

Any 403 on GKE Job create: `dispatch.py` `_is_forbidden` maps every 403 to `gke_create_job_forbidden`, then `return_to_ready_after_failed_dispatch` (`apps/scheduler/scheduler/store.py`) retries on a fixed `now + 30s` and fails the task at `max_attempts`.

### What you expected instead

A refusal that is the platform's (admission policy, quota) parks the task with a reason, without spending an attempt, and raises an alert. Transient errors back off exponentially. A refusal that persists ends the task with the precise code after a bounded park count.

### Identifiers

`apps/scheduler/scheduler/dispatch.py` `_is_forbidden`, `apps/scheduler/scheduler/loop.py` (the failed-dispatch path), `apps/scheduler/scheduler/store.py` `return_to_ready_after_failed_dispatch`. Example task: `task_1cdb7e05…` created 19:56:00Z, FAILED 19:58:05Z after 3 attempts.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Scheduler log: 54 × `dispatch failed … gke_create_job_forbidden` with the ValidatingAdmissionPolicy denial text.

### Anything else

**Needs the owner (contract):** a new park reason is a frozen-contract change (`swarm_common` ParkReason), so it needs a contract request in `docs/contract-change-requests.md`. Also proposed: a release preflight that server-side dry-runs one rendered Job per GKE profile in each tenant namespace before the new scheduler revision takes traffic, and a shorter Job TTL (3600 s to about 600 s) to raise the per-tenant Job ceiling. #1590 is a different 403 (missing namespace).

Found by the 2026-10-21 system analysis (read-only, 48 h window 2026-10-19 09:00Z to 2026-10-21 09:00Z, plus live snapshots 08:57Z-09:20Z).

title: One in five ci-fix rounds loses its fix to a rejected push onto a PR branch that moved
body:
### What happened

Of 69 ci-fix tasks in 48 h, 14 (20%) FAILED with `publish_failed: push failed … Updates were rejected because the remote contains work`. The fix survives only as `swarm-work.patch` in GCS and is hand-recovered or lost.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Worker on Cloud Run (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-base)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

A ci-fix clones the PR branch; something else (another fix round, the merge step's branch update, or a conflict-fix) moves the branch before the fix pushes; `push_branch` never forces and raises `PushRejected`.

### What you expected instead

The fix lands on the moved branch (rebase its single commit onto the new tip, re-run the leak scan, authorship check and fence check, push again, never forced), or fix rounds on one PR are serialised so the branch cannot move under them.

### Identifiers

`apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/gitops.py` `push_branch` (non-fast-forward raises `PushRejected`), `own_branch_tip` covers the task's own `swarm/<task>` branch only (#1438).

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Worker logs: 14 × `Updates were rejected because the remote contains work` on ci-fix tasks.

### Anything else

**Needs the owner:** which of the two designs (rebase-and-retry in the worker, or serialise fix rounds per PR in the scheduler). Which actor moved the branch was not traced. The worker runs on GKE for claude-code; the form has no plain GKE worker entry.

Found by the 2026-10-21 system analysis (read-only, 48 h window 2026-10-19 09:00Z to 2026-10-21 09:00Z, plus live snapshots 08:57Z-09:20Z).

title: oracle-api@ is on the shared deny-list and is also a platform principal (service tenant, IAP member, ALLOWED_USERS)
body:
### What happened

DENY-LIST-REFRESH (PR 1834, epic #1822) added `oracle-api@saga-agents-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com` to `SHARED_DENY_LIST`, as its brief listed. The same account is also a principal of this platform:
- the service tenant `u-or-9a0792` (`terraform/environments/dev/dev.tfvars`);
- `frontend_iap_members` (`terraform/bootstrap/terraform.tfvars`);
- `ALLOWED_USERS` (`terraform/infra/locals.tf`).

Today no guard trips. The infra plan guard reads `member`, `name` and `email` fields; `ALLOWED_USERS` is an environment value; the tenant principal is a Firestore field; and the bootstrap root, where the IAP binding lives, is not run through `plan-guard.sh`. But a future infra-root `*_iam_member` naming this account would be STOPPED by the plan guard.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Scripts or make targets (scripts, Makefile)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

Write an infra-root IAM member resource naming `oracle-api@…` and run the plan guard: it refuses it as a shared resource.

### What you expected instead

A deliberate choice between two treatments:
- **(a) Keep it on the list** (the lane's recommendation). The account belongs to the Oracle team, and this platform only names it as a member. Any future grant to it through the infra root then needs the guard's override.
- **(b) Remove it**, treating it as a client of the platform rather than another team's resource.

### Identifiers

PR 1834; `scripts/lib/common.sh` `SHARED_DENY_LIST`; the lane's question in task_1c6e8ed4a7224ea9b7ed questions.json.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

None; this is a design question raised by the lane.

### Anything else

**Parked for the owner** under the overnight rules (IAM and tenancy). PR 1834 was left to merge with the account ON the list, because that fails safe (a guard refuses; nothing is granted or removed), and it also protects 11 other resources of other teams tonight. Removing it is a one-line change if the owner chooses (b).

title: swarm-graph's answer p95 on this repository rose from 64-68 ms to 152-165 ms in five days, and nothing measures the 300 ms target once PR 1838 merges
body:
### What happened

swarm-graph's answer latency on this repository grows with the repository. It was measured on 2026-10-21 by lane FLAKE-FIX (PR 1838) in a 6-core SwarmCloud container, with the server held at b12bc65 and only the data changing:

| tree | symbols | answer p95 | ratio to reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10-16 (cb67509) | 49,058 | 64-68 ms | 2.08-2.18 |
| 2026-10-21 | 58,930 | 152-165 ms | 4.52-5.32 |

The slowest answers are cold `context` calls on large test modules, for example `tests/unit/control_plane/conftest.py#auth_header` at 330-357 ms. Cold `context` decodes whole per-module shards, so latency grows with the module.

PR 1838 moves the CI p95 gate (`test_graphmcp_budgets`, which reached main red at 10.7-11.4x the reference) onto a generated workload of fixed size. That stops the flake, but after it nothing measures the KG4 design target any more: answer p95 under 300 ms on THIS repository.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Not sure

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

Run the graphmcp answer battery on main's snapshot of this repository and on the 2026-10-16 snapshot, with the same server code.

### What you expected instead

The answer p95 stays under the 300 ms design target as the repository grows, and something notices before it does not.

### Identifiers

PR 1838 (FLAKE-FIX, part of #1822); its question in task_957f1506877240fdbe3a questions.json; `graphmcp/snapshot.py`, `repo_graph_shards.py`.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

The numbers above are from the lane's measurement.

### Anything else

**Needs the owner:** which of the lane's three answers, or more than one:
1. **Accept the generated-workload gate as it is.** This repository's own p95 is then measured nowhere.
2. **Add a scheduled report-only measurement on main's snapshot**, opening an issue when p95 nears 300 ms (the lane's recommendation). It is a new recurring CI job, and needs a workflow change pushed by the operator. The 2026-10-21 analysis found GitHub fires only 2-6% of this repository's frequent cron schedules, so it may need Cloud Scheduler instead.
3. **Fix the growth in the product:** split or cap the per-module shards that cold `context` decodes.

At today's rate, the unloaded p95 crosses 300 ms within weeks.

title: The worker's prepublish typecheck fails on every Next.js repository because it runs tsc without generating Next's route types first
body:
### What happened

The prepublish check runs `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` on a clean checkout. Next.js generates `PageProps`/`LayoutProps` only during `next build` or `next typegen`, so the check fails with 17 errors in files the lane never touched. Lanes a1, a2, a4, d5, d11 and fix-222 each spent a turn explaining "not my files". c2 and two fix lanes added out-of-scope workarounds (retyping 10 route files) that later had to be dropped or conflicted.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Worker on Cloud Run (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-base)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

Run a claude-code lane on a Next.js repository whose `package.json` `typecheck` script is not a plain `tsc ...` (for example `next typegen && tsc --noEmit`).

### What you expected instead

The prepublish typecheck matches what the repository itself runs: it generates Next's types first, or runs the repository's own typecheck script.

### Identifiers

`apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/prepublish.py` `_typecheck_args()`: it uses the package's `typecheck` script only when that is a plain `tsc ...` with no `&&`/`||`/`;`/`|`, else falls back to `--noEmit -p tsconfig.json`, so `next typegen && tsc --noEmit` falls back and skips typegen.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

17 tsc errors on `PageProps`/`LayoutProps` in untouched route files.

### Anything else

Mechanical fix, lane PREPUB-NEXT-TYPEGEN: when the package depends on `next` (or its typecheck script runs `next typegen`), run `next typegen` in the package before tsc. A repository-declared typecheck command is the larger option the peer also suggested, left for the owner.

title: The bridge refuses a swarm_follow format that arrives JSON-quoted ('"progress"'), so a step row ends UNKNOWN while its task finishes
body:
### What happened

A `/sc:swarmcloud` step row ended UNKNOWN although its task finished normally. The bridge refused the row's `swarm_follow` call with: unknown format '"progress"'; swarm_follow takes json, lines or progress. The value the bridge received was the JSON-quoted string `"progress"` (quotes included), not `progress`. The row agent (`plugin/agents/step.md`) is told to pass `format: "progress"` and to stop with UNKNOWN on any format error, so one mis-quoted argument cost the row. The other two rows of the same run reported fine.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Claude Code plugin or MCP bridge — /sc and the swarm_* tools (plugin, apps/swarm-mcp)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

Call `swarm_follow` with `format` set to a string that carries its own quotes, `"\"progress\""` (what a row agent sends when it JSON-encodes the value twice). The bridge refuses it before following.

### What you expected instead

The bridge accepts `"progress"`, `'progress'` and ` progress ` as `progress`: it normalises the value at the boundary (trims whitespace and one layer of matching quotes) before it validates, and uses the normalised value everywhere after. A value that is still not one of json, lines, progress or summary after that is refused as now, and the error shows the value it received.

### Identifiers

wf_647d11a5f7d1492b9b5c, step review-226, task task_2eb872b0d769446d9dac; plugin sc 0.5.45; the attach run wf_24a475cd-a28 in the Product Oracle session. The check is `apps/swarm-mcp/swarm_mcp/server.py`, the `name == "swarm_follow"` format guard (about line 4552 on main at 2026-10-21 12:25Z), and the reads of `args["format"]` after it.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

unknown format '"progress"'; swarm_follow takes json, lines or progress

### Anything else

Main's message now also lists `summary`; the refusal itself is unchanged. Mechanical fix, lane SC-FOLLOW-FORMAT.

title: A laptop plan of main destroys the GitHub push receiver, because the applied image_refs it pins have no swarm-github-hooks digest
body:
### What happened

A laptop `scripts/plan.sh` (dev, main at 02c20150, 2026-10-21 ~16:00Z) plans to DESTROY the GitHub push receiver: `google_cloud_run_v2_service.github_hooks[0]` and `google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member.github_hooks_public[0]`. `plan.sh` pins the digests in state's `image_refs` output (`scripts/lib/image-refs.sh --applied`). That output lists agent-runtime-base, agent-runtime-browser, agent-runtime-indexer, swarm-api, swarm-live, swarm-quota-broker, swarm-reconciler, swarm-scheduler, swarm-ui and swarm-verify. It has no `swarm-github-hooks`, so `local.github_hooks_serving` (`terraform/infra/github_hooks.tf:100`, `lookup(var.image_refs, "swarm-github-hooks", "") != ""`) reads false and the receiver's `count` drops to 0. A release plans with the promotion manifest's full digest set, so releases keep it. The control: the same plan with and without PR 1877's one-line change shows the same two destroys, so they are not that PR's.

### Severity

S2 — wrong data on screen or in the API (states, counts, capacity, costs, timings) — I can't trust what it says

### Where you saw it

Release pipeline or CI (.github/workflows)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

From a checkout of main with `.env` for dev: `make tf-init`, then `scripts/plan.sh`. The plan ends `0 to add, 7 to change, 2 to destroy`, and the two destroys are the push receiver and its public invoker.

### What you expected instead

A laptop plan of main shows no image-driven destroys. `image-refs.sh --applied` returns a digest for every image terraform deploys, the receiver included. Or `plan.sh` refuses to plan when the applied refs lack an image a resource needs, instead of planning that resource away. `make tf-plan && make tf-apply` would otherwise take the push receiver down.

### Identifiers

title: A no-account park waits for a 7-day window ~46 h out and is not re-checked when an account frees up
body:
### What happened

On 2026-10-21, QAFIX3-OVERVIEW-B's implement step (task_1c8fc70bf26242328572, wf_10712ab44d1d42d1aa04, submitted 16:08Z) parked at `park_phase: account_assign` with `PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` and `account_pool_reason: no_account_available`. Its `waiting` read "Provider quota exhausted on anthropic; until 2026-10-23 14:00Z", `next_check_at` 2026-10-23T14:00:00Z, about 46 h later.

Accounts had room long before that:
- At 17:01Z, FS-BACKUPS' implement step (task_1fc85b8f11c84073abe1) was assigned an account and ran.
- The pool read at about 17:00Z showed eng:devops-team at 0% for both 5h and 7d, eng:devops-main "cleared", and eng:aieng-claude1 at 9% for 5h. All five accounts were `available`.

The parked step was still waiting at 18:56Z, when it was cancelled and resubmitted. The resubmission was DISPATCHED at once. The owner noticed it as a merge step "waiting while CI is not busy".

### Severity

S2 — wrong data on screen or in the API (states, counts, capacity, costs, timings) — I can't trust what it says

### Where you saw it

Quota broker (apps/quota-broker)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

Not reproduced on purpose. The shape: submit a claude-code step while every eng account is momentarily unable to take a new agent. The step parks at account_assign with a `next_reset_at` that is a 7-day window's clear, about 46 h out, and it is not re-checked when an account frees up sooner.

### What you expected instead

A no-account park resumes as soon as any candidate account can take the agent. That is what `quota_broker/main.py`'s assign docstring promises ("resumes by itself the moment an account frees up"). The park's instant is the EARLIEST time any candidate could become eligible: a 5-hour window, a concurrency slot freed by another agent finishing, or a fresh usage reading. It is never the latest 7-day clear. A released assignment wakes quota-parked tasks instead of leaving them to a far `next_check_at`.

### Identifiers

task_1c8fc70bf26242328572 (parked; cancelled 18:56Z), wf_10712ab44d1d42d1aa04, resubmitted as wf_fdc0c924a7964187a6b7. Code: `apps/quota-broker/quota_broker/main.py` account assign (`choose` / `eligibility` → `next_reset_at`), `quota_broker/accounts.py` `eligibility`, and the scheduler or worker path that turns `next_reset_at` into the park's `next_check_at`.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

    waiting_line: Provider quota exhausted on anthropic; until 2026-10-23 14:00Z
    blocked_by: park_phase account_assign, account_pool_reason no_account_available, provider anthropic

### Anything else

Lane QUOTA-PARK-RECHECK finds the cause and fixes it (owner, 2026-10-21). It holds no capacity while parked (invariant 1 holds); the cost is a lane silently losing two days.

title: swarm-images grows about 125 GB a day: every build is tagged and only untagged images are ever cleaned
body:
### What happened

Artifact Registry `swarm-images` (saga-agents-staging, us-central1) held **2,096 GB** on 2026-10-21 16:10Z: 12,850 digests carrying 17,214 tags. Over the last 7 days it grew by about 1,030 digests and about 125 GB of real storage a day. Its cleanup policies (`terraform/modules/artifact_registry/main.tf`) delete only UNTAGGED images older than 7 days and keep the newest 20 per package. Every build is tagged with its commit SHA, so tagged images are never deleted:
- 9,187 digests carry only a commit-SHA tag and were never promoted, about 2.8 TB logical;
- 1,834 carry a `dev-promoted-*` mark.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Release pipeline or CI (.github/workflows)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

`gcloud artifacts repositories describe swarm-images --location us-central1 --project saga-agents-staging` (Repository Size), and `gcloud artifacts docker images list .../swarm-images --include-tags` grouped by tag shape and age.

### What you expected instead

The registry keeps what a release, a rollback or a CI reuse can read: `:dev`, `:prod`, promoted images for as long as their manifests live (30 days), the owner-pinned workspace-apply digest, and the newest 20 per package. It deletes other tagged images after 14 days, so storage levels off (about 2.5 TB at last week's build rate) instead of adding about $12.50 a month every day. At about $0.10 per GB-month (from memory, not billing), today's storage is roughly $210 a month.

### Identifiers

`terraform/modules/artifact_registry/main.tf` cleanup_policies; `scripts/lib/common.sh` `promotion_mark_prefix`; `scripts/push-images.sh` MARK; `scripts/lib/deploy.sh`.

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

    Repository Size: 2095931.089MB

### Anything else

Owner approved the plan 2026-10-21, in two lanes:
- **REGISTRY-MARKS:** rename the mark to `promoted-<channel>-<tag>` so the channel tags can be kept with no age limit, and a one-off re-mark script.
- **REGISTRY-CLEANUP:** the policies in dry-run.

Nothing is deleted until the owner reads the would-delete list.

Seven misnamed one-version packages (`agent-runtime-baseb885502568e`… from 09-16) are kept forever by keep-recent and need a one-off delete, which is also the owner's call.

title: The Jobs swarm-scheduler creates for self-service tenants have no VPC egress, so a switched worker's state/open is refused at swarm-api's ingress
body:
### What happened

The Cloud Run Jobs swarm-scheduler creates for a tenant that Terraform does not know carry no `vpc_access`. That is every self-service `u-<email>` tenant. The Job builder in `apps/scheduler/scheduler/dispatch.py` (the `run_v2.Job(...)` it returns, labels `managed-by: swarm-scheduler`) sets containers, volumes, timeout, service account and execution environment, and no VPC. Terraform's Jobs (`terraform/modules/cloud_run_jobs/main.tf` `vpc_access`) set `egress = "ALL_TRAFFIC"` on `swarm-vpc` / `swarm-subnet-us-central1` with tag `swarm-worker`.

Read 2026-10-21 21:25Z:
- `gcloud run jobs describe swarm-job-u-bogdan-mock` has no network interfaces and no egress annotation, and its creator is `swarm-scheduler@`.
- `swarm-job-eng-mock` has `run.googleapis.com/vpc-access-egress: all-traffic` and the `swarm-worker` tag.

Three consequences:
1. **Isolation cutover a1 (#1457) cannot work for these tenants on Cloud Run.** A switched worker calls swarm-api at its `run.app` URL from the public internet, and swarm-api's ingress `internal-and-cloud-load-balancing` answers 404 before the app sees the request. All three u-bogdan evidence agents exited 1 at `state/open` with `StateRefused ... (404 http_404)`, over three generations each (21:20-21:24Z). The same tenant's GKE indexer attempts passed 196 state calls, all 200. The control is the same tenant, the same switch and the same release: the only difference is the backend.
2. **The provider allow-list does not apply.** Their provider calls do not leave through the swarm Cloud NAT, so they do not carry the reserved addresses a provider allow-lists (the module's own comment gives this as the reason for ALL_TRAFFIC).
3. **Child tasks are out of reach.** A child task, or any other swarm-api call from such a worker, fails the same way while `enable_child_tasks = true`.

### Severity

S1 — blocked: I cannot do the thing at all

### Where you saw it

Scheduler — admission and dispatch (apps/scheduler)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. List a self-service tenant in `state_via_api_tenants` and release (done for u-bogdan in PR 1877).
2. Dispatch a `mock` task in that tenant (a Cloud Run profile).
3. The execution exits 1 at `state/open` with a 404, and swarm-api logs no request.

### What you expected instead

A Job the scheduler creates is built like a Terraform-made worker Job: Direct VPC egress `ALL_TRAFFIC` on the swarm network and subnetwork, tagged `swarm-worker`. The scheduler also brings the Jobs it already created up to that template, as `_refresh_image` does for their image. Then a switched worker reaches swarm-api from inside the VPC, its provider calls carry the NAT addresses, and the worker-ingress firewall rule can name it.

### Identifiers

- Code: `apps/scheduler/scheduler/dispatch.py` (the tenant Job builder and `_refresh_image`) and `terraform/modules/cloud_run_jobs/main.tf` `vpc_access`.
- Jobs: `swarm-job-u-bogdan-mock` (no VPC) and `swarm-job-eng-mock` (VPC).
- Tasks: task_1271b8e022ca4023922e, task_be20957bcc024b66b31e, task_8dd60579530e43d8ac77 (cancelled 21:27Z).
- Rollback: PR 1892 (draft).

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

    agent_worker.statecall.StateRefused: swarm-api refused the state call (404 http_404):
    reconciled: execution swarm-job-u-bogdan-mock-wksj8 exited 1 before its runner started (task was DISPATCHED); not counted (1/3); retrying

### Anything else

The fix very likely needs an IAM change. `swarmJobDispatcher` holds only `run.*` permissions, and attaching a Job to a subnet needs a compute subnetwork permission for the principal that creates it. The exact permission is not yet verified against Cloud Run's Direct VPC documentation. Not verified here either: whether a Job updated in place keeps a running execution's environment.

title: Questions a lane's agent asks the owner never reach the Claude Code session: the plugin drops them and /sc check never lists them
body:
### What happened

A lane's agent asks the owner questions (its `questions.json`), but the questions never reach the Claude Code session that launched the lane, so the owner never sees them there. The owner found one only by opening the console: task_dccf3e5fc5dd4a0b8cdf (QUOTA-PARK-RECHECK, #1885), whose question about waking no-account parks on a hold release went unanswered while its PR merged.

A sweep read at 2026-10-22T01:00Z found:
- 31 unanswered questions from 17 tasks submitted under one Claude Code session tag (2026-10-21 10:12Z onward);
- 5 more under this session's tag, including two from lanes running now: QAFIX4-PAGEHEADS-A task_9daa28fba3ec481cae60 and QAFIX4-AGENT-PANES task_f88310d09496438483e5.

Measured causes, on main at 314f1cca or later, plugin 0.5.53 (installed 0.5.49 shows the same):
1. `plugin/workflows/run.js` `stepAnswer()` builds the flat step result from state, answer_excerpt, cost_usd, duration_s, pr_url, artifacts, last_error and console. It drops `questions`, although `STEP_FIELDS` accepts it and the `sc:step` / `sc:task` agents return it (agents/step.md). Every per-step run's result therefore carries no questions. Seen today on NOVPC-JOBS (wf_268e5f8cad9649789fba) and QAFIX4-AGENT-PANES (wf_ac9eed2e58b647cba4f1): their implement steps wrote questions.json, and their rows' results have no questions field.
2. In the one-row summary mode (`rows: summary`), the run logs only a count ("N question(s) for the owner") and its result carries only that count. The questions themselves are never in front of the session.
3. Nothing in the `sc` skill or the `/sc:swarmcloud` workflow tells the session to put a run's questions to the person when the run ends. `swarm_check` (`apps/swarm-mcp/swarm_mcp/check.py`) lists AWAITING_INPUT steps but not unanswered owner questions, so a question from a row the session did not watch end, or one that ended before a context compaction, is never raised again.

### Severity

S2 — wrong data on screen or in the API (states, counts, capacity, costs, timings) — I can't trust what it says

### Where you saw it

Claude Code plugin or MCP bridge (plugin/, apps/swarm-mcp)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. Launch any lane with `/sc:swarmcloud` whose implement step writes questions.json.
2. Let the run end, and read its result. No step carries `questions`.
3. Run `/sc check`. It does not mention the questions.
4. Open the task in the console: the questions are there, unanswered.

### What you expected instead

- Every question a step's or task's agent asks reaches the session that launched it, whole (question, options, recommended, context), when the run ends.
- The session puts it to the person with AskUserQuestion and records the pick with swarm_task_answer.
- `/sc check` lists this session's finished tasks whose questions have no answer, so nothing is lost to a missed row or a compaction.
- The console and the session agree on which questions are open.

### Identifiers

task_dccf3e5fc5dd4a0b8cdf; `plugin/workflows/run.js` `stepAnswer`, `summaryNotices`, `summaryResult`; `plugin/skills/sc/SKILL.md`; `apps/swarm-mcp/swarm_mcp/check.py`; `progress.owner_questions` (already reads them, used by buildboard.py and compact.py).

### Does it look like one of these?

None of the listed shapes.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

    QAFIX4-AGENT-PANES implement: artifacts [..., "questions.json", ...]  -> step result keys: state, answer_excerpt, cost_usd, duration_s, pr_url, artifacts, last_error, console

### Anything else

The owner asked for it to be fixed on 2026-10-22. Lane PLUGIN-OWNER-QUESTIONS.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body: Another place the questions are lost: review steps. The PAGEHEADS-A review (task_9f2af094846f49a3813d) wrote "an empty 'needs_owner', because the implementer left no 'questions.json'", but the implement step's artifacts list `questions.json` (task_9daa28fba3ec481cae60), with one question the owner has since answered. The CAPACITY and QATOOL reviewers made the same claim, and there the implementers really had asked none. So a review step's `needs_owner` cannot be trusted to carry the implementer's questions. It probably reads the working tree, not the implement step's artifacts. Lane PLUGIN-OWNER-QUESTIONS covers the plugin and `/sc check`; the review step's brief template is a follow-up once that lane lands.

title: A lane's CI-fix round was not told which test failed, the lane never ran the stylesheet guards, and its page read as stuck (PR 1905)
body:
### What happened

BGD asked why workflow `wf_15160fca1d07438ab594` (QAFIX4-RUNS, PR 1905) was stuck. It was not dead, but three platform defects made it slow and made it look stuck. Measured 2026-10-22 01:20-01:35Z.

The PR was red because `apps/swarm-ui/src/styles/intake.css` declared `.rn-filters > .c-seg > button` twice in the 560px block (lines 506 and 515), which `stylesheet.gate.test.ts` and `sections.stylesheet.test.ts` refuse ("swarm-ui component tests (2/4)" and "(4/4)"). The merge step started CI-fix round 1 (`task_d38fb3ecddb6463288b5`) at 01:26:42Z.

1. **The CI-fix round was not told which test failed.** The excerpt (`swarm_api/issueci.py` `_check_section`) keeps `MAX_LOG_TAIL_BYTES = 3_000` from each job log's END. On "swarm-ui component tests (2/4)" about half of those bytes are "Post job cleanup" git lines. The `FAIL src/__tests__/sections.stylesheet.test.ts > ... intake.css` line and the "Received" naming the selector and its two lines sit just above the cut. What reached the fixer was the matcher line, `m(r.duplicates).toEqual([])`, and "1 failed". The checks were also taken in GitHub's order: `ci-gate`, a roll-up whose tail is only the `needs` JSON, came first among the 5 kept. The agent spent ~9 minutes reconstructing vitest's sha1 shard split to find which files had run. The vitest jobs had no annotations to fall back on. The PR-side fixer (`scripts/ci-fix.sh`) has a sibling defect: `gh run view <run> --log-failed` on run 39703499595 returned 106 lines, all from `ci-gate`, and none from the three failed jobs whose names contain `/` ("swarm-ui component tests (2/4)", "(4/4)", "swarm-ui typecheck / component tests").
2. **The lane never ran the stylesheet guards.** `scripts/related-tests.sh` selects vitest files through the import graph. The two stylesheet guards read CSS from disk, so a CSS-only change never selects them. The implement, fix and re-review steps all passed what they ran.
3. **The status reads did not say what was happening.** `swarm_workflow_status` answered `state: UNKNOWN` ("step_tasks_missing ... ci-fix:1 ... not in the page this read loaded"), and the merge step's waiting line kept reading "CI on PR #1905: 1 checks pending (ci-gate); next check 01:35Z" after `ci-gate` had FAILED at 01:25:51Z. The page showed no sign that a fix round was running.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround (read the job logs by hand).

### Where you saw it

https://swarm.saga.xyz/workflows/wf_15160fca1d07438ab594, PR 1905, application run 39703499595.

### Environment

SwarmCloud (dev), 2026-10-22.

### Steps to reproduce

A lane PR whose only failure is in a vitest shard job: read the CI-fix round's FAILING CHECKS excerpt, the merge step's waiting line and `swarm_workflow_status` while the round runs.

### What you expected instead

Owner decision 2026-10-22 (BGD), all three approved as lanes:
1. A CI-fix round's excerpt names each failing test, its file and the assertion's message, for every failed job. Logs are cut at the failed step's end, not the job's end. Roll-up checks (`ci-gate`) go last. `scripts/ci-fix.sh` reads every failed job, including names with `/`.
2. `scripts/related-tests.sh` selects `stylesheet.gate.test.ts` and `sections.stylesheet.test.ts` whenever an `apps/swarm-ui` stylesheet changes.
3. A workflow with a CI-fix step reads its real state (PARKED, with `ci-fix:1` RUNNING), and a merge step's waiting line names a failed check as failed, with the fix round under way, not as pending.

### Identifiers

`wf_15160fca1d07438ab594`, merge `task_0b5b07c139a54ee78a39`, ci-fix:1 `task_d38fb3ecddb6463288b5`, run 39703499595, jobs 119584394927 / 119584394667.

### Does it look like one of these?

No.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

The 3,000-byte tail the fixer received ends with `Test Files 1 failed | 128 passed (129)`, `##[error]Process completed with exit code 1.`, then 13 lines of "Post job cleanup".

### Anything else

Lanes CIFIX-EXCERPT (1), RELATED-CSS-GUARDS (2) and STATUS-TRUE (3).

title: A failure-review schedule finds every failed agent and workflow of the last 7 hours, root-causes each and runs a fix for it
body:
### What are you trying to do?

BGD, 2026-10-22: "set up an automation job that will run every 6 hrs and investigate all of the agents and workflows that failed in the past 7 hrs, do an exhaustive in depth review and root cause analysis and why it failed. Propose a solution or a fix and, for each proposed solution, dispatch a workflow to design, plan, implement, review test and merge each fix".

### What would you like to see?

A SwarmCloud schedule type, `failure-review`. Owner decisions, 2026-10-22 ~04:40Z (BGD):
- **Runs where:** "Platform type only". It is built into SwarmCloud and fires on its cron with no Claude Code session. Nothing runs until it is live.
- **Autonomy:** "Dispatch and merge; hold risky". Each root cause gets an issue and a fix run (design, plan, implement with red-first tests, review, fix, merge on a MERGE verdict) without asking. A fix that touches IAM, the frozen contract (`apps/common/swarm_common/`), secrets or tenant isolation, the other team's resources in the shared project, or cost stops with `needs-owner` and goes to BGD. Each run ends with one summary. For this job only, this overrides the standing "ask before each proposal" rule.
- **Scope:** "All tenants; fix SwarmCloud causes". Every tenant's failures are reviewed. Expected failures are skipped (the acceptance suite's deliberate cases, a person's cancel, verify-remote's deliberate fences). A cause in the SwarmCloud platform is fixed in this repository. A cause in another repository's own code is reported for that repository, never fixed here.
- **Budget:** "No cap". There is no per-run limit on the number of fix runs.

Every 6 hours, over the previous 7 (one hour of overlap, so nothing falls between two runs):
1. Gather every FAILED or DEAD_LETTERED task and every failed workflow, with what explains each: last_error, end cause, events, attempt errors, heartbeat series, the log tail, and for a merge step its CI excerpt.
2. Group them by root cause and investigate each group against the code, exhaustively, with the evidence written down. A root cause already filed by an earlier run is updated, not filed again.
3. File one issue per root cause, with its proposed fix.
4. Start one fix run per issue, unless it falls in a hold category.

### Where would this live?

The schedules catalogue (`docs/schedules.md`, swarm-api's schedule types and executors), with the issue runs that the issue-sweep type already uses for plan, execute, review and merge.

### How do you do it today?

By hand, in a Claude Code session: on 2026-10-22 alone, PR 1905's stalled CI-fix round, the out-of-memory retries (#1926), the account label 500 (#1912) and the metric replace that failed every release were each found only because someone looked.

### How would you know it worked?

A firing over a window that holds a known failure (for example a seeded mock task failing with a fixed error) files one issue naming its cause and starts one fix run. A second firing over the same window files nothing new. A failure whose fix touches IAM is filed with `needs-owner` and gets no run.

### Constraint check

Reading every tenant's failures crosses tenants (invariant 9), so the type is platform-scoped (platform admin), and the digest given to the agent is redacted data, never instructions (invariant 10). Any new IAM it needs (for example reading logs) is held at dev-iam for BGD. The design lane names every such row.

title: The swarm-workers log view cannot be filtered to SwarmCloud on _Default: view filters allow only source, resource type and log id
body:
### What happened

The release's IAM apply failed creating the `swarm-workers` log view that AU5-LOG-VIEW (PR 1945) declared on the `_Default` bucket: `Error creating LogView: googleapi: Error 400: Filter exceeds the view filter nesting depth limit of 1.` (terraform/infra/log_view.tf line 113). The fault is in the design, not just the filter's shape. Google's LogView reference restricts a view filter to a logical AND of `=`/`!=` checks on the originating project/folder/organization/billing account, the resource type and the log id. So no view on `_Default` can select by `resource.labels.cluster_name` or `namespace_name`, which is what agent-autonomy.md §3.5 needs: the other team's agents-staging cluster writes to the same bucket. The view was never created and the L-1 binding was never attempted, so nothing was exposed.

### Severity

S2. Nothing is exposed and nothing is broken that worked before. Every release fails its IAM job at this one resource until the view is switched off or redesigned, and logs_query (AU-4) answers `logs_unavailable`.

### Where you saw it

Release workflow, job "terraform apply, IAM (dev-iam)".

### Environment

SwarmCloud dev (saga-agents-staging), release run 39742374084 at main 34e8d6b0, 2026-10-22 ~09:10Z.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Plan terraform/infra with log_view.tf as merged in PR 1945.
2. Apply: google_logging_log_view.swarm_workers fails with the 400 above.

### What you expected instead

A view swarm-api can read that shows only SwarmCloud's containers and Cloud Run resources (agent-autonomy.md §3.5, owner decision Q4: "A log view filtered to SwarmCloud resources, viewAccessor on the view only").

### Identifiers

- Release or CI run id: 39742374084 (job 119727768185)

### Does it look like one of these?

A design premise a provider limit rules out.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

```
Error creating LogView: googleapi: Error 400: Filter exceeds the view filter nesting depth limit of 1.
  with google_logging_log_view.swarm_workers, on log_view.tf line 113
```

### Notes

Mitigation dispatched overnight: lane AU5-VIEWOFF puts the view and its binding behind `swarm_workers_log_view_enabled` (default false), so releases stop failing; nothing existed to destroy.

The redesign is the owner's decision (cost and IAM). One shape that meets §3.5: a dedicated log bucket fed by a sink that carries the four branches (sinks accept the full query language), with an unfiltered view on that bucket and L-1 on that view. Routing duplicates those entries into a second bucket, so it adds ingestion cost.

title: The pre-publish uv run creates .venv and uv.lock inside the clone, and the publish commits the uv.lock into the lane's PR
body:
### What happened

The worker's pre-publish check runs `uv run pytest` from the project directory **inside the agent's clone** (`apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/prepublish.py` `_pytest_project`, ~871: `runner(argv, Path(repo) / project, env, timeout)`, with no `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`). uv then creates the project's `.venv` and, where the project has none, a `uv.lock` inside the checkout. The publish step then stages everything with `git add --all -- .` (`apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/gitops.py` ~2307), so a file the check itself created is committed into the lane's PR.

Reported by the AI Studio session on 2026-10-22 for sagaxyz/ai-studio:
- task_2df71fc1d5d34997957a (PR #791 there): the pre-publish `uv run pytest` created `runner/.venv` and an untracked `runner/uv.lock`. The venv made 4 pin guards in `runner/tests/test_aipipeline_pin_sync.py` go red (they sweep `runner/**` for hex strings; that repository's runner/CLAUDE.md requires the venv outside the repo), and the 1,659-line `runner/uv.lock` ended up in the PR.
- task_65d0f0328cc6464f8358 (PR #792 there): the same `runner/uv.lock` (+1659) is in the PR; that repository's main has no `runner/uv.lock`.

### Severity

S2. Lane PRs in other repositories carry files no one wrote, and a repository's own guards can go red on an environment the platform put inside its tree. Not an isolation or secrets defect.

### Where you saw it

Lane PRs (the publish step), via the pre-publish check.

### Environment

SwarmCloud dev, claude-code lanes on sagaxyz/ai-studio, 2026-10-22.

### Steps to reproduce

1. A lane changes a Python file under a subproject with a `pyproject.toml` and no `uv.lock` (ai-studio's `runner/`).
2. Pre-publish selects tests there and runs `uv run pytest` from that directory.
3. The PR contains `<project>/uv.lock`; `<project>/.venv` exists in the clone during the check.

### What you expected instead

The checks run with the project environment outside the clone, and leave the working tree exactly as the agent left it: nothing a check created or changed is committed.

### Identifiers

- Task id: task_2df71fc1d5d34997957a, task_65d0f0328cc6464f8358

### Does it look like one of these?

A check with a side effect on the thing it checks.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

See the two tasks' summaries (the AI Studio session's report).

### Notes

Fix lane PREPUB-UV-OUTSIDE: `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` in a temporary directory outside the checkout for every uv invocation the pre-publish checks make, and a before/after snapshot so any path the checks created or changed is restored before the publish stages.

title: The graphsvc 'forged' ticket test can mint a ticket whose forgery equals the original, about once in 1,024 runs
body:
### What happened

`tests/unit/graphsvc/test_graphsvc_ticket.py::test_what_the_reference_refuses_is_refused_here[forged]` failed with `Failed: DID NOT RAISE TicketRefused` on PR 1966's CI (run 39755620191, job 119753483938, "unit tests (4/8)"; 1 failed, 3803 passed), on a change that does not touch graphsvc.

The case builds its forgery as `mint(key, raw=RAW)[:-2] + "AA"`: it replaces the last two base64url characters of the ticket. The ticket is minted against `time.time()`, so its MAC differs on every run. When the original last two characters already decode to the same MAC bytes as "AA" (the last character carries only 4 significant bits, so this happens about once in 1,024 runs), the "forged" ticket is the genuine one and is accepted.

### Severity

S3. A flaky unit test turns unrelated lane PRs red and costs a CI-fix round each time.

### Where you saw it

CI, application.yml unit tests.

### Environment

GitHub Actions, PR 1966 (AU8-SEED), 2026-10-22 ~09:3xZ.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the case enough times; it fails whenever the minted ticket's tail already matches "AA" after decoding.

### What you expected instead

The forged case always alters the MAC, so the refusal is deterministic.

### Identifiers

- Release or CI run id: 39755620191 (job 119753483938)

### Does it look like one of these?

A test whose input is random and whose assertion is not.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

`FAILED tests/unit/graphsvc/test_graphsvc_ticket.py::test_what_the_reference_refuses_is_refused_here[forged] - Failed: DID NOT RAISE TicketRefused`

### Notes

Fix lane GRAPHSVC-FORGED: build the forgery by flipping one bit of the decoded MAC (decode, XOR a byte, re-encode), so it always differs.

title: Console QA captures fail on every route: the persona cookie is set via Storage.setCookies, which the live gate refuses
body:
### What happened

Console visual QA run 5 (workflow wf_b7b49ff2307a467e94a2, 2026-10-22 ~10:25Z) captured nothing: every capture step (overview-automate, work-a, work-b, capacity, admin, task) failed on every route, e.g. "captured 0, failed 32", each failure "the live gate refusing `Storage.setCookies`". `swarm_qa capture` sets the QA persona cookie with Playwright's `context.add_cookies(...)` (`images/agent-runtime-browser/swarm_qa.py` ~749), which Playwright sends over CDP as `Storage.setCookies`; the live gate refuses the cookie APIs by design (cookies are never exposed through the gate). The persona cookie arrived with QAFIX4-FIXTURE-A (PR 1924, merged 2026-10-22 06:42Z), after run 4, so run 5 was its first real use; its unit tests use a fake context and could not see the refusal. A generic capture with no persona routes (VQ5-PERSONA) is unaffected: the external TodoMVC proof captured fine the same hour.

### Severity

S2. The console visual-QA pipeline produces no screens until fixed; nothing else is affected.

### Where you saw it

`swarm_qa capture` inside claude-code-browser tasks, through the live gate's CDP proxy.

### Environment

SwarmCloud dev, main after PR 1924 (and VQ5-PERSONA, PR 1952), 2026-10-22.

### Steps to reproduce

Run any group of `apps/swarm-ui/qa/routes.json` through `swarm_qa capture` on a claude-code-browser task: every route fails at the persona step.

### What you expected instead

The persona is set in a way the gate allows, and the capture proceeds as in run 4.

### Identifiers

- Workflow id: wf_b7b49ff2307a467e94a2 (run 5); task_9f00e2badaf44c19bac1 (capture-overview-automate)

### Does it look like one of these?

A test double that accepts a call the real proxy refuses.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Every capture manifest lists each route failed at step "persona" with the gate's `Storage.setCookies` refusal.

### Notes

Fix lane QA-PERSONA-COOKIE: set the cookie from the page on the console's origin (`document.cookie`), which the gate allows, and make the fake context refuse `add_cookies` so the tests catch a regression. The gate's cookie rule is a security property and is not changed.

title: The merge step decides a required check's state with required_check_state, which returns "failed" when ANY run of that check at the head has a non-green conclusion, so PR #1966's first ci-gate run (f…
body:
<!-- failure-review fingerprint=fr-e2456fb8d259 -->
### What happened

2 failure(s) in the window 2026-10-22T05:41:22.198659+00:00 to 2026-10-22T12:41:22.198659+00:00 share one cause: The merge step decides a required check's state with required_check_state, which returns "failed" when ANY run of that check at the head has a non-green conclusion, so PR #1966's first ci-gate run (failure, a unit-tests 4/8 flake) kept ci-gate failed after a later ci-gate run at the same head 5b25774 succeeded; _red then spent CI-fix round 1 on a check that was already green (f-001, whose agent correctly found nothing to fix and so failed published_nothing), and once that round ended at the unchanged head refused checks_failed (f-002).

### Severity

S1 — blocked: I cannot do the thing at all

### Where you saw it

Worker on Cloud Run (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-base)

### Environment

Not sure

### Steps to reproduce

Found by the failure-review schedule `sch_54e9828e6772`, firing `sch_54e9828e6772:run_now:b946b43875e14768b099eedf139c6505`, from the failures it reviewed: agent `task_21bce87e04884bcdb3bb`; agent `task_8a40d6634c4c421a96b1`.

### What you expected instead

These agents end without this failure: the cause below is fixed in the code, with a test that fails before the fix and passes after it.

### Identifiers

- Fingerprint: `fr-e2456fb8d259`
- Signature: `checks_failed: at <id>: ci-gate (failure, success), after CI fix round <n> (<id>) ended at this head`
- Failures: agent `task_21bce87e04884bcdb3bb`; agent `task_8a40d6634c4c421a96b1`

### Screenshots, errors, logs

- `read apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/merge.py:387-396 (required_check_state) and :1437-1450 (_forge_outcome's required-check loop)`: required_check_state returns 'green' only if all(run.conclusion in REQUIRED_GREEN for run in runs); the failed label is built from the SET of every run's conclusion, which is exactly the '(failure, success)' text in f-002's last_error. latest_reading (:399-426), which judges by the latest run, is used only for the park RECORD; its docstring says 'the merge decides on required_check_state ... which still read every run (#1778 is the same latest-run rule for the decision)'.
- `mcp swarm-git pr_checks pr=1966`: head 5b25774d14ed9886a454d106e6b4a72e68732c5b, overall state green; ci-gate (required) appears twice, both rows completed/success at read time (2026-10-22 ~12:45Z); every unit tests (n/8) row success.
- `read f-001's agent_stdout in the digest`: the CI-fix agent reports: in the first CI run on 5b25774 'unit tests (4/8)' failed and turned python-unit and ci-gate red; in the second run every group passed and ci-gate reported success, 'so there was nothing in the branch to fix'; it made no commit, hence published_nothing at lifecycle.py::_published_nothing (git.commit_count 0).
- `read apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/merge.py:2259-2292 (_red)`: with rounds left _red waits CI_FIX_PENDING (round 1 dispatched, task_8a40d6634c4c421a96b1); when the last round's recorded head equals the current head and the round ended, it refuses 'checks_failed: ..., after CI fix round N (task) ended at this head' -- f-002's text verbatim.
- `mcp swarm-state workflow_view wf_2a083f38090f4f99b4c9`: steps implement/review/fix/re-review SUCCEEDED; merge FAILED merge_refused with the checks_failed text; ci-fix:1 FAILED outputs_missing published_nothing -- both failures are this one workflow.
- `mcp swarm-git issue_view 1778`: open S2 bug 'The merge step reads a cancelled check run as a failure even when a later run of the same check succeeded' -- the same decision site, reported for (cancelled, success); this firing shows it also holds for (failure, success), and that it dispatches a CI-fix round over a check that is already green.

### Anything else

**Proposed fix.** In merge.py::_forge_outcome decide each required check by its LATEST run at the head (ordered as latest_reading orders them: run_id, then position), i.e. make required_check_state judge ordered[-1] and build the failed label from that run's conclusion only; a latest run not completed stays pending. Red first in tests/unit/worker (beside test_wait_record.py): a required check with runs [failure(run_id=1), success(run_id=2)] at the head must read green and run_merge must not refuse checks_failed or request a CI-fix round; and [success(1), failure(2)] must still read failed. Secondary (optional, same lane): a CI-fix round whose agent changed nothing because the head is already green should end via the no-change path, not published_nothing -- the CI-fix brief should ask for verification.md so _verified_no_change applies. This is part of #1778, not a new issue.

**Files.** `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/merge.py`, `tests/unit/worker/test_wait_record.py`

A fix run is started for this issue by the failure-review schedule.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Owner decision, 2026-10-22 18:30Z (BGD): a required check is decided by its latest run per event.**

A re-run replaces earlier runs of the same event (push or pull_request). Every event's latest run must still be green, so CI-EARLY's guarantee (#1694, `test_ci_early.py`) holds: a red push run is never outvoted by a green pull_request run. This answers question 1 of the fix run's planner (task_f3002686ee854e5495ff). Its question 2, whether the same rule also applies to swarm-api's `forgechecks` and `auto-merge.yml`, is still open. The fix lane is dispatched once that is answered. Related: #1778, the same site with (cancelled, success).

title: A refused workflow push's workflow-lines.patch is stored but missing from the task's artifact list, and its reason is cut mid-sentence
body:
### What happened

When the broker refuses a workflow-touching push (`workflow_scope_missing`), the worker writes `workflow-lines.patch` and uploads it, but the task's artifact list never shows it. The step's error names the file and its `gs://` URI, yet `swarm_result` / `swarm_artifact` list six artifacts without it. An operator or a following step (the CI-fix agent) then concludes the patch was never written.

The same error is also cut mid-sentence: `_workflow_push_refused` keeps `refused['message'][:300]`, which drops the refusal's last words, so the reason reads "Push without those files and write them as. Nothing was pushed".

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Worker on Cloud Run (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-base). This attempt ran on GKE_AUTOPILOT with runner profile claude-code; the code path is the same.

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. A claude-code step commits a change to `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` (the CI-fix step for PR 2019 did, task_58815d231b2146689808, attempt att_3a25f73128d14e168d8d, 2026-10-22 20:28Z).
2. The worker publishes through swarm-api's `git_push_branch`, which answers `workflow_scope_missing` (the `-git-wf` slot holds no version).
3. `swarm_result task_58815d231b2146689808`: `outputs.artifacts` lists claude-code.stderr.log, claude-code.stdout.log, claude-transcript.json, pr-title.txt, prepublish-advisory.md and swarm-work.patch. No workflow-lines.patch.
4. `gcloud storage ls -l` on the attempt's artifacts prefix, read 2026-10-22T22:15Z: workflow-lines.patch IS there, 3,867 bytes, stored 20:32:52Z. The other six were stored 20:32:47-48Z.

### What you expected instead

The artifact list a task serves includes every artifact the worker uploaded for the attempt, including the `workflow-lines.patch` that `_write_workflow_patch` uploads after the manifest has gone. The refusal reason quoted in the step's error is either whole or cut at a word boundary with an ellipsis, so it never reads as a different sentence.

### Identifiers

task_58815d231b2146689808, att_3a25f73128d14e168d8d, PR 2019 (CHECK-RULE). Code: `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py` `_workflow_push_refused` (the `[:300]` cut) and `_write_workflow_patch` (the upload after the artifacts manifest).

### Does it look like one of these?

A listing that disagrees with the store.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

The step's error, as served (URIs shortened):
"...and it answered workflow_scope_missing: the push touches .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml; GitHub takes a workflow file only from a credential with the workflow scope, and swarm-tenant-eng-git-wf holds no version (...). Push without those files and write them as. Nothing was pushed; the workflow change is in workflow-lines.patch (gs://.../artifacts/workflow-lines.patch)."

### Anything else

The control: the six artifacts listed were all stored before the publish ran, and the one missing was stored 4 s after. So the listing is the manifest written before publish, not a read of the store. The CI-fix agent's summary says "that patch isn't in this workspace". It re-derived the auto-merge.yml change from the failing tests, and CLD hand-pushed it as commit 8a604e7c.

title: Workflow-file pushes use a per-repo GitHub App token, switched on per repository, and the -git-wf slot is gone
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Let an agent's branch push that changes `.github/workflows/**` or `.github/actions/**` land without a person handing over a token. The same job should be pointable at another project or repository later, without CLD or BGD storing anything per repo.

Today the broker (`apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/gittools.py` `_workflow_token`) pushes such a change only on the `platform: true` registration, and only with the `-git-wf` slot (`swarm-tenant-<tenant>-git-wf`, a personal token BGD would store by hand, read by swarm-api through IAM row L-2). The slot was never filled. Every workflow-touching lane ends `workflow_scope_missing`, and CLD hand-pushes its `workflow-lines.patch` (PR 2019 and PR 2024 on 2026-10-22).

### What would you like to see?

Decided by BGD on 2026-10-22, in four answers:

1. **The SwarmCloud GitHub App mints the token at push time.** swarm-api mints an installation token for ONE repository (`repositories=[<repo>]`) with `contents: write` and `workflows: write`, from the workspace's OWN installation (its `forge_orgs` documents, invariant 9). It is used for that one push call, never stored, never handed to a worker, and lives at most an hour. BGD: "can we use the github app creds for this? This way we can point a similar job in the future at another project or repo."
2. **Self-serve, per-repo opt-in.** A `workflow_files` switch on each repository registration, off by default, set by the workspace's admin when the repo is added or later. It is audited like `agents_may_file_issues`. With it off, a workflow-touching push is still refused `workflow_scope_missing` with `workflow-lines.patch`. The SwarmCloud repository is switched on after deploy. BGD: "when adding a new repo to SwarmCloud, the per-repo token is created for the new repo as well, self serve".
3. **The `-git-wf` slot and IAM row L-2 are removed in the same lane** (BGD chose this over removing them after a live proof). The release holds at `dev-iam` for the L-2 removal.
4. **The App asks for "Workflows: Read and write".** CLD changes the App's settings in Chrome, and each installation's owner accepts. An installation that has not accepted reads as "Workflows: not granted" in the console, and its pushes fall back to the patch.

Unchanged: a merge of a workflow change stays held NEEDS_OWNER (`STOP_WORKFLOWS`, owner decision Q3). The hold now covers every repository whose switch is on, not only `platform: true`.

### Where would this live?

API — /v1, including sign-in and tenant resolution (apps/swarm-api). Then the console's Repositories pages for the switch, and Terraform and scripts for the removal.

### How do you do it today?

CLD downloads `workflow-lines.patch` from the lane's artifacts and pushes it to the PR branch as bogdan-alexandrescu.

### How would you know it worked?

* A lane on the SwarmCloud repository changes `.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml`, and its branch is pushed by the App (the push actor is `swarmcloud-saga[bot]`), with no hand push. The PR's merge is held for BGD.
* The same push on a repository whose switch is off is refused `workflow_scope_missing` and leaves `workflow-lines.patch`.
* `swarm-tenant-eng-git-wf`, IAM row L-2 and `create-secrets.sh --git-wf` no longer exist.

### Constraint check

None of the above, as far as I can tell. A branch workflow runs with that repository's secrets before any merge hold, which is why the switch is per repo and off by default.

title: The publish scan's key_value_assignment refuses a 12-character mock fixture and a runtime template expression, and its repair advice is to split strings
body:
### What happened

The worker's final-tree credential scan (rule `key_value_assignment`, a GENERIC rule in `GENERIC_CREDENTIAL_RULES`, `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py` ~15055) refused to publish a `direct-pr` task in the Product Oracle repository three attempts in a row. It flagged two lines that carry no credential:

* line 70 of `web/lib/api/mock/interviews.ts`: `export const MOCK_INTERVIEW_TOKEN = "i-mock-token";`, a client-side mock fixture used only by the mock build and Playwright. The value is 12 characters, hyphen-joined, lowercase and ends `-token`, the shape the scan's own comment lists as a reference rather than a value. Line 69 is its doc comment.
* line 387: `r.token = `i-${mockUuid().replace(/-/g, "")}`;`, a value built at runtime with no literal in it.

The step's error: "the final tree adds a credential in web/lib/api/mock/interviews.ts (rule key_value_assignment, line 70); remove it" (`lifecycle.py` ~15898). The repair prompt the agent got (`runners/cliagent.py` ~1088-1090) tells it "a test value is built at runtime from pieces, never written as one literal". That repository's own rules forbid string-splitting, so the agent had no way through. The task failed after 4 attempts, cost at least $13.34, and its dependants were cancelled.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Worker on Cloud Run (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-base)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. Task task_40b0f14c58094189839b in workflow wf_a069039a24b44498b5ba (tenant eng), a `direct-pr` step on the Product Oracle repository, reported by that repository's Claude Code session (product-oracle-f2) to this session on 2026-10-23.
2. The final tree adds the two lines above.
3. The publish step refuses with the error above, on every attempt.

### What you expected instead

* A line whose value is a runtime expression (a template literal whose only content is `${...}` slots and fixed short affixes, or a function call) is not a credential, and neither is a comment line.
* A short, low-entropy, hyphen-joined lowercase value ending `-token` reads as a reference, as the scan's comment says. If the comment and the code disagree, one of them is wrong.
* A repository can declare test-fixture paths (for example `web/lib/api/mock/**`) where the GENERIC rules relax to the vendor-format rules only. It is set by that repository's owner on its registration, never by an agent.
* The refusal and the repair prompt name what was matched and why, and never prescribe string-splitting as the way through. Splitting is a workaround that defeats the scan, and some repositories forbid it.

### Identifiers

task_40b0f14c58094189839b, wf_a069039a24b44498b5ba. Code: `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py` (`GENERIC_CREDENTIAL_RULES` ~15055, the refusal ~15898), `apps/redaction/swarm_redaction/rules.py` (`key_value_assignment` ~758), `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/runners/cliagent.py` (repair prompt ~1088).

### Does it look like one of these?

A guard that refuses more than its name says.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

"the final tree adds a credential in web/lib/api/mock/interviews.ts (rule key_value_assignment, line 70); remove it"

### Anything else

Reported by the Product Oracle session. Their workaround: BGD approved publishing that one patch from his machine after a manual secret check (their PR 301). CLD has not reproduced the match yet. The fix lane's first test should run the two lines through the scan as committed and show which tier matched. The value is copied here from the reporter's message, not read from the task, and it is a fixture name, not a credential.

title: The merge step waited 6 h on a check run GitHub left in_progress after giving it a conclusion and completed_at
body:
### What happened

The merge step for PR 2006 (VQ6-ROUTE, task_6f92e2833ee442728d38) parked CI_PENDING 23 times and then FAILED `checks_timeout: CI has not settled in 368 min, past 6 h: at 8843eed7...: secret scan`. Every check at that head was green. One check run, `secret scan` (id 120028057811), reads `status: in_progress` with `conclusion: success` and `completed_at: 2026-10-22T19:05:52Z`. Its workflow run, security 39836987498 (push), is `completed`/`success`. GitHub never moved the job's status to completed. GitHub's own rollup (the PR page, GraphQL `statusCheckRollup`) shows it SUCCESS. The worker's merge step reads `status` alone, so it waited out the whole 6 h window on a run that had finished.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Worker on Cloud Run (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-base)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. `gh api repos/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/check-runs/120028057811`, read 2026-10-23T01:02Z: `status=in_progress conclusion=success`.
2. `gh api "repos/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/actions/runs?head_sha=8843eed7fcf54e93c275e58bc9aa9bb83cf6ff03"`: run 39836987498 `completed success`.
3. `swarm_result task_6f92e2833ee442728d38`: FAILED `checks_timeout` on `secret scan`.

### What you expected instead

A check run that carries a `conclusion` and a `completed_at` is judged by its conclusion, whatever `status` says. That applies in the worker's merge step (`apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/merge.py`: `required_check_state` and `other_check_blocks`), in swarm-api's `forgechecks`, and in auto-merge.yml gates 5-6 and `merge-train.sh judge`, so all four agree. A run with no conclusion stays pending. The other control: a run with `status: completed` and no conclusion is not green either.

### Identifiers

PR 2006, task_6f92e2833ee442728d38, check run 120028057811, workflow run 39836987498, head 8843eed7fcf54e93c275e58bc9aa9bb83cf6ff03.

### Does it look like one of these?

A wait that cannot end.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

`checks_timeout: CI has not settled in 368 min, past 6 h: at 8843eed7fcf54e93c275e58bc9aa9bb83cf6ff03: secret scan`

### Anything else

Workaround: CLD re-ran workflow run 39836987498 at 2026-10-23T01:02Z, so the same event gets a newer `secret scan` run, and put the rescue watcher on PR 2006. The same rule site is being changed by lane CHECK-RULE-2 (PR 2024). A fix lane should start after that merges.

title: A /sc:swarmcloud launch retypes the embedded spec, and a brief with template-literal text arrives altered and is refused
body:
### What happened

The `/sc:swarmcloud` launch of lane SCAN-FP submitted nothing. Its result was `NOT_SUBMITTED`: "the spec this tool received has digest fnv1a32:9e7e101e, and `spec_digest` says the spec meant was fnv1a32:ee384b34: the spec was changed on its way here -- by whoever retyped it". The spec was embedded in the titled script copy that `swarm_workflow_launch` wrote, and the script's `sc:workflow` agent still passes the spec to `swarm_workflow` by value, so it retypes ~23 KB of JSON. This brief is the only one of five launched the same way tonight that contains JavaScript template-literal text: backticks with `${...}` inside, e.g. `` `i-${mockUuid().replace(/-/g, "")}` ``. The other four (CHECK-RULE-2, LOG-BUCKET-2, WF-APP-TOKEN, and earlier lanes) submitted.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Claude Code plugin or MCP bridge — /sc and the swarm_* tools (plugin, apps/swarm-mcp)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. `swarm_workflow_launch {spec_path: scratchpad/specs-1016/scan-fp.json}`, embed the spec in the returned script, run it with the Workflow tool (2026-10-23 ~01:35Z, run wf_053776f6-dcb).
2. The Submit row's agent calls `swarm_workflow` with the spec text, and the digest check refuses it.

### What you expected instead

A launch submits by reference whenever the spec is a file or an embedded object, so no agent ever retypes it. The script hands the bridge the path or the embedded object, and the agent passes only a handle. The digest check stays, and a refusal still submits nothing. The submission never depends on whether the spec contains backticks, `${`, or anything else a model may "fix".

### Identifiers

Launch run wf_053776f6-dcb (NOT_SUBMITTED); the same spec submitted directly as wf_ebe23d21e378406db82e and attached with `{attach: ...}`.

### Does it look like one of these?

A copy that is the defect.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

`NOT_SUBMITTED: the spec this tool received has digest fnv1a32:9e7e101e, and spec_digest says the spec meant was fnv1a32:ee384b34`

### Anything else

Workaround: `scratchpad/ops-1016/submit_direct.py` (the API client tagged with the session), then `swarm_workflow_launch {attach}` for rows. The digest check worked as designed: it stopped an altered spec.

title: A hand-applied workspace namespace gets render.py's 100-pod/400-vCPU quota, not its record's, so the final check fails the workspace
body:
### What happened

u-bogdan's workspace (w-752763) read `failed` on /setup with VERIFY_FAILED: "the final check could not find one of your workspace's objects". The final check (A9, `scripts/register-tenant.sh` ~1846-1854) compares the namespace's ResourceQuota against the record's limits: 100 agents gives pods 200, requests.cpu 800 and limits.cpu 1600 (`WS_PODS_PER_AGENT=2`, `WS_CPU_PER_AGENT=8`, `CPU_BURST_MAX_RATIO=2`). The live quota in `swarm-tenant-u-bogdan`, read 2026-10-23 02:34Z, was pods 100, requests.cpu 400 and limits.cpu 800. Those are `kubernetes/render.py`'s defaults (`--quota-pods 100`, `--quota-cpu 400`, ~1482-1487). The namespace had been applied by hand with `kubernetes/apply.sh --tenant u-bogdan`, which renders a workspace tenant from those defaults and not from its record.

### Severity

S2 — wrong data on screen or in the API (states, counts, capacity, costs, timings) — I can't trust what it says

### Where you saw it

Web UI · Work › Setup (/setup)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. Apply a workspace tenant's namespace by hand: `kubernetes/apply.sh --tenant <t> --confirm`, with no quota flags.
2. Run `scripts/register-tenant.sh --workspace <id> --mode verify` under the call guard.
3. A9 fails on `ResourceQuota`, and the workspace goes `failed`. `--mode limits` then refuses ("a ceiling change needs a ready workspace"), so the job cannot repair it itself.

### What you expected instead

One formula for a workspace tenant's quota, in one place, read by `kubernetes/render.py`/`apply.sh` and by `register-tenant.sh`. `apply.sh` renders a workspace tenant's quota from its record's limits, never from the renderer's defaults. A quota mismatch is reported as such, not as a missing object. A failed verify whose only finding is the quota can be repaired by `--mode limits`.

### Identifiers

w-752763 (u-bogdan). Code: `scripts/register-tenant.sh` (`WS_PODS_PER_AGENT`, `WS_CPU_PER_AGENT` ~319-323, `ws_quota_args` ~1520, A9 ~1846), `kubernetes/render.py` (~1482-1487), `kubernetes/apply.sh`.

### Does it look like one of these?

The mirrored copy is the defect.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

`fail verify: a ResourceQuota is missing or not as specified` / `fail w-752763: A9 failed (VERIFY_FAILED, retryable: true)`

### Anything else

Repaired by hand at 02:37Z with BGD's approval. CLD ran `kubernetes/apply.sh` with the job's own A7 arguments: `--quota-pods 200 --quota-cpu 800 --quota-memory 1600Gi --quota-jobs 800 --quota-ephemeral 2000Gi`. The dry run changed only the ResourceQuota. The verify then read "verified: 34 of 34 objects", and w-752763 is `ready`. Lane QUOTA-ONE fixes the root cause. The page also says "checked 12d ago", which looks like the directory check's age rather than this verify's.

title: Tier 2 of the publish guard (_match_counts) passes a generic key/value match only when _is_a_reference AND _ends_the_value both hold, and _value_continues returns True for any word after a value's cl…
body:
<!-- failure-review fingerprint=fr-4eec45937823 -->
### What happened

3 failure(s) in the window 2026-10-22T17:01:01.775761+00:00 to 2026-10-23T00:01:01.775761+00:00 share one cause: Tier 2 of the publish guard (_match_counts) passes a generic key/value match only when _is_a_reference AND _ends_the_value both hold, and _value_continues returns True for any word after a value's closing quote, so a JSDoc comment that names the fixture value in backticks followed by prose (`/** The fixture's link token: ******** works on a freshly seeded mock. */`, product-oracle web/lib/api/mock/interviews.ts:70) is refused as a credential, although the same value assigned on line 71 (`= "...";`) passes; build-152-lane1 failed all 3 attempts on it, and its two dependants build-152-lane2 and review-152 were cancelled as failed_parent.

### Severity

S0 — a platform guarantee at risk (tenant isolation, the other team's resources, over-admission or a slot released under a running worker, a stale generation that ran, a secret printed)

### Where you saw it

Worker on Cloud Run (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-base)

### Environment

Not sure

### Steps to reproduce

Found by the failure-review schedule `sch_54e9828e6772`, firing `sch_54e9828e6772:29878560`, from the failures it reviewed: agent `task_40b0f14c58094189839b`; agent `task_81a58c3341f842e69285`; agent `task_a3a8c2e27f3141a59be1`.

### What you expected instead

These agents end without this failure: the cause below is fixed in the code, with a test that fails before the fix and passes after it.

### Identifiers

- Fingerprint: `fr-4eec45937823`
- Signature: `the final tree adds a credential in web/lib/api/<path> (rule key_value_assignment, line <n>); remove it`
- Failures: agent `task_40b0f14c58094189839b`; agent `task_81a58c3341f842e69285`; agent `task_a3a8c2e27f3141a59be1`

### Screenshots, errors, logs

- `swarm-state agent_artifacts task_40b0f14c58094189839b swarm-work.patch (hunk web/lib/api/mock/interviews.ts, new file, @@ -0,0 +1,400 @@)`: line 70 = `/** The fixture's link token: ******** works on a freshly seeded mock. */`; line 71 = `export const MOCK_INTERVIEW_TOKEN = "********";`; the agent's questions.json and final reply say the value is the issue-specified mock token ******** and line 70 is a comment
- `read apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py:15466-15475 (_match_counts), 15154 (_looks_like_a_credential), _REFERENCE_SHAPE, _ends_the_value, _value_continues (15413-15463), _assigns_a_literal/_BARE_CREDENTIAL_RE (15655-15677)`: a bare ******** would not count (_BARE_CREDENTIAL_RE needs a digit), so line 70 can only be refused as a quoted (backtick) literal: ******** matches _REFERENCE_SHAPE `[a-z]+(?:-[a-z]+)*-token` and _is_a_reference is True, but _value_continues(' works on a freshly...', '`', 0) falls through to `if rest[:1] != ",": return True`, so _ends_the_value is False and tier 2 refuses; line 71 ends in `;`, which _value_continues accepts
- `digest f-004 attempts and stderr`: generations 3, 4 and 5 all exit 0 and fail with the same 'line 70' refusal; two repair turns per attempt; the agent refused to split the string (lane rule), so retries_exhausted -> FAILED
- `swarm-state workflow_view wf_a069039a24b44498b5ba`: build-152-lane1 FAILED publish_refused; build-152-lane2 (task_81a58c3341f842e69285) and review-152 (task_a3a8c2e27f3141a59be1) CANCELLED failed_parent 'an upstream workflow step did not succeed', the only two failed_parent steps in the window, matching group f-005/f-006
- `an attempted probe of _credential_in on the three lines with uv run --offline`: did not run: offline uv could not install google-cloud-firestore. The conclusion above comes from reading the code. The .venv it created was removed.

### Anything else

**Proposed fix.** In _value_continues/_ends_the_value, treat a closed quoted reference followed by whitespace and then prose as whole when the match sits inside a comment (the line, after its indent, starts with //, /*, * or #). Or check the reference value itself in comment lines. Keep refusing when the value is joined to more value by +, a template or an adjacent quote. Red first: add a case in the publish-guard unit tests (tests/unit/worker/, the file holding _value_continues/_ends_the_value cases) asserting that _credential_in('web/lib/api/mock/x.ts', "/** The link token: ******** works on a seeded mock. */") is None, and that `token = ******** + suffix` is still a hit. Separately, the repair-turn text should not tell the agent to 'build the value from pieces' when the value is a reference shape, because the lane rules forbid that. Product-oracle's branch swarm/c3-interviews-lane1 publishes unchanged once this lands.

**Files.** `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py`

Held for the owner (`needs-owner`, category `secrets`): no fix run is started.

title: swarm-tenant-eng-git-wf holds no version, so gittools._workflow_token raises workflow_scope_missing for every push that touches .github/workflows/. The CHECK-RULE lanes (PR #2019, PR #2024) therefore…
body:

title: Browser agents get past CAPTCHAs by owner bypass and a person's hand-off, never by solving them
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Stop CAPTCHAs from blocking SwarmCloud's browser agents (visual QA, live-browser tasks), without solving or evading them. BGD asked on 2026-10-23 for "a solid solution for passing captcha in our browser agents".

**Out of scope, by design:** automated solving (solver services, models solving challenges), and detection evasion (stealth fingerprints, rotating residential proxies). A CAPTCHA is a site owner saying no to automated access. SwarmCloud's gate already ends a QA sign-in with `qa_sign_in_challenge` rather than solve one (visual-qa-any-app.md §2.4).

### What would you like to see?

BGD chose all three legitimate routes on 2026-10-23:

1. **Owner bypass per QA target** (lane CAPTCHA-BYPASS). A QA target may carry a challenge bypass that the app's owner configures: a header or cookie whose value is stored write-only like the QA credential. Only the gate adds it, and only on the target's own approved origins. The runbook for app owners covers always-pass test keys in staging (reCAPTCHA, hCaptcha, Cloudflare Turnstile) and a WAF skip rule matching the header in production.
2. **Reliable human hand-off** (lane CAPTCHA-HANDOFF). When the gate sees a challenge on an agent's page, it raises the hand-off itself: the agent is paused, and the console bell says "Agent needs you: CAPTCHA on <host>" with the take-control link. A person solves it, the agent resumes, and an unanswered hand-off times out cleanly. **Console bell only** (BGD): no Slack or email channel for now.
3. **Avoid triggers** (lane CAPTCHA-AVOID). Browser agents use the WebSearch tool instead of google.com in the browser, prefer a site's official API to scraping, and keep to polite rates on stable egress. The benchmark counts challenge pages per run, so before and after are measurable.

### Where would this live?

Worker on GKE — browser (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-browser, kubernetes): the live gate, plus swarm-api's QA targets and the console's QA targets page.

### How do you do it today?

Visual QA's sign-in refuses a challenge. A live-browser agent must notice a CAPTCHA itself and call `swarm-handoff`, and a person only learns of it from the console bell. Google search from the browser produces `/sorry` pages: 11 to 21 Google 429s per benchmark batch on 2026-10-15.

### How would you know it worked?

* A QA run against a target with an owner bypass passes a page that shows a challenge without it. The bypass value appears in no log, artifact or agent-visible message.
* A benchmark hand-off prompt (`recaptcha-demo-handoff`) raises its hand-off without the agent asking, and resumes after a person solves it.
* The next benchmark batch shows fewer challenge and `/sorry` pages than bench3-2026-10-23, the baseline.

### Constraint check

None of the above, as far as I can tell.
