Add tests to tests/unit/control_plane/test_issue_run_auto_merge.py, using its existing helpers (_checking, _read, _merge_workflows, writes.check; extend _checking so the 'review' and the re-review task can each be given a verdict.json): (a) the review says NOT_YET, the fix runs, the re-review says MERGE, CI is green -> the run submits one merge workflow (today: FAILED 'NOT_YET, not MERGE'); (b) the re-review still says NOT_YET -> FAILED with 'NOT_YET, not MERGE' and no merge workflow; (c) the review says MERGE and the re-review step re-publishes that MERGE -> merges; (d) a run whose stored workflow has no re-review step (compiled before this change) still reads the 'review' step's verdict. Add compile tests (in tests/unit/control_plane/test_issue_run_keyword.py beside test_a_staged_plan_compiles_to_one_review_after_every_step_and_one_integrator, or a new tests/unit/control_plane/test_issue_run_rereview.py) asserting that both a chain plan and a staged plan compile to ... -> review -> fix -> re-review, the re-review gated {step: review, verdict_in: [NOT_YET]}, builds_on fix, input_from review's verdict.json by parent, runner_profile equal to the review's, prompt starting with REREVIEW_PREAMBLE, and that the fix is still the integrator (resolve_integrator_step) so the re-review never publishes. Update test_a_staged_plan_compiles_to_one_review_after_every_step_and_one_integrator and any other test that counts compiled steps; do not weaken what they assert …

title: runner-fallback's judge has never minted its token since 2026-10-23, so SELF_HOSTED_CI is never flipped back
body:
### What happened

`runner-fallback.yml`'s `judge` job has failed on every scheduled run since at least 2026-10-23 05:48Z, at the step "mint the merge App's token for the variable", with `The permissions requested are not granted to this installation`. So the judge never runs, and `SELF_HOSTED_CI` is never flipped to `off` when the self-hosted pool stops picking up jobs (or back `on` when it recovers). The fallback this workflow exists for is not working.

The same step also logs: `Unexpected input(s) 'permission-variables'`. The pinned `actions/create-github-app-token` does not accept `permission-variables`, so the step does not ask for Variables: write the way the workflow assumes. What it requests instead is refused by the swarmcloud-merge App's installation.

### Severity

S2: CI resilience. Nothing is broken while the self-hosted runners work; when they stop, nothing flips the variable back and jobs queue until someone sets `SELF_HOSTED_CI=off` by hand.

### Where you saw it

GitHub Actions: `.github/workflows/runner-fallback.yml`, job `judge`.

### Environment

bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud, main. Merge App `swarmcloud-merge` (App ID 5157524).

### Steps to reproduce

1. `gh workflow run runner-fallback.yml --ref main`
2. Read the `judge` job's "mint the merge App's token for the variable" step.

### What you expected instead

The step mints a token that may write the `SELF_HOSTED_CI` repository variable, and the judge runs. That needs two things: an input the action accepts (or an action version that accepts `permission-variables`), and the App installation granted **Variables: write**. Either may be the missing half; this issue does not know which.

### Identifiers

- Scheduled runs failing the same way: 39907798990 (2026-10-23 05:48Z), 39939992330, 39978342016, 40011920920, 40034800742, 40048139865, 40067583019 (2026-10-24 05:46Z).
- Dispatched on main at 2026-10-24 08:09Z: run 40070696780, same error. That was after `MERGE_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` moved to environment `repo-secrets` (PR 2128) and was re-set; the key itself reads (a malformed key fails earlier, with `Invalid keyData`, as run 40068610214 did).

### Does it look like one of these?

A workflow-file change: any fix to `.github/workflows/runner-fallback.yml` is pushed by hand after BGD sees the diff. An App permission change is BGD's, on GitHub.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

```
##[warning]Unexpected input(s) 'permission-variables', valid inputs are ['app-id', 'private-key', 'owner', 'repositories', ... 'permission-workflows']
##[error]The permissions requested are not granted to this installation. - https://docs.github.com/rest/reference/apps#create-an-installation-access-token-for-an-app
```

### Anything else

Found by CLD while proving the repo-secrets switch-over (PR 2128), on 2026-10-24 08:09Z.

title: The pool parks every agent while six accounts' weekly windows sit under a 15% floor, and the accounts page reads as plenty
body:
### What happened

Read 2026-10-24 09:16Z (02:16 PDT). 60 eng tasks are parked: 28 on PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED (22 claude-code, 4 claude-code-browser, 2 indexer) and 32 later steps of the same workflows on DEPENDENCY_INCOMPLETE. Capacity › Accounts reads "7 accounts · 7 available" and shows 5-hour figures that look like plenty (devops-team "~40%").

Every one of the 28 parks carries the broker's own answer: `account_pool_reason: no_account_available`, provider anthropic, `next_eligible_at` 10:09-10:10Z.

**Why:** `quota_broker.accounts.choose()` hands a new agent an account only when its BINDING window (the fullest) has at least `DEFAULT_ASSIGN_FLOOR = 0.15` remaining. Read from `GET /v1/accounts` at the same time (observed 1-11 min before):

| account | 5-hour | 7-day (left) | 7-day resets | blocked by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ai-eng-2 | reset 08:39Z | 86% (14%) | Oct 25 18:59Z | 7-day |
| ai-eng-3 | reset 03:20Z | 97% (3%) | Oct 27 10:59Z | 7-day |
| aieng-claude1 | **99%**, resets 10:10Z | 39% (61%) | Oct 30 14:00Z | 5-hour |
| devops-main | reset 04:59Z | 88% (12%) | Oct 26 14:59Z | 7-day |
| devops-team | reset 04:20Z | 86% (14%) | Oct 28 12:00Z | 7-day |
| saga-personal | reset 06:00Z | 98% (2%) | Oct 26 07:59Z | 7-day |
| team | reset 05:59Z | 98% (2%) | Oct 26 08:00Z | 7-day |

So the pool is out of WEEKLY quota on six of seven accounts. The 5-hour figures the page shows with `~` belong to windows that have already reset.

### Severity

S1: every pool-credentialed agent in eng (and the tenants these accounts are lent to) is stopped until 10:10Z, and then the pool runs on one account until Oct 25.

### Where you saw it

Capacity › Accounts (`/capacity/accounts?account=eng%3Adevops-team`); the waiting line "Provider quota exhausted on anthropic; until 10:10Z".

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), tenant eng, main at a62643c2.

### Steps to reproduce

`GET /v1/tasks?state=PARKED`, then each task's `quota_exhausted` event (`account_pool_reason`), against `GET /v1/accounts` windows.

### What you expected instead

The accounts page says which accounts can take a new agent, which window blocks each and when it clears. The waiting line names the pool and the account, not "provider quota". And the pool never stampedes one account when it frees up.

### Identifiers

Sample park: task_1f5b717a56c34a36a768 (lease, container, clone, a 49 MB checkpoint, then the broker's no, then park).

### Does it look like one of these?

Capacity accounting and the account pool.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

See the table above and the findings below.

### Anything else

**Findings beyond the floor**
1. **eng:team appears to be saga-personal registered twice.** Identical readings (5-hour 0.11, 7-day 0.98) with resets one second apart, and eng:team still carries an old extra window (`harbor_lantern`, reset Oct 15). Meanwhile claudeswitch's **saga-team** (7-day 35%) is in no pool.
2. **The pool's accounts are claudeswitch's accounts.** Laptop sessions and SwarmCloud lanes spend the same weekly windows.
3. **Nothing caps agents per account** (`choose()` docstring). The wake sweep (`_prewarm`, 10 per pass) promotes every due park without asking whether an account can take it. So at 10:10Z every waiting agent lands on aieng-claude1.
4. **Admission leases and starts a container before the pool is asked** (`scheduler/credentials.py`: "WHAT IT DOES NOT ASK: whether an account has room now"). Each wait costs a container, a clone and a 49 MB checkpoint.
5. **The waiting line says "Provider quota exhausted on anthropic"** although the reason is the pool's floor, with a known account and instant.
6. **The floor is hard-coded** (`DEFAULT_ASSIGN_FLOOR`), shared by the broker and the scheduler (`from quota_broker.accounts import choose`).

**BGD's decisions, 2026-10-24 09:16Z (02:16 PDT)**
- eng:team is removed and added again as **saga-team**. BGD signs in; nothing passes through a session.
- **Per-window floors:** 5-hour stays **15%**, 7-day becomes **5%**.
- **Until the per-account cap ships, `provider:anthropic:tenant:eng` hard_limit is 6** (was 100; effective 50). Set by CLD at 09:15Z through `PUT /v1/admin/limits/provider/anthropic/tenant/eng`. **Restore to 100 when the cap is deployed.**
- Fix lanes, each below.

**Plan**
- **POOL-FLOORS-CAP** (quota-broker `accounts.py`, `main.py`): per-window floors (5-hour 0.15, 7-day 0.05); a per-account agent cap (`max_agents`, default 6, settable per account by an admin) that `choose()` and `eligibility()` respect; and `GET /v1/accounts` carries, per account, whether it can take a new agent, what blocks it (window, remaining, floor, or full at N of M) and when that clears.
- **POOL-WAKE-GATE** (scheduler, after the above): wake only as many parked agents as accounts can take, gated on `choose()`. Admission asks the pool before leasing a pool-credentialed task, so no container starts just to park. The waiting line names the blocking account, window and instant.
- **POOL-DUP-DETECT** (quota-broker, after POOL-FLOORS-CAP): record each account's Anthropic identity at add and refresh; refuse a second registration of one subscription and flag existing ones.
- **Capacity › Accounts:** "N of 7 can take a new agent · next: …", per-account block and clear time, reset windows shown as reset, unknown windows labelled, and a weekly burn forecast. This is a changed page, so it gets competing mock-ups first (BGD's standing rule), then the build.

comments.body:
**Lanes for the rest of the plan, chained 2026-10-24T09:24Z** (each runs implement → review → fix in SwarmCloud):

- [ ] **POOL-ACCOUNT-CAP**: per-account `max_agents` (default 6, admin-settable); `choose()` skips a full account; `eligibility()` answers `accounts_full`; the worker parks on it as a quota wait; GET /v1/accounts gains `can_take_new_agent`, `blocked_by`, `next_eligible_at`, `max_agents`. Starts when POOL-WINDOW-FLOORS (PR 2223) merges.
- [ ] **POOL-WAKE-GATE**: the due-park sweep and `release_dependants` promote at most the pool's free slots, oldest first; admission parks a pool-credentialed task before leasing when no account can take it (no container, clone or checkpoint spent); the waiting line names the account, window and instant. After POOL-ACCOUNT-CAP.
- [ ] **POOL-DUP-DETECT**: the broker records an opaque provider identity at add and refresh, refuses an add that matches an existing account, flags two existing accounts that share one and hands out only the older. Falls back to identical-readings detection if the provider gives no identity. After POOL-ACCOUNT-CAP.
- [ ] **ACCOUNTS-MOCKUPS-A..D**: four competing Capacity › Accounts proposals (A Answer first, B Timeline, C Window grid, D Account cards and forecast) on the browser runner, merge off; BGD picks one on a local picks page, then the build lane is written. After POOL-ACCOUNT-CAP.

**Held:** `provider:anthropic:tenant:eng` stays at 6 (set 09:15Z) until POOL-ACCOUNT-CAP and POOL-WAKE-GATE are deployed; then CLD restores it to 100.
**BGD's step, still open:** re-add eng:team signed in as saga-team (`uv run sc account remove team`, then `uv run sc account add --label team --lend-to smoke --lend-to u-bogdan`).

**Finding, read 09:43Z 2026-10-24 in the console and claude.ai:**
- eng:team is gone, and **eng:saga-team** was registered in its place ("never given out", lending off: the old loans to smoke and u-bogdan are gone).
- It reads **7-day 98%, clears 46h 17m**, the same as eng:saga-personal. claudeswitch reads the real saga-team subscription at **36%** weekly, so this registration is the Personal subscription again.

comments.body:
**Measured 10:40Z 2026-10-24, after POOL-WINDOW-FLOORS (PR 2223) released** (release run 40082382522, success at 10:25Z):
- [x] **Agents start again.** Assigned went from 0 (09:24Z, with 28 waiting) to 6, which is eng's limit. At 10:38Z they were on aieng-claude1 (4: its 5-hour window reset ~10:10Z, so it has the most headroom) and eng:saga-team (1).
- ai-eng-2, devops-main and devops-team hold none. They are assignable now, but `choose()` always takes the account with the most headroom first. That is the stampede POOL-ACCOUNT-CAP (per-account agent cap) addresses. The cap lane was submitted at 09:34Z, wf_86b6d874c36a47f69a79.

So it takes each new agent until the poller reads it, bounded today only by eng's limit of 6.

title: Artifact redaction masks a CSS class and code expressions as credentials, so a lane's patch read through the API cannot be applied
body:
### What happened Reading CONFIG-NAV's `swarm-work.patch` through `GET /v1/tasks/{id}/artifacts/content` (task_194160a8cba240e594c3) returned it with 6 redactions, all false positives: - the existing CSS class `sk-pscroll` (`apps/swarm-ui/src/Spine.tsx`, `styles.css`), masked as `sk-pscrol********`, as if it were an API key; - two `token: secretsLink.current` expressions in `App.tsx`; - `secrets: [], platform_credentials: {` in a test fixture. A patch read this way cannot be applied, and the raw object in GCS needs a gcloud sign-in an unattended session does not have. Recovering the lane needed six hand-restorations from context. ### Severity S3 — broken, but I found a workaround ### Where you saw it Not sure ### Environment Not sure ### Steps to reproduce 1. Read any artifact whose text contains `sk-pscroll` or `token: ` through the artifact content route (`swarm_artifact`, `SwarmClient.artifact_content`). 2. `redacted: true` and `redaction_count` > 0, with the masked text in place. ### What you expected instead The read-time redaction masks what looks like a credential's value, not a CSS class whose name starts with `sk-` or a code expression after `token:`. A false positive in a patch is worse than in a log, because it makes the patch unappliable. So the patch artifacts, at least, need a stricter rule. For example: an `sk-` token requires the provider's length and alphabet, and `token:` requires a quoted literal value. ### Identifiers - task_194160a8cba240e594c3, artifact `swarm-work.patch` (attempt att_86f8a041557d4d6c9bfc) - Read: 2026-10-24T13:28Z ### Does it look like one of these? _No response_ ### Screenshots, errors, logs ``` -

title: A check-only lane fails on an empty diff, so a rendered review that finds nothing to fix never becomes a verdict
body:
### What should change

A workflow whose implement step's job is to CHECK something can finish with no change when the check finds nothing to fix. That covers a rendered review of a PR that changed a page, or a "confirm and fix if broken" follow-up. Today the worker fails that step with `empty_diff`. Its review step never runs, so the evidence never becomes a verdict the merge step can use.

### Why

On 2026-10-24, COUNTS-MOCKUP-GUARD-RENDER (wf_8f732b1d5f8142969494) existed only to give PR 2235 the rendered review its merge needed. Its implement step rendered every frame in both themes at 1440 and 390, found no defect, and rightly changed nothing. The step failed (`expected outputs missing ... empty_diff`), review and fix were cancelled, and PR 2235 still carries its earlier NOT_YET. The evidence sits in an artifact (`review.md`) that no merge step reads.

### Options

- **A spec flag** (`allow_empty_diff: true` on the implement step, or a `verify` step kind): an empty diff is a success that publishes nothing, and the review step runs on the PR's current head.
- **A review-only workflow shape** for `publish_to_pr`: one review step on the browser runner whose MERGE verdict the PR's merge step accepts.

### Where

The worker's expected-outputs check (`swarm-work.patch` / `empty_diff`); the workflow spec for `publish_to_pr` lanes.

title: A step cannot run a repository's own Playwright suite: claude-code has no Chromium libraries and claude-code-browser's agent path is the live-browser stub
body:
### What happened

A workflow step cannot run a repository's own Playwright suite (`npx playwright test`) on either Claude profile. So a review step that needs the repository's Playwright tests cannot run them in SwarmCloud. Product Oracle reported it on 2026-10-24 with three tasks in tenant `eng`:

- **claude-code-browser**, `task_2791f0996eab4f958252` (step `suite-train-kl`, workflow `wf_5ef1a45816564e58a5a3`), last_error: "The suite did not run: the container cannot start Chromium (playwright install refused: su authentication failure, read-only file system)."
- **claude-code**, `task_69128d776a52467488e4` (step `review-520b`, workflow `wf_75297079c3f146cf831a`): "Executable doesn't exist". After `npx playwright install chromium`, Chromium cannot start: `libglib-2.0.so.0` is missing and the agent is not root.
- **claude-code**, `task_e97a6439de29456ba6ab` (`fix-520b`), got around it by unpacking Chromium's system libraries and fonts under `/tmp` (`LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `FONTCONFIG_FILE`). Without fonts the renderer crashes with `Skia FontConfig FATAL`.

**Cause, read from main** (CLD, 16:52Z). Each profile fails for its own reason.

1. **claude-code-browser: blocked by design.** The browser image installs Chromium and all of its system libraries at build time (`images/agent-runtime-browser/Dockerfile`: `playwright install --with-deps --no-shell chromium`, Playwright 1.63.0, under `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=/opt/playwright`). The pod runs with `readOnlyRootFilesystem: true` (`scheduler/dispatch.py`). When the live browser exists, BROWSER-ENFORCE (owner decision 2026-10-13, #1030) sets the agent's `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` to `/opt/swarm/live-browser-only`, a stub whose every launch fails and names the CDP endpoint (`runners/claude_code.py` `AGENT_BROWSERS_PATH`). The point is that the person watching sees the agent's browsing. A repository's `npx playwright test` launches its own headless Chromium, at the revision its own `@playwright/test` pins. That is exactly what the stub refuses, and a different revision has nowhere writable to go either.
2. **claude-code: no Chromium libraries.** `agent-runtime-base` installs none of them, and the agent is not root, so `install --with-deps` cannot add them.

### Severity

S1 — blocked: I cannot do the thing at all

### Where you saw it

Worker on GKE — browser (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-browser, kubernetes)

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), tenant eng, 2026-10-24. Reported by the Product Oracle session (`product-oracle-f2`).

### Steps to reproduce

1. Submit a step on `claude-code-browser` (or `claude-code`) on a repository whose tests use `@playwright/test`.
2. Have the step run `cd web && npm ci && npx playwright test`.
3. On claude-code-browser, launches fail on the live-browser stub or the read-only browsers path. On claude-code, the browser executable is missing, and once installed, `libglib-2.0.so.0` is missing.

### What you expected instead

A step can run a repository's own headless Playwright suite, with the Chromium revision that repository pins and the fonts and libraries Chromium needs. On claude-code-browser, the agent's own browsing should still go through the watched live browser.

### Identifiers

`task_2791f0996eab4f958252`, `task_69128d776a52467488e4`, `task_e97a6439de29456ba6ab`. Workflows `wf_5ef1a45816564e58a5a3` and `wf_75297079c3f146cf831a`.

### Does it look like one of these?

No. #1366 is the live browser being absent, which is a different fault.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Quoted above, from the tasks' last_error and the reporting session.

### Anything else

**Held for BGD: this needs an owner decision before a fix lane runs.** The candidate fixes:

- **(a) A test-suite exception on claude-code-browser.** The worker makes a writable `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` under the workspace for test runners only (seeded with symlinks to `/opt/playwright`), so `npx playwright install chromium` (never `--with-deps`: the libraries are already in the image) puts the repository's revision beside the bundled one. The agent's interactive browsing stays on the live browser. This relaxes BROWSER-ENFORCE for headless test processes, and the workspace is memory-backed tmpfs, so a Chromium download (~170 MB) costs memory.
- **(b) Chromium's system libraries and fonts in agent-runtime-base**, so claude-code can run a suite headless. Every claude-code image grows by Chromium's dependency set, and BROWSER-ENFORCE does not apply there.
- **(c) Both.**

Until then, the workaround `fix-520b` used is the only one that works: unpack the libraries and fonts under `/tmp`. Product Oracle runs its suite locally meanwhile.

A headless TEST process (`npx playwright test`) may launch its own Chromium from a writable browsers path in the work area. The agent's own browsing stays on the live browser (BROWSER-ENFORCE, #1030, unchanged). claude-code is unchanged. Lane **PW-TESTRUNNER** (`wf_e5f8606522d34ebab58c`) builds it with an attacker-lens review.

title: An owner-only merge hold on a schedule the owner last edited can be approved by no one, and a hold matched only on prompt mentions is never re-checked against the PR's files
body:
### What happened

On 2026-10-24 BGD pressed Approve on merge approval `apr_76e9cdc4800ea95c5609fd9b` in the console (https://swarm.saga.xyz/approvals/apr_76e9cdc4800ea95c5609fd9b). It was refused: "Not decided: the member who last changed this schedule's gate, scope or spec cannot approve its merge-tier items; another member must".

The approval gates issue run `run_52b61f4ac2d74a01a6c9` (#2179). Its PR, 2234, was green, and the review verdict was MERGE. The run's hold is `NEEDS_OWNER`, approvers `owner_only`, reasons `contract` and `workflows`. Two rules then leave nobody who may decide (`apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/approvals.py` `check_gate_approver`):
- `owner_only` admits only the platform owner, BGD.
- The second-person rule (`second_person_required`) bars the schedule's last editor from merge-tier items. The schedule is the failure-review `sch_54e9828e6772`, whose gate BGD last changed when he turned on its merge.

**The hold itself was a false positive.** PR 2234 changes only `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/gitops.py`, `lifecycle.py` and one test. The hold matched `apps/common/swarm_common` and `.github/workflows` from the plan's PROMPT, which says those must not be touched (`issueruns.py` `_PROMPT_PATH`: "the prompt is read for the paths too"). Nothing re-checks the hold against the PR's real files at merge time.

BGD had the PR merged on GitHub (labelled `ready` at 18:17Z) because the console could not decide it.

### Severity

S1 — blocked: I cannot do the thing at all

### Where you saw it

Web UI · Automate › Approvals (/approvals)

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), tenant eng, 2026-10-24.

### Steps to reproduce

1. The owner edits a merge-tier schedule's gate (here, the failure-review schedule's merge switch).
2. The schedule's issue run holds its merge `NEEDS_OWNER` (owner only).
3. The owner presses Approve: refused as the last editor. No other member is allowed by `owner_only`.

### What you expected instead

Every pending approval has at least one person who may decide it. Either an owner-only hold is decidable by the owner even when the owner last edited the schedule (recorded in the audit), or the hold names who may decide and the console says so. A hold set from prompt mentions alone should also be re-checked against the PR's changed files when the merge approval is requested, and clear when none matches.

### Identifiers

Approval `apr_76e9cdc4800ea95c5609fd9b`, run `run_52b61f4ac2d74a01a6c9`, schedule `sch_54e9828e6772`, PR 2234, issue #2179.

### Does it look like one of these?

No.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Refusal text, verbatim: "Not decided: the member who last changed this schedule's gate, scope or spec cannot approve its merge-tier items; another member must".

### Anything else

The console's message tells the owner that "another member must", but `owner_only` refuses every other member, so the advice cannot be followed.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**BGD's decision, 2026-10-24 18:18Z: "Owner may decide, audited".**

1. On an `owner_only` hold, the platform owner may decide even when he is the schedule's last editor. The decision is recorded in the audit as the second-person rule waived for the owner.
2. A hold matched only on prompt mentions is re-checked against the PR's changed files when the merge approval is requested, and clears when nothing matches.

Fix lane: **APPROVAL-OWNER-WAIVE**.

Lane APPROVAL-OWNER-NAMED (wf_529c03905cb54b958711) adds it to PR 2269.

title: For a tenant on the state routes (eng; dev.tfvars state_via_api_tenants), merge._own_doc reads the merge step's own task document with ctx.fetch_upstream(ctx.task_id), which AttemptState.upstream ref…
body:
<!-- failure-review fingerprint=fr-67795a1ca698 -->
### What happened

3 failure(s) in the window 2026-10-24T11:01:01.905864+00:00 to 2026-10-24T18:01:09.972294+00:00 share one cause: For a tenant on the state routes (eng; dev.tfvars state_via_api_tenants), merge._own_doc reads the merge step's own task document with ctx.fetch_upstream(ctx.task_id), which AttemptState.upstream refuses (its own id is in neither the declared set nor _derived_upstream). The bare `except Exception: return {}` then makes _rounds_asked 0 and _fix_rounds [], so merge._red refuses checks_failed on the first red reading instead of parking CI_FIX_PENDING for the lane's 2 CI-fix rounds. The red CI underneath was a stale red base for f-001 (fr-0be9f0179eb8), a missing UNCAPTURED_ROUTES entry for f-019 (fixed later by a ci-fix round, PR #2240 merged), and three swarm-ui tests broken by PR #2250 for f-027.

### Severity

S0 — a platform guarantee at risk (tenant isolation, the other team's resources, over-admission or a slot released under a running worker, a stale generation that ran, a secret printed)

### Where you saw it

Worker on Cloud Run (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-base)

### Environment

Not sure

### Steps to reproduce

Found by the failure-review schedule `sch_54e9828e6772`, firing `sch_54e9828e6772:29881080`, from the failures it reviewed: agent `task_74dc90722ad14b1a996a`; agent `task_b225bc6d0c744ffd8ebc`; agent `task_0da41bca79da4879b3f5`.

### What you expected instead

These agents end without this failure: the cause below is fixed in the code, with a test that fails before the fix and passes after it.

### Identifiers

- Fingerprint: `fr-67795a1ca698`
- Signature: `checks_failed: at <id>: ci-gate (<event>: failure)`
- Failures: agent `task_74dc90722ad14b1a996a`; agent `task_b225bc6d0c744ffd8ebc`; agent `task_0da41bca79da4879b3f5`

### Screenshots, errors, logs

- `sed -n 2269,2287p apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/merge.py`: _own_doc = _mapping(ctx.fetch_upstream(ctx.task_id)) under `except Exception: return {}`. _rounds_asked returns 0 when metadata has no merge_fix_rounds
- `sed -n 2560,2592p apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/merge.py (_red)`: waits CI_FIX_PENDING when len(rounds) < asked. It appends ', after <n> CI fix round(s)' only when asked > 0. None of the three last_errors carries that suffix, so asked was 0
- `sed -n 1651,1672p apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/attemptstate.py (AttemptState.upstream)`: declared = depends_on | input_from | dispatch.input_parents, plus _derived_upstream (index base, builds_on, verdict gate, workflow ancestors). The task's own id is not in any of them, so UpstreamNotDeclared is raised
- `child agent: workflow_view wf_c81d5b1a17344f73b9a8 + agent_events task_b225bc6d0c744ffd8ebc`: the merge failed 14:08:42Z about 17 s after the attempt started, with no CI_FIX_PENDING park. Server-side mergewake appended ci-fix:1 (task_92a11a18), which started 14:16Z after the merge had failed. It fixed the PR, and #2240 merged while the workflow stayed FAILED
- `child agent: run_list application.yml head_sha=96ed69e7 (f-001, PR #2225)`: push runs 40071118778 and 40085432797 failed only unit tests (1/9). pull_request run 40085435544 passed. The branch was cut 2 min after #2213 left main red (fr-0be9f0179eb8). PR #2225 later merged green
- `child agent: run_view 40106903052 / 40108185656 (f-027, PR #2250)`: qa.u12.shell.test.tsx:82 (/admin/limits -> /overview), limits.link.test.tsx:85 and spacing.admin help-glyph failed on both push and pull_request, a deterministic content failure a CI-fix round could have fixed
- `grep -n state_via_api_tenants terraform/environments/dev/dev.tfvars`: line 732: ["u-bogdan", "eng"]. The child agents found these tasks' documents and artifacts under tenants/eng
- `ref mapping`: Ref-to-task mapping: the digest numbers refs by completion time; agents_list (FAILED, CANCELLED; 2026-10-24) sorted by completed_at reproduces every group exactly (f-001 task_74dc9072 11:03Z ... f-028 task_6194cfde 17:59Z).

### Anything else

**Proposed fix.** Have the merge worker read its own task document through the attempt's own-task route, since AttemptState._own_task already loads it. Alternatively, let AttemptState.upstream serve attempt.task_id. Make _own_doc log a refused read instead of silently returning {}. Red first: in tests/unit/worker/test_state_reads.py, use a state client that refuses undeclared ids, a merge task with merge_fix_rounds=2 and a red required check. run_merge must park ci_fix_pending; today it refuses checks_failed. Pair it with a 200 case in tests/unit/control_plane/test_attemptstate.py for GET state/upstream of the caller's own task id.

**Files.** `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/merge.py`, `apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/attemptstate.py`, `tests/unit/worker/test_state_reads.py`, `tests/unit/control_plane/test_attemptstate.py`

Held for the owner (`needs-owner`, category `tenancy`): no fix run is started.

title: Gate._round computes one per-check timeout, min(CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600, remaining()-30), once per round and gives that full budget to each check _run_checks runs in sequence (changed-guards, ruff,…

### What happened

### SwarmCloud plan for #2274

**Approved** by automatic approval (`plan_approval: auto`) at 2026-10-25T00:06:11 UTC.

**Mode:** one agent · **Estimate:** 2 agent-hours · **Revision:** 1 · **Digest:** `sha256:71572a4fb47200310aef9916da3894ed2bcb5572fe29fd8367bcee2f6a0a8160`

The pre-publish gate (apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/prepublish.py) computes one per-check timeout per round in Gate._round -- max(30, min(CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600, remaining()-30)) -- and _run_checks hands that same value to every check it runs in sequence (changed-guards, ruff, pytest, vitest, tsc...). With 640 s left after the agent's end_turn, three or more checks could each take ~610 s, so the gate ran past the step's 3,600 s deadline, the runner was SIGKILLed (exit -9), no prepublish-checks.md was written, and the workflow's review/fix/re-review/merge were cancelled. The fix threads a deadline into run_checks/_run_checks: before each check, the budget is recomputed from the clock as min(CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, deadline - now - margin); once less than a minimum check budget is left, no further check is started and every remaining check is recorded as SKIPPED with a 'step budget ran out' reason (advisory, never sent to the fix prompt, like any other skipped check). Gate._round passes a deadline derived from self.remaining() and self.clock instead of a fixed timeout. The runner side (cliagent.py's gate_remaining) already gives the gate the step's true remaining budget, so cliagent.py needs no change; the step confirms that and leaves it alone, which also keeps the plan off the three open PRs editing that file. A red-first unit test with a fake clock and fake runner proves the total stays within 640 s and the third check is skipped.

#### Requirements
1. Each check the pre-publish gate runs gets a timeout computed from the time left when it starts, min(CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, deadline - now - margin), not one value computed once per round.
2. When less than a minimum budget is left, the gate stops starting checks and records the remaining checks as skipped for budget, with that reason.
3. The gate as a whole never runs past the step's deadline: with remaining()=640 s and three checks that each use their whole timeout, the total stays at or under 640 s and the third check is skipped (main gives about 1,800 s).
4. A tests/unit/worker test that runs the Gate with a fake clock and fake runner demonstrates this, failing on main and passing with the fix.
5. The agents named in the issue would end without the runner-timeout SIGKILL: the cause is fixed in code, with that test.

### SwarmCloud plan for #2276

**Approved** by automatic approval (`plan_approval: auto`) at 2026-10-25T00:08:05 UTC.

**Mode:** workflow · **Estimate:** 5 agent-hours · **Revision:** 1 · **Digest:** `sha256:45f3c433cd99213ea72f0b1cf923262c33be4367b34b2dfe3d768d6832b3dd82`

A CI-fix task (scripts/ci-fix.sh, metadata.ci_fix) can wait hours before it starts. Today the only check that the red commit is still the pull request's head happens when the fix is submitted (scripts/ci-fix.sh around line 357). Nothing checks again when the attempt starts. For PR #2224 this produced two failed fixes: one agent found nothing to change and failed published_nothing, and the other reset onto the old red sha and failed head_moved. The fix has three parts. (1) swarm-api copies the red head (pull_request, head_sha) from metadata.ci_fix into the SIGNED dispatch block. The worker acts on no unsigned metadata (lifecycle.py CONFLICT_ROUND_FIELD comment), so the work cannot be done in the worker alone. (2) The worker gets a start-time check. On a fresh clone of a task whose signed dispatch block carries that record, it compares head_sha with the commit it cloned from the continued branch, and reads the pull request through the forge. If the branch has moved past the red commit, or the PR is merged or closed, the attempt ends SUCCEEDED with no_change and a no_change_reason starting 'superseded'. That happens before any runner starts, through a functools.partial ending from _prepare, the same way _finish_nothing_to_change works. (3) The ci-fix.sh brief tells the agent to write verification.md when nothing needs changing, and never to check out or reset onto the red sha.

#### Requirements
1. At attempt start, a task carrying metadata.ci_fix compares ci_fix.head_sha with the continued branch's tip (the commit the clone started from).
2. At attempt start, the same task checks the pull request's state through the forge.
3. If the branch has moved past head_sha, or the PR is merged or closed, the attempt ends SUCCEEDED as no_change with a 'superseded' reason, and the agent never runs.
4. The scripts/ci-fix.sh brief tells the agent to write verification.md when nothing needs changing.
5. The scripts/ci-fix.sh brief tells the agent never to reset onto, or check out, the red sha.
6. Red first: a tests/unit/worker test where ci_fix.head_sha differs from the clone HEAD expects no agent run and a no_change result.
7. Red first: a tests/unit/scripts test asserts the brief names verification.md.
8. The two reviewed failures (published_nothing with no commits; HEAD moved off the task's branch) no longer happen for a superseded CI fix.

Step worker-superseded-at-start adds one early ending in _prepare and puts its logic in a new module, so the two edits are in different regions. Whichever lands second rebases. No other action.

Reuse the fixtures in tests/unit/control_plane/test_cifix_one_live_fix.py / test_cifix_fix_heads.py. Run scripts/related-tests.sh --run, then scripts/changed-guards.sh once at the end.

   </details>

2. **The worker ends a superseded CI fix SUCCEEDED no_change before the agent runs** (`worker-superseded-at-start`) — 2.5 agent-hours
   - files: `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/cifixstart.py`, `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py`, `docs/ci.md`, `tests/unit/worker/test_ci_fix_superseded_at_start.py`

One agent committed nothing and failed published_nothing. The other checked out refs/swarm/fetched/<red sha> and failed with HEAD moved. The previous step signs {pull_request, head_sha} into metadata.dispatch.ci_fix_head.

   Do this:

      - record(metadata) -> Record | None. It reads only metadata['dispatch'][FIELD] and raises WorkerError for a shape swarm-api could not have written (follow publishpr.target).

It returns a reason starting 'superseded: ' when: clone_commit is a full sha that differs from record.head_sha (the branch moved past the red commit); or pull is merged; or pull.state != 'open'; or pull.head_sha differs from head_sha. title: The console's QA credential form drops the link's environment, so no multi-entry target can be given a credential, and it discards the still-valid link after the refusal
body:
### What happened

The console's QA credential form cannot save a credential on any QA target that has more than one environment entry. It sends the PUT without the link's `environment`, so the API refuses with "this QA target has several environments; name the one to use". **The refusal still uses up the one-time link** ("The link is used; ask for a new one").

Measured 2026-10-25 00:41Z on SwarmCloud. A link minted with `POST /v1/qa-targets/qat_46d56b2eb9e81ecf/credential-links {"environment":"prod-user"}` opened the form "Test credential for ai-studio-prod". BGD typed the username and password and clicked Save credential. The form showed the refusal, and `GET /v1/qa-targets/qat_46d56b2eb9e81ecf` still reads prod-user's credential as not set.

Cause, read from main:
- `apps/swarm-ui/src/qaTargetsApi.ts` `qaCredentialLinkFrom()` reads only `t` from the link and never `environment`.
- `putQaCredential(id, username, password, linkToken)` has no environment argument, so `QaTargets.tsx` (line ~714) can't send one.
- The API side consumes the link before refusing for the missing entry, even though the link record already names the entry it was minted for.

The control: a single-entry target (the old `ai-studio-staging-routes`) saved through the same form on 2026-10-23, because the API needs no entry name there.

### Severity

S1 — blocked: I cannot do the thing at all

### Where you saw it

Web UI · Work › Repositories (/repositories) — now Config › Repositories › QA targets (`/config/repositories?page=qa-targets`)

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. Use a QA target with two or more `environments` (for example `ai-studio-prod`, `qat_46d56b2eb9e81ecf`).
2. Mint a link: `POST /v1/qa-targets/<id>/credential-links` with `{"environment": "<entry>"}`, and open its URL signed in as the minting admin.
3. Type a username and password and click Save credential.

### What you expected instead

The credential is stored on the entry the link was minted for. Concretely:
- The console reads `environment` from the link and sends it in the PUT. The challenge-bypass form gets the same fix.
- The API takes the entry from the link record when the body omits it. A link is already bound to one entry (qa-environments.md §1.4), so the request should never have to restate it.
- A refusal that isn't about the link itself (wrong or missing entry, validation) leaves the link usable.

### Identifiers

- target `qat_46d56b2eb9e81ecf` (ai-studio-prod, 5 entries) and `qat_063754a54a321aa5` (ai-studio-staging, 7 entries)
- entry `prod-user`; link minted at ~00:41Z on 2026-10-25, expiring 00:51Z

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Form alert, verbatim: "this QA target has several environments; name the one to use The link is used; ask for a new one to …"

### Anything else

This blocks all 12 per-role QA logins decided on #2136 (one QA user per AI Studio role on production and staging). No terminal path exists either: `sc` has no hidden-prompt command for a QA credential, unlike `sc key set`.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**Correction to "the refusal burns the link".** The API does not burn it. In `apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/qatargets.py`, `set_credential()` calls `_entry_of(current, environment)` before `consume_link()`, so the missing-entry refusal arrives with the link still unused.

The console is what throws the link away. `apps/swarm-ui/src/QaTargets.tsx` `submit()` calls `onSent()` after any response, under the comment "Sent once: the API consumed the link before it wrote". On every error it then shows "The link is used; ask for a new one to try again". That's true for a write that reached the store, and false for a refusal made before the link was checked (a missing or wrong entry, validation, a 403 on the link itself).

So the fix needs three things: send the link's entry, have the API take the entry from the link when the body omits it, and have the console keep the token after a refusal the API made before consuming the link.

title: The live browser paints over password fields, rule-matched text, the address bar and whole pages; BGD decided on 2026-10-25 it shows every frame as drawn
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Watch and drive an agent's browser in the live view and see the page exactly as Chromium draws it.

Today the live gate paints over parts of the screen before a frame leaves the pod (docs/design/live-browser.md §5.3, LB-3; `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/livegate/mask.py`, `observer.js`, `rfb.py` `masked()`):

* opaque boxes over every input that is or has ever been `type=password` and every input whose `autocomplete` names a credential;
* boxes over any visible text a `swarm_redaction` rule matches;
* the address bar, when the top frame's URL matches a rule;
* and, failing closed, the whole page area (`Outcome.PAGE_BLANKED`), a child frame's box, or the whole frame ("masking unavailable", `Outcome.UNAVAILABLE`) whenever a rectangle report is stale, missing or cannot be placed, with the strip saying "Can't show this page safely: …" or "Part of this page is covered: …".

**BGD decided on 2026-10-25 (06:00 UTC):** "Stop redacting elements or sections of the visual content that a browser agent or session displays via the live browser. There is no need to redact parts of the screen in any situation."

### What would you like to see?

Every frame the live view, the thumbnails and the recordings show is the screen as drawn: no box, no blanked page area, no covered frame, no "masking unavailable" frame, in any situation (a person holding control or not, any tab, any device preset, a challenge page or not).

What stays, because it is not visual redaction:

* the text redaction of logs, prompts, metadata, artifacts, the caption's path, hand-off reasons and Chromium's stderr (`swarm_redaction`), unchanged;
* nothing a person types, and no page content, is logged (§5.3.3), unchanged;
* the CAPTCHA hand-off the gate raises (`_on_challenge`, `SHOWN_IN_CONTROL`), the caption and tab following, which use the same gate-only CDP session, keep working;
* the QA identity is still scrubbed from everything the agent receives (that is a credential in requests, not pixels).

### Where would this live?

Agent worker · live gate (`apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/livegate/`); Web UI · Agent inspector's Browser tab, the live thumbnails, Recordings and the hand-off panel copy; docs/design/live-browser.md §5.3.

### How do you do it today?

There is no way to see a masked field or a blanked page. On ad-heavy pages and on iframe-heavy pages the page area has been blanked for minutes (#1030 LIVE-BLANK, #1344 DEVB-MASK, #1340), which the fail-closed rule causes.

### How would you know it worked?

* A unit test renders a page with a password field, a revealed password, rule-matching text and a token in the URL, and the published frame equals the captured frame pixel for pixel.
* A missing, stale or unplaceable rectangle report, a frame between tabs, and a child frame that never reports all publish the captured frame unchanged.
* No desktop name says "Can't show this page safely" or "Part of this page is covered".
* The CAPTCHA hand-off tests still pass.
* On SwarmCloud, a live view of a login page shows its password field's dots and the address bar as Chromium draws them.

### Constraint check

- None of the above, as far as I can tell.

title: One pool account's 429 halves the whole tenant's anthropic ceiling, and nothing records an account's rate-limit hits or errors
body:
### What happened

One pool account's rate limit halves the whole tenant's anthropic concurrency. `provider:anthropic:tenant:eng` read an adaptive target of 26 at 04:19 UTC on 2026-10-25; a single 429 at 04:40:57 UTC halved it to 13-14, and the pool sat full (14 of 14) with 100+ tasks queued while other pool accounts had room (saga-team 7-day 61%, aieng-claude1 59%).

The worker reports a provider outcome per (provider, tenant) only: `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/control.py` `report_provider_state` posts `/v1/quota/{provider}/{tenant}/rate-limit` with no account, and `apps/quota-broker/quota_broker/aimd.py` multiplies the tenant's `adaptive_target` by `multiplicative_decrease` (0.5) on every one. The climb back is +1 per 20 consecutive successes, so 14 -> 50 takes 720 successes with no 429 in between. On a subscription pool the account that hit its 5-hour or weekly window is already withheld by the broker's own window readings (S15), so halving the tenant punishes every other account for one account's window.

BGD reset eng's target to 50 by hand at 06:25:29 UTC through `PUT /v1/admin/quota/anthropic/eng/adaptive-target` (QUOTA-RESET).

### Severity

S2 — capacity accounting: the pool under-admits by half for hours after one account's limit.

### Where you saw it

Capacity › Pools (`provider:anthropic:tenant:eng` full at 14); the quota broker's AIMD.

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), tenant eng, 2026-10-25.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run more agents on the eng tenant than one pool account's 5-hour window allows.
2. That account's CLI gets a `rate_limit_event` REJECTED; the runner parks with PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED and the worker reports `rate-limit` for (anthropic, eng).
3. Read `GET /v1/admin/quota?tenant_id=eng`: `adaptive_target` has halved, though the other accounts are well inside their windows.

### What you expected instead

A 429 that comes from one pool account's window counts against that account (its hold, its windows, its health record) and does not halve the tenant's target. The tenant's target is halved only for API-key traffic (no pool account), or when every account the tenant may use is limited at once.

BGD also asked on 2026-10-25 for "more details about rate limit hits, error rates, error logs and other potential issues with the subscription accounts used and their health overall": each account needs a health record (rate-limit hits, errors by kind, refusals, re-auths, with times and short redacted messages) that the console can draw.

### Identifiers

- Release or CI run id: whatever was deployed at 2026-10-25 04:40 UTC
- `GET /v1/admin/quota?tenant_id=eng` at 06:03 UTC: `adaptive_target` 14, `configured_hard_max` 50, `last_429_at` 2026-10-25T04:40:57Z, `success_count` 16, `feeds_pool.effective_limit` 14, `active` 14, `available` 0. After the reset at 06:25 UTC: `effective_limit` 50, `active` 15, `available` 35.

- **Account 429s stop halving the tenant**, and every account keeps a health record (rate-limit hits, errors by kind, refusals, re-auths): lane ACCOUNT-429-SCOPE, wf_f0bb624fabe54826a2e1.

title: A merge step held by unanswered owner questions is shown as a browser sign-in, and its Ready button only re-parks it
body:
### What happened

A workflow's merge step that is held by unanswered owner questions is shown as a browser sign-in. The merge step (runner profile `merge`: git only, no model, no browser) parks `HUMAN_REQUIRED` while a lane's owner questions are open (apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/merge.py, "THE OWNER QUESTIONS THE REVIEW SAID HOLD IT", #2070). swarm-api describes every `HUMAN_REQUIRED` park the same way, `"Waiting for a person: sign in on its console page, then say it is ready"` (apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/waiting_detail.py `_human`, mirrored in apps/swarm-ui/src/api.ts), and the console opens the task's Browser tab (`/agents/live/<task>/browser`).

BGD asked on 2026-10-25 at ~07:38 UTC: "why a merge step in a workflow needs to use a browser agent and also needs user input to move forward?" on task_7ee2d99642c84dc0b3b2 (GA-MOVE-VIEWS' merge, held by 2 open questions). The same happened on task_ad66d2b402a847ca8b7d (ACCOUNT-429-SCOPE's merge, 3 open questions); someone pressed Ready at 07:32:52 UTC, which re-ran the merge, and it parked again because the questions were still open.

### Severity

S3 — misleading console: the owner is sent to a browser that does not exist instead of the questions that hold the merge.

### Where you saw it

Web UI · Agent inspector (a merge step's page and its Browser tab); `/sc check` ("PARKED on HUMAN_REQUIRED ... sign in on its console page").

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), tenant eng, 2026-10-25.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a workflow whose implement step writes questions.json and whose review lists them under `needs_owner`.
2. Let the merge step start before the questions are answered.
3. Open the merge task in the console.

### What you expected instead

A merge step held by owner questions says so: "Waiting for BGD's answers to N questions (implement: 2, fix: 1) before merging", lists the questions with their options and an answer control (the same one the console already offers for a task's owner questions), and links each to its asking task. No Browser tab, no "sign in", and no Ready button that only re-parks. A real hand-off park keeps today's copy.

### Identifiers

- Task id: task_7ee2d99642c84dc0b3b2, task_ad66d2b402a847ca8b7d
- Workflow id: wf_7548cc6f627f42769919, wf_f0bb624fabe54826a2e1

title: The sc plugin follows SwarmCloud work in a zero-token pane that mirrors the console's phases and loads agents and details only on click
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Follow SwarmCloud workflows and tasks from Claude Code without spending model tokens on it by default.

Today the sc plugin starts one Claude Code workflow run per SwarmCloud workflow with one model-driven row per step (plugin/workflows/run.js, plugin/agents/step.md and task.md), each row polling `swarm_follow` for as long as its step runs. Every running step costs tokens whether anyone is looking or not, and the rows don't mirror the console's stages.

### What would you like to see?

BGD, 2026-10-25:
- The plugin mirrors exactly the number and names of the phases (stages) the SwarmCloud console shows for a workflow.
- Each phase's status and the workflow's overall status are still tracked (phases done, duration, tokens), at the minimum token cost.
- Lazy loading: a workflow opens to its phases; selecting a phase loads its agents (name, state); opening an agent loads its details. Data is loaded and refreshed only on demand while browsing, never by default.

Decided the same day (08:10 UTC): a **SwarmCloud pane beside the chat** (a plugin mod pane that calls the sc plugin's MCP tools directly, so browsing costs zero model tokens) **plus one row per workflow** in /workflows so finishes are still noticed; **a toggle between today's layout and the new one** so both can be tried side by side; **mock-ups first** (lane SC-BROWSER-MOCKS), then build.

### Where would this live?

The sc Claude Code plugin (plugin/), as a mod pane and a changed /sc:swarmcloud workflow; no console change.

### How do you do it today?

One row per step in /workflows, each an agent that polls and spends tokens; or opening the console in a browser.

### How would you know it worked?

- With the new layout on, a session following 15 workflows spends no model tokens while nobody browses, beyond one row per workflow.
- A workflow's phases in the pane match the console's stages one for one, by name and count.
- Opening a phase or an agent makes exactly one sc tool call and no model call.
- The toggle switches between the two layouts without restarting the session.

### Constraint check

- None of the above, as far as I can tell.

title: A step's runtime is chosen by its submitter, never by what it needs: browser pods run no agent, implement steps on the browser fail, and UI reviews without one are forced NOT_YET
body:
### What happened

A step's runtime is chosen once by whoever submits it, never by what the step needs, and nothing measures whether a browser runtime was used. Measured by a read-only audit of tenant eng, 2026-10-24 07:45Z to 2026-10-25 07:45Z (757 tasks, 206 workflows, complete listing):

- 204 tasks ran on claude-code-browser. 53 implement steps there used 83% of browser unit-hours (69.5 of 83.4); 16 of 48 finished browser implements failed (6 memory kills, 9 timeouts, 1 empty diff), forcing 11 lanes into re-runs.
- 43 browser pods ran no agent at all: fix and re-review steps after a MERGE verdict. The control plane declined to publish all 69 MERGE fix steps in the window without a pod ("the step builds on no upstream branch", verdictpublish.py:641), and a re-review takes the review's profile by name (validation.py:2984) even when it only copies the staged verdict (lifecycle.py:7177).
- The reverse: 8 reviews of UI files ran on claude-code and were forced NOT_YET by the rendered-review gate (verdict.py:746, :776); each lane needed a follow-up -RENDER workflow (0.9 to 6.2 h of delay).
- The gate counts test files as UI (verdict.py:643), so a test-only change needed a render follow-up.
- Nothing counts browser calls beyond screenshots (runners/claude_code.py:1111, :1362), flags a browser step that never used its browser, or sums unused browser hours.

Where the choice is made: the plugin checks only that the profile name exists (apps/swarm-mcp/swarm_mcp/workflows.py:301), swarm-api accepts any available profile (swarm_api/validation.py:164), the scheduler adds the display container for any live-browser profile (scheduler/dispatch.py:791); the worker already measures a change's UI paths before a review starts (lifecycle.py:3371, :6909) but uses them only at the verdict. The issue-run planner hard-codes claude-code for every step (issueruns.py:224-225).

### Severity

S2 — capacity: browser capacity spent on steps that never used it, failed implements, and a follow-up lane per misprovisioned review.

### Where you saw it

Runtime audit, 2026-10-25 (per-task table kept by the operator); Capacity › Pools; the Agents page.

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), tenant eng, 2026-10-24/25.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Submit a lane whose review is on claude-code-browser and whose change touches only scheduler code: the review gets a browser pod it never uses.
2. Submit a lane whose review is on claude-code and whose change touches apps/swarm-ui: the review is forced NOT_YET.
3. Let any review say MERGE: the fix step still starts a pod.

### What you expected instead

BGD decided on 2026-10-25: only a review that needs to look at UI gets a browser ("if a review only does code review and a UI review or UI QA is not needed, it should not dispatch a review task with a browser runtime"). The platform should choose a review's runtime once the diff is known (browser only if the change touches UI, test files excluded); steps that run no agent should not start a pod; and every task should record whether its browser was used, with unused browser hours visible.

### Identifiers

- Release or CI run id: origin/main a14eb7ef9 (code references above)

Applied at once in the operator's lane generators (territory decides; the fix step depends on implement so a MERGE publishes without a pod; mock-up lanes opt in to a browser implement).

title: A person can ask to join a group workspace, and its admin decides it from Admin › People and roles (S5f)
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Let a person ask to join a group workspace, and let that workspace's admin answer from Admin › People and roles, as mock-up config-e.html frame S5f draws ("lee to join Example Labs").

### What would you like to see?

A join request: a person asks to join a group workspace they are not in; the workspace's admins see it as the grid's `requested` cell and in the page's lead ("who is waiting for an admin"), and approve or deny it. What approval does needs deciding in the design: membership of a group workspace is its Google group today, so approving either adds the person to the group (a Cloud Identity write the platform does not make today) or grants a platform-side membership beside the group.

BGD decided on 2026-10-25 (ADMIN-PEOPLE-ROLES' question, recorded on task_31ecaec218d1408a9c8d): "Later lane": file it, don't build it inside ADMIN-PEOPLE-ROLES.

### Where would this live?

Web UI · Admin › People and roles; swarm-api people routes; possibly Cloud Identity.

### How do you do it today?

A person asks an admin out of band, and the admin changes the Google group. The grid's `requested` cell shows only a person's request for their own personal workspace, which is a platform admin's to decide.

### How would you know it worked?

A person outside a group workspace can ask to join it; that workspace's admin sees the request in the grid's lead and decides it; the decision takes effect without anyone editing a Google group by hand (or the design says plainly why it must).

### Constraint check

- None of the above, as far as I can tell.

comments.author: bogdan-alexandrescu
comments.body:
**BGD's answers, 2026-10-25 11:02Z, to the six questions in docs/design/join-requests.md §7 (PR 2332, merged); all the recommended option, recorded on task_1b7fd78601294459b26f:**

1. Approval writes **(A) a platform-side membership beside the Google group** (signed, append-only), behind its switch, off. No Cloud Identity write, no IAM.
2. A person finds the workspace through **a join link with a per-workspace code** (off by default, rotatable, hashed at rest).
3. **That workspace's admins and platform admins** decide.
4. The approved person gets **the workspace default role**, which the approving admin may lower to viewer.
5. A request is **open 14 days**, and a decided one is **kept 90 days**. The audit row is permanent.
6. A membership **has no end date** and lasts until an admin removes it.

Build lanes from §6: JOIN-STORE and JOIN-INDEX are running now. JOIN-RESOLVE (security review) and JOIN-API start from STORE's PR. JOIN-BELL, JOIN-UI-ADMIN and JOIN-UI-PERSON start from API's PR. JOIN-DOCS-ACCEPT runs last.

title: The rendered-review gate counts UI files a lane merged in from main or its base PR as the lane's own
body:
### What happened

The worker's rendered-review gate (`apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/verdict.py` `ui_paths_in_patch` / `gate_rendered_review`) takes every `apps/swarm-ui/` or `docs/web-ui/` path in a lane's patch as a UI change the lane made. A lane that starts from another open PR's branch and runs `git merge origin/main` first, as BGD asked on 2026-10-25 so lanes run in parallel, carries main's and the base PR's UI files in its patch. Its code-only review on claude-code is then forced to NOT_YET with "not reviewed rendered", even though the lane changed no UI.

### Severity

S2: every code-only lane started from another PR's branch fails its merge and needs an owner waiver.

### Where you saw it

Lane merge steps (`verdict_not_merge`) on:
- RUNNER-ERROR-KINDS (PR 2334, from PR 2305's branch): 20 UI paths, 18 byte-identical to main and 2 inherited vitest files.
- MERGE-PARK-BELL (PR 2335, from PR 2324's branch): 10 UI paths. Its own commits b619f94 and d5d398d touch only apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/notifications.py and its test.

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), read 2026-10-25 10:41Z.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Start a code-only lane (no UI in its TERRITORY, so the review runs on claude-code) from an open PR's branch that changes UI files.
2. Have it `git merge origin/main` and change only API files.
3. The review's MERGE is recorded as NOT_YET "not reviewed rendered", and the merge step fails with `verdict_not_merge`.

### What you expected instead

The gate judges only the paths the lane itself changed: its own non-merge commits, measured against the commit it started from. A merge of main or of another branch brings nothing into `ui_paths`. The same rule should hold for the scheduler's runtime choice from a step's changed files (RUNTIME-BY-DIFF, PR 2329), so such a lane is neither sent to the browser nor forced to NOT_YET.

### Identifiers

task_8d593c38de5242ee82f1 (RUNNER-ERROR-KINDS review), task_f523a8b8aab2441d8349 (MERGE-PARK-BELL review); PRs 2334 and 2335.

### Does it look like one of these?

Part of #2322 (lane runtimes per step). Not a duplicate of RUNTIME-BY-DIFF: that decides the profile, and this is the gate's own path list.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

`verdict_not_merge: the review's verdict is NOT_YET, not MERGE (1 finding(s))`, with the finding `not reviewed rendered: ran on runner profile claude-code, not claude-code-browser; no image under shots/`.

### Anything else

BGD decided on 2026-10-25 10:41Z: waive the rendered review when CLD has verified that every UI path is inherited (recorded on both tasks), and fix the gate in lane GATE-OWN-PATHS.

title: _park_payload refunds attempt_count only for CHILDREN_INCOMPLETE, HUMAN_REQUIRED, release waits and CI_PENDING. A PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED park-and-exit therefore counts as a spent attempt. Four acco…
body:
<!-- failure-review fingerprint=fr-cf923874b60e -->
### What happened

5 failure(s) in the window 2026-10-24T23:01:01.747685+00:00 to 2026-10-25T06:01:01.747685+00:00 share one cause: _park_payload refunds attempt_count only for CHILDREN_INCOMPLETE, HUMAN_REQUIRED, release waits and CI_PENDING. A PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED park-and-exit therefore counts as a spent attempt. Four accounts_full parks, each 24-31 s and each dispatched by a 'prewarm' ready before the park's next_eligible_at, took task_c61ee787 to attempt_count 5 of max_attempts 3. Its first infrastructure loss, a node-memory-pressure eviction before the worker started (started_at null), was then final: detect.py's retries_exhausted said 'no attempts left'.

### Severity

S1 — blocked: I cannot do the thing at all

### Where you saw it

API — /v1, including sign-in and tenant resolution (apps/swarm-api)

### Environment

Not sure

### Steps to reproduce

Found by the failure-review schedule `sch_54e9828e6772`, firing `sch_54e9828e6772:29881800`, from the failures it reviewed: agent `task_c61ee787d5744b399762`; agent `task_0856b85b3c4749809128`; agent `task_961d56aa08cc48cc8f90`; agent `task_979b3bcbbb4e4aa7964f`; agent `task_e03bba19330d4c5fba01`.

### What you expected instead

These agents end without this failure: the cause below is fixed in the code, with a test that fails before the fix and passes after it.

### Identifiers

- Fingerprint: `fr-cf923874b60e`
- Signature: `reconciled: evicted: The node was low on resource: memory. Threshold quantity: <n>Mi, available: <n>Ki. (execution <id>); no attempts left`
- Failures: agent `task_c61ee787d5744b399762`; agent `task_0856b85b3c4749809128`; agent `task_961d56aa08cc48cc8f90`; agent `task_979b3bcbbb4e4aa7964f`; agent `task_e03bba19330d4c5fba01`

### Screenshots, errors, logs

- `agent_view task_c61ee787d5744b399762`: max_attempts 3, attempt_count 5. Generations 1-4 ran 24-31 s each and ended exit 75 'PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED'. Generation 5 has started_at null and 'reclaimed: evicted: The node was low on resource: memory ... no attempts left'
- `agent_events task_c61ee787d5744b399762`: each park is quota_exhausted with park_phase account_assign and account_pool_reason accounts_full, and the agent never ran (publish_reason 'the agent changed nothing'). Generations 2 and 3 were readied with reason 'prewarm' before was_eligible_at (04:24:07Z vs 04:25:36Z; 04:29:07Z vs 04:30:32Z), then parked again. generation_fenced comes 64 s after dispatch 5, finding worker_evicted
- `sed -n 1310,1395p apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/attemptstate.py`: `refund` is set only in the CHILDREN_INCOMPLETE, HUMAN_REQUIRED, release-wait and CI_PENDING branches. The else branch (PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED and the rest) never sets payload['attempt_count'] = attempt_count - 1
- `sed -n 1795,1830p apps/reconciler/reconciler/detect.py`: for a non-disk eviction, tail = 'no attempts left' if retries_exhausted(task.attempt_count, task.max_attempts), with no startup refund even when the evicted execution never started
- `issue_list 'quota park attempt_count refund' (all states)`: no issue

### Anything else

**Mode:** workflow · **Estimate:** 4 agent-hours · **Revision:** 1 · **Digest:** `sha256:057d8636e9d8a3d6de3a48bb8b4c82be465650082933b368579b1c0d001d5c9a`

The unit-test shard weights (tests/unit/scripts/unit_test_durations.json) are refreshed only by hand, and test_unit_shards.py::test_the_weights_name_test_files_and_cover_most_of_them asserts a hard 80% coverage floor, so when enough new test files land between refreshes main and every pull request built on it go red on the python-unit shard that runs that test (1069/1337 at 82638be8, until #2312 refreshed the weights). Stale weights never drop a file: scripts/lib/unit_shards.py gives an unweighted file the median weight. So staleness only unbalances shards, and it should not fail the gate. This plan does two things. (1) The coverage floor becomes report-only. `unit_shards.py count` computes the coverage and, below 80%, writes a `::warning` annotation and a step-summary line instead of failing. The unit test drops its hard floor, keeps the well-formedness checks, and adds a red-first test: in a temporary tree with 25% unweighted files the count/pick still succeed and no shard is over budget. (2) A scheduled, dispatchable workflow refreshes the weights automatically. It downloads the `unit-durations-*` artifacts from the newest green push run on main that uploaded them, merges them over the stored weights (measured values replace stored ones, files that no longer exist are dropped, unmeasured files keep their stored weight), and opens or updates a single pull request through the merge App's token so CI runs on it. docs/ci.md 'Refreshing the shard weights' is rewritten to describe both.

#### Requirements
1. A growing count of unweighted unit test files can no longer turn python-unit red on main or on pull requests: the 80% coverage floor is report-only (a warning), not a failing assertion.
2. A red-first test: a temporary tree where 25% of the test files are unweighted keeps the check green and still shards each part under budget (540 s). It fails against today's hard floor.
3. The weights file stays well-formed: keys name tests/unit/**.py files and values are positive numbers. These assertions stay hard.
4. The shard weights are refreshed automatically from main's green push runs' unit-durations artifacts by a scheduled (and dispatchable) workflow that opens or updates a pull request, with no manual step.
5. The refresh merge is tested offline: measured weights replace stored ones, deleted files are dropped, unmeasured existing files keep their weight, and the output is sorted, stable JSON.
6. docs/ci.md 'Refreshing the shard weights' describes the report-only floor and the automatic refresh, and why (#2364, failure-review fr-87a9244bfaef).
7. A test that fails before the fix and passes after it is committed alone first (red first), then the fix.

The merge step's suite reader, GitHubMerger.checks_at (apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/merge.py:917), lists commits/{sha}/check-runs. That list holds every check suite at the sha, from whichever branch pushed it. The only extra reader, _suite_events (merge.py:957), keeps just {check_suite_id: event}, and _event_group/latest_per_event then group runs by event alone. So when a sibling branch (swarm/task_43f879fb, run 40185474045) pushed the same commit edb9c942 that PR #2340's branch carries, its red push ci-gate stood as the PR's push result while the PR branch's own push run 40186863356 was still running, and merge._red refused checks_failed. The fix: _suite_events also reads each Actions run's head_branch, and checks_at takes the PR's head ref (the call site at merge.py:1763 passes pr.head_ref) and drops every check run whose suite was triggered by a push to a branch other than that head ref. Runs from pull_request and other events, commit statuses, and suites whose branch is unknown are kept as they are now. The Actions read currently happens only when some check name repeats. It now also happens whenever a check run at the sha has finished non-green, because a red sibling run can stand alone. A head where every check has one green run still costs no extra request, so test_a_single_run_per_check_reads_no_workflow_runs keeps holding. A 403 or 404 on actions/runs still means no event and no branch, which filters nothing and keeps the current grouping by check suite. ### SwarmCloud plan for #2366

**Approved** by automatic approval (`plan_approval: auto`) at 2026-10-25T18:08:04 UTC.

Two of the three failures (task_685bf392, task_7ee2d996: head_moved) are merge.py::_accept refusing a PR head the owner moved from a laptop while the merge step was parked HUMAN_REQUIRED. That refusal is by design and the issue asks for no change to it. The third (task_fa6637b0) is the hardening the issue offers: a conflict-fix round made one merge commit (the branch merged with main), the owner's hand merge 0626eadf then moved the branch by a merge of main, `gitops.base_merge_tip` accepted that tip, and `gitops.replay_onto_tip` (apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/gitops.py:4405-4408) refused the round's own merge commit with 'commit <id> is a merge and cannot be replayed', so the round ended publish_failed even though the moved tip already held what it did. The change: when replay_onto_tip meets a two-parent merge in the replayed span whose second (default-branch) parent is already an ancestor of the moved tip, it applies the merge against its first parent (`cherry-pick -m 1 --no-commit`) onto the tip. If the tree comes out the same as HEAD's, the merge is dropped like any other already-held commit, so a round whose only commit is that merge returns None and the existing lifecycle path (`_publish_onto_base_merge` -> BASE_MERGE_NO_CHANGE_FIELD -> `_no_change_after_publish`) ends it as no_change with nothing pushed. A merge whose second parent is not on the tip, a merge that conflicts there, or one that would add a change over the tip is still refused as today, after restoring HEAD. So a different resolution from the owner is never silently dropped, and no merge is ever turned into a linear commit. lifecycle.py is not changed: its None path already does the right thing.

#### Requirements
1. A conflict round whose single merge commit's main (default-branch) parent is already an ancestor of the moved tip ends with nothing to push (no_change), not publish_failed.
2. A test fails before the fix and passes after it: it reproduces the task_fa6637b0 shape (round merge commit, owner's hand merge of main moves the branch) and asserts no_change with nothing pushed.
3. A merge commit that the moved tip does not already hold (its default-branch parent is not on the tip, or its resolution would change the tip's tree, or it conflicts) is still refused, with nothing pushed or forced and HEAD restored.
4. merge.py::_accept's head_moved refusal of an owner push to a parked merge step's PR is left as it is: by design, per the issue's proposed fix.
5. The replay never rewrites a merge into a linear commit and never pushes over the moved tip with force or a lease.

#### Overlaps with open work

<!-- swarmcloud-issue-run:run_117cf54fc0f54671a862:plan -->
### SwarmCloud plan for #2367

**Approved** by automatic approval (`plan_approval: auto`) at 2026-10-25T18:46:10 UTC.

**Mode:** workflow · **Estimate:** 6 agent-hours · **Revision:** 1 · **Digest:** `sha256:deedf5131dec77dccb07ef470b0148019a3ae1e1a745164904b8dd0adafdd15e`

A CI-fix round continues a pull request's branch. When GitHub's "Update branch" merges main into that branch mid-run, the round's push is refused, and `_push_onto_base_merge` replays the round's commits onto the moved tip with `gitops.replay_onto_tip` (apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/gitops.py:4339). That replay drops a commit only when the cherry-pick leaves the tree unchanged. On any conflict it raises 'replaying commit ... conflicted' (gitops.py:4411), and the round ends publish_failed. This is what happened to four rounds on 2026-10-25. Each had hand-patched tests/unit/scripts/unit_test_durations.json, and main's #2312 rewrote that file and was merged into their branches. This change teaches the replay to recognise that its fix was superseded by the base. If every conflicted path of a cherry-pick is a path the base merge changed (`git diff --name-only <clone base> <tip>`), the replay takes the tip's version of those paths, records them, and goes on with the rest of the round. If nothing is left over the tip, the round ends as a SUCCEEDED no_change carrying a distinct `superseded_by_base` reason that names the paths and the tip, not publish_failed. If something is left, it is pushed as the existing fast-forward, after the authorship, leak and workflow-path checks that already run, and the superseded paths are recorded on the git record. A conflict in any path the base merge did not change, a merge commit in the span, or any other replay failure is still a GitError and publish_failed, as now. The second step does the issue's other proposal: neither the merge-wake tick (apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/mergewake.py `_on_red`) nor scripts/ci-fix.sh submits a CI-fix round when every failing check is also red at the default branch's own head. A round can only re-apply main's own fix by hand, and that is the race above. The tick waits on CI_PENDING for main to go green and update the branch. The script logs and comments that main is red on the same checks and passes without submitting. No frozen contract is touched. Invariants 1-10 are unaffected: no capacity, lease, fencing or dispatch path changes, and nothing is ever force-pushed.

#### Requirements
1. replay_onto_tip no longer raises 'conflicted' when every conflicted path of a replayed commit is a path the base merge (clone base..moved tip) changed; it resolves those paths to the tip's version and records them as superseded.
2. A round whose whole change is superseded by the base merge ends with a distinct superseded_by_base outcome (a no_change result naming the superseded paths and the moved tip), not publish_failed.
3. A round that is partly superseded still publishes its remaining change as a never-forced fast-forward onto the moved tip, after the existing authorship, leak-scan and workflow-path checks, and records which paths were superseded.
4. A replay conflict in a path the base merge did not change, a merge commit in the replayed span, or any other replay failure still pushes nothing and ends publish_failed with the 'base merge ... conflict' reason.
5. A red-first test in tests/unit/worker/test_continued_branch_moved_by_base_merge.py shows that a round editing file F, whose tip's base merge rewrote F, ends with the superseded outcome; it raised GitError / publish_failed before the fix.
6. The merge-wake tick does not submit a CI-fix round for a pull request whose failing checks are all red at the default branch's own head; it keeps waiting instead.
7. scripts/ci-fix.sh does not submit a PR-side CI-fix round when every failed job of the run is also failing at the default branch's head; it logs and comments why and exits 0.

#### Overlaps with open work
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2288](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/2288) (pull request): Open PR 'The CI-fix brief forbids moving onto the red sha' changes apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py (cifixstart path) and scripts/ci-fix.sh, both of which this plan edits: step replay-superseded edits `_push_onto_base_merge` / `_no_change_after_publish`, and step main-red-skip edits ci-fix.sh's submit path. The hunks are in different functions. Whichever lands second rebases onto the first; the engineer on main-red-skip must read #2288's ci-fix.sh diff and keep its brief changes.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2305](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/2305) (pull request): ACCOUNT-429-SCOPE changes apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py (account 429 reporting), not the publish/base-merge functions this plan edits. - [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2323](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/2323) (pull request): Changes tests/unit/scripts/unit_test_durations.json only, alongside mock-ups; this plan does not edit it.
