title: A merge step refuses the head its own conflict-fix or CI-fix round just pushed as head_moved, so four MERGE-verdict PRs on 2026-10-25 waited for a hand ready label
body:
### What happened

On 2026-10-25 four workflows whose review gave MERGE ended with their merge step FAILED `head_moved`, each refusing the head that **its own** fix round had pushed moments earlier. The merge step parked for that round (`conflict_fix_pending` or `checks_pending`), the round pushed and SUCCEEDED, the step woke, and it refused the round's head as foreign:

| PR | workflow | round | round pushed / succeeded | merge woke and failed | head refused |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2341 (SCHED-HISTORY-CSS) | wf_858cb62dfe664ebb96b8 | conflict-fix:1 task_9c2cea64d41d45809580 | 6a52d2b2 at 11:26:51Z, done 11:26:56Z | parked `conflict_fix_pending` 11:20:41Z, woke 11:27:09Z, failed 11:27:31Z | 6a52d2b2 (not e596dc7b, the head the workflow pushed) |
| 2343 (ADMIN-PEOPLE-FILTER) | wf_30cb76aa6a564c4aa984 | ci-fix:1 task_7131dcf3bb8f495cb6c1 | 8d6e2761, done 11:22:59Z | parked `checks_pending` 11:10:10Z, failed 11:23:28Z | 8d6e2761 (not 55bd8af5) |
| 2349 (QA-RUN-REMOVE) | wf_4a21e222924f4917a75a | conflict-fix:1 | done 12:35:18Z | parked `conflict_fix_pending` 12:32:29Z, failed 12:36:28Z | 6796bb49 (not e279fc2e) |
| 2352 (BROWSER-USE-UI) | wf_33bcbe22479e4c8692c0 | conflict-fix:1 task_030b303c54874269b0cf | done 13:02:28Z | parked `conflict_fix_pending` 13:00:18Z, failed 13:03:41Z | 70a8911f (not 41162218) |

Each refusal's own message says it checked "one of its CI-fix or conflict fix rounds' heads", so the round's head was not among `_fix_round_heads`' candidates. In each case the round's only commits were a merge of main (2341, 2349, 2352) or a one-line guard fix (2343, `signoutState.ts`).

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround

### Where you saw it

Worker on Cloud Run (apps/agent-worker, images/agent-runtime-base) — the merge runner, here on backend GKE_AUTOPILOT

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. A three-step lane (implement, review, fix; strategy `integrate`, merge `on_merge_verdict`) whose fix step publishes the PR from its own branch (`swarm/task_<fix task>`), with a MERGE verdict.
2. main moves so the PR conflicts (or CI goes red), and the merge step parks for a conflict-fix (or CI-fix) round.
3. The round merges main into the PR branch, pushes, and succeeds.
4. The merge step wakes and fails `head_moved` on the round's head.

### What you expected instead

The merge step accepts the head its own conflict-fix or CI-fix round pushed, re-reads the checks on it, and merges when they are green, as #1073 made it do for the PR-side CI fixer. The four PRs above were green and CLEAN at those heads and merged only after a hand `ready` label.

### Identifiers

- Merge tasks: task_c5b88bef0f6540bf9c16 (2341), task_3391685e5a7844ba85da (2343), task_68b1380d9fe140a19992 (2349), task_0526d58ce32c4acd8f4d (2352)
- Code: `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/merge.py` `_fix_round_heads()` (the candidate filter: skipped when the round's task is the target or the root, or when its signed dispatch `continues` is not `_branch_task(opener, target)`), called from merge.py:1414. Suspect: with strategy `integrate` the PR branch belongs to the fix step, so the round may `continue` a different task than the root this compares against. Not verified.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Merge task events for 2341, read 2026-10-25 ~00:10Z through `/v1/tasks/{id}/events`:

```
11:20:41 parked {"reason": "CI_PENDING", "code": "conflict_fix_pending", "pull_request": 2341, "head": "e596dc7b..."}
11:27:09 ready {"reason": "wake_requested"}
11:27:31 failed {"error": "head_moved: pull request #2341's head is 6a52d2b2190a..., not e596dc7b5580..., the head this workflow pushed, nor one of its CI-fix or conflict fix rounds' heads, ..."}
```

### Anything else

Not #2366 (an owner's laptop push to a parked branch) and not the closed #1073 (the PR-side CI fixer's head); this is the merge step's own conflict-fix and CI-fix rounds. A fourth lane, PR 2324 (MERGE-PARK-QUESTIONS), lost its CI-fix round to `publish_failed` (a replay over a main merge, task_6b5399d107cb45498a0d), which may share the root.

title: [epic] Failures 2026-10-25 14:44Z to 2026-10-26 00:44Z: 18 failures, each analysed one at a time, reported and fixed
body:
### Wave

Failures 2026-10-25 14:44Z – 2026-10-26 00:44Z (the ten hours before BGD asked, at ~00:45Z on 2026-10-26, for every failure to be analysed one at a time, reported in full, and fixed until all are covered).

### Where these findings came from

Read by CLD from the SwarmCloud API (tenant `eng`, every task that ended `FAILED` or `DEAD_LETTERED` in the window, with its attempts, its last events and its stderr tail, all as the API serves them, redacted) and from GitHub Actions (every workflow run that ended `failure` in the window, with its failed jobs and the error lines grepped from their logs). 5 SwarmCloud tasks and 13 Actions runs: **18 failures, one comment each below (F01–F18).** Nothing was filtered out by cause.

Each comment carries the evidence a container agent cannot fetch itself (it has no GitHub or SwarmCloud credentials). The analysis lane FAILURES-1026 reads them one at a time, finds each root cause in the code, and writes the report; fix lanes follow from it.

### Recorded elsewhere, deliberately not duplicated here

Work already in flight that some of these failures belong to (the analysis still analyses each failure on its own and says whether the work in flight covers it fully):

- **PR 2378**: two accounts tests (`accounts.timeline`, `accounts.addbutton`) pin `Date` to midday UTC, so main's UI tests stop failing every night after 22:00Z.

title: [epic] Visual QA pass 1 (2026-10-26): 57 console findings against the decided mock-ups, 3 major, 23 medium, 31 minor
body:
### Wave

Visual QA pass 1, 2026-10-26 (about 00:55Z to 02:00Z). BGD asked for a full, exhaustive visual QA of the console in Claude in Chrome against the decided mock-ups: find and fix every major, medium and minor finding that diverges from the mock-ups in a bad way or hurts the UX.

### Where these findings came from

A headless Claude-in-Chrome session on the live account walked every page of https://swarm.saga.xyz, read-only. It compared each page against docs/web-ui/mockups/*.html (the picked variants in PICKS.md) and BGD's later decisions on #2157, #2222, #2149, #2302, #1109 and #2158. Desktop ran at 1512x806 (the window would not resize to 1440x900); phone width used a same-origin 390px frame; both themes. It found **57: 3 major, 23 medium, 31 minor**, one comment each below (VQ-001 to VQ-057). Five are on areas still being built (`in_flight`) and are re-checked after they ship. Screenshot paths are Chrome's temporary files and may not last.

Not checked in pass 1: Platform counts' Over time readout (it needs a priced Run), the join-request screens (not shipped), Approvals with items (empty inbox), member and viewer views (another person's session), and dark theme on Runtimes, Holders, API reads, Provider quota, Repositories and one run page.

### Recorded elsewhere, deliberately not duplicated here

- Account health (VQ-034), GitHub access E-rest (VQ-038, VQ-039), Platform counts' one Run (VQ-050), and Admin People's filter and join requests (VQ-051) are in-flight lanes: ACCOUNT-HEALTH-PAGE-FIX3 (PR 2357), GA-MOVE-VIEWS (PR 2301) and GH-ACCESS-E-REST (PR 2346), COUNTS-ONE-RUN (PR 2348), and ADMIN-PEOPLE-FILTER (PR 2343) with JOIN-UI-ADMIN.
- Side observations, not findings: aieng-claude1 and saga-team are both signed in to "Saga · Team" with identical usage, and Model prices has no price for claude-haiku-5-5 or claude-sonnet-5-5.

title: Automate is redesigned from four fresh mock-up proposals in the Config E and Subscription accounts style: schedules, one schedule, a new schedule, approvals and one approval
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Redesign the console's **Automate** section completely, from fresh mock-ups. BGD, 2026-10-26: "lets redesign automate completely with fresh new mockups". Earlier, about one approval's page (https://swarm.saga.xyz/approvals/apr_31f74dc3dc84349da9b83697): "The UX/UI should follow the style we set in configs or subscription accounts but lets have some mockup proposals".

### What would you like to see?

Four competing, complete proposals (A-D), each covering every Automate screen in both themes and at phone width. Each is drawn in the house style BGD set in **Config E** (`docs/web-ui/mockups/config-e.html`, #2157) and **Subscription accounts A** (`docs/web-ui/mockups/accounts-a.html`, #2222). A picks page (Pick per frame, a "Copy my picks" tray) lets BGD mix frames across proposals, as on the account health picks (#2302).

The frames every proposal draws, under the same ids so picks can mix:
- **A1, Automate's landing:** schedules of every state (active, paused, paused by its spend tripwire, waiting on an approval, failing, never fired) and approvals waiting.
- **A2, one schedule:** what it does, its type and target, next firings, its firing history and outcomes, spend against its tripwire, its gates and approvers, and its actions.
- **A3, a new or edited schedule:** type and template, target, cadence, gates, budget, validation, and a preview of the next firings.
- **A4, Approvals:** waiting (oldest first, with expiry), decided (by whom), and expired, filtered by kind.
- **A5, one approval:** apr_31f74dc3dc84349da9b83697 is the canonical example. It is a `merge` approval for PR 2392, green at dbd00f06c5cd with 10 of 10 checks passed. It is held `NEEDS_OWNER` for reasons `workflows` and `shared` (matched `.github/workflows/unit-weights-refresh.yml` and `scripts/lib/common.sh`), approvers `owner_only`. The failure-review schedule's firing asked for it, with a run and issue #2364, and it expires in 3 days. Draw it pending, approved, denied, expired, superseded (head moved), and as seen by someone who may not decide.
- **A6, empty and honest states:** no schedules; Automate not served by the deployment; an unreadable read (a dash with its reason, never 0); nothing waiting.
- **A7, phone at 390:** A1, A2 and A5.

### Where would this live?

Automate › Schedules and Automate › Approvals: `apps/swarm-ui/src/Schedules.tsx`, `ScheduleDetail.tsx`, `ScheduleEdit.tsx`, `ScheduleHistoryTimeline.tsx`, `ScheduleTemplates.tsx`, `Approvals.tsx`, and Admin's `AdminSchedules.tsx` where it overlaps. Mock-ups go in `docs/web-ui/mockups/automate-a.html` to `automate-d.html` and `automate-picks.html`.

### How do you do it today?

Automate is two tabs, Schedules and Approvals (SD1, docs/schedules.md §6.1, 2026-10-08). The current schedules mock-up is `docs/web-ui/mockups/schedules.html` (#1109). Visual QA pass 1 (#2391) found Automate findings, and lane VQ-SCHEDULES is fixing them now. A redesign supersedes that work once BGD picks.

### How would you know it worked?

BGD picks frames on the picks page. The picks are recorded on this issue, and build lanes implement them with tests and a rendered review in both themes at desktop and phone.

### Constraint check

The rules that override every mock-up still apply (PICKS.md): a 12px type floor, no all-caps, a theme toggle, and an unknown figure as a dash with its reason, never 0. Every field a frame draws either exists in the API (`apps/swarm-api` schedules and approvals routes) or is listed as a new field the proposal needs. Approve and deny keep the approvers rule (`owner_only` etc.) and the expiry. Automate stays one section of the nav: whether it keeps two tabs is open to the proposals, which must say why if they change it.

title: The Outcomes headline read takes 22.6 s at p95 because its coverage and previous sections each fold the span again
body:
### What happened

Work › Timeline's Outcomes headline read, `GET /v1/outcomes`, takes **22.6 s at p95**. Visual QA pass 1 (#2391, finding VQ-021) recorded it as a blank Outcomes chart. Lane VQ-TIMELINE (PR 2419) made the chart draw from the cards' faster read, and the region now says what is still loading. The route itself is unchanged: the sealed days, the delta and the foot still wait on it.

VQ-TIMELINE's implement step (task_8934b2a2cee9418093ac) found the slow part is two sections the headline computes with reads of their own, in `apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/outcomes.py`:
- `coverage`: a count() per terminal state per workspace;
- `previous`: a second fold over the span before.

### Severity

S3. The page works but makes a reader wait about 20 seconds.

### Where you saw it

Work › Timeline › Outcomes (`GET /v1/outcomes`).

### Environment

SwarmCloud (swarm.saga.xyz), 2026-10-26. The p95 is the figure VQ-021 recorded; this issue does not re-measure it.

### Steps to reproduce

Open Work › Timeline › Outcomes with a default span and watch the headline read's time in the network panel.

### What you expected instead

The headline answers in about 2 s at p95. `coverage` and `previous` are cached, rolled up (`rollup_outcomes` in routes/admin.py already exists for rollups), or split into their own reads, so the first paint never waits on them. Every figure still states its coverage honestly: a section that is still being read or failed is a dash with its reason, never 0.

### Identifiers

VQ-021 (#2391) · VQ-TIMELINE task_8934b2a2cee9418093ac · PR 2419.

### Does it look like one of these?

The Outcomes design decisions are in `outcomes.py`'s header.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

None. The fix lane measures the route before and after (sections timed separately) and puts the numbers in its PR.

### Anything else

Found by visual QA; BGD asked on 2026-10-26 for every finding that hurts the experience to be fixed.

title: A step evicted for a full /tmp is not told what filled it, and nothing steers big scratch data to the 20 GiB cache volume
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Make a step that is evicted for a full disk volume say **what filled it**, and steer agents away from writing to a literal `/tmp`. Product Oracle's integration lane task_73850f24085447368991 (wf_6d886901f62e40c2a646) was evicted twice with `EmptyDir volume "tmp" exceeds 3Gi`, after about two hours each, and published nothing. It was not retried. Its /tmp held a Postgres 16 data dir (/tmp/pgdata), test logs (/tmp/tr) and Chromium's unpacked libs and fonts for Playwright. Reported by the product-oracle-f2 session, 2026-10-26.

### What would you like to see?

1. The eviction report (task last_error and the console) names the volume's largest paths at eviction time, for example the top 5 directories with sizes. Something like `/tmp/pgdata 2.1 GiB, /tmp/ms-playwright 0.7 GiB`, so the next run knows what to move.
2. The agent's prompt or environment tells it where large scratch data belongs: `$TMPDIR` / `$SWARM_CACHE_ROOT`, the 20 GiB network-disk cache that is never an eviction. Literal `/tmp` (3 GiB) and the workspace (5 GiB, checkpointed) are not the place for it. Set `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` under the cache root too, if it is not already.
3. Optional: the worker warns in the step log once literal `/tmp` passes about 2 GiB, before kubelet evicts.

### Where would this live?

The worker (agent_worker: eviction reporting and cachedirs.py's env) and the reconciler's eviction message. The sizes are in apps/scheduler/scheduler/dispatch.py's GKE_DISK.

### How do you do it today?

An eviction reports only `EmptyDir volume "tmp" exceeds 3Gi`. TMPDIR already points at the cache volume (cachedirs.py `cache_env`), but an agent or tool that names `/tmp` literally bypasses it.

### How would you know it worked?

A test evicts, or simulates evicting, a volume with known contents and asserts that the report names the largest paths. A step's environment carries the cache-root guidance and PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH under the cache.

### Constraint check

Raising /tmp is not free: a GKE pod's ephemeral storage is capped at 10 GiB by Autopilot (AUTOPILOT_MAX_EPHEMERAL_GIB). The standard class splits it workspace 5 + /tmp 3 + HOME 2, so /tmp can only grow by taking from the others. That is a sizing decision for the owner, not part of this issue. The cache volume (20 GiB) is outside that cap.

### SwarmCloud plan for #2436

**Approved** by automatic approval (`plan_approval: auto`) at 2026-10-26T12:12:06 UTC.

**Mode:** workflow · **Estimate:** 8 agent-hours · **Revision:** 1 · **Digest:** `sha256:bd75942e68f1061879c5b3c53e9fc52cc6c4119b91699bffed6ed68259483319`

Make a GKE step evicted for a full scratch volume say what filled it, and steer agents' big scratch data onto the 20 GiB cache volume. kubelet's local-storage eviction kills the pod with no grace period, so the worker cannot report at the moment of eviction. Instead it reports the last reading before it. (1) The GKE dispatcher, and the YAML templates kubernetes/render.py renders, tell the worker its local scratch volumes: their names, mounts and sizeLimits from GKE_DISK. The variable is SWARM_SCRATCH_VOLUMES. (2) On every heartbeat the worker takes a bounded size walk of those volumes. It puts the largest paths of each, top 5 with bytes, on the HEARTBEAT event as a `scratch` key. It logs a warning once in the step log when a volume passes two thirds of its limit (2 GiB of /tmp's 3 GiB). At that crossing it also writes an extra, out-of-cadence HEARTBEAT event, so the last reading before an eviction is recent. (3) When the reconciler repairs a disk-limit WORKER_EVICTED finding, it reads the attempt's events, as `_out_of_memory` already does. It then adds the evicted volume's largest paths from the newest reading to the reason. For example: `evicted: EmptyDir volume "tmp" exceeds 3Gi; largest at 10:41:12Z: /tmp/pgdata 2.1 GiB, /tmp/ms-playwright 0.7 GiB, ...`. That reason reaches the task's last_error and the attempt's error, which the console and swarm-mcp show. (4) cachedirs.cache_env sets PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH under the attempt's cache when the image or the live browser has not set it. The claude-code runner appends a short scratch note to the agent's prompt: put databases, test logs, unpacked libraries and fonts, and downloads under $TMPDIR (the cache volume, 20 GiB on GKE, never an eviction); never use literal /tmp (3 GiB, evicts the pod) or the workspace (5 GiB, checkpointed). Volume sizes are not changed: the /tmp sizing is the owner's decision and the issue places it outside this work.

#### Requirements
1. A step evicted for a full disk volume names that volume's largest paths, for example the top 5 with sizes, in the task's last_error.
2. The console shows the same report, through last_error and the attempt error it already reads.
3. The report reads as `<path> <size>` pairs, for example `/tmp/pgdata 2.1 GiB, /tmp/ms-playwright 0.7 GiB`, so the next run knows what to move.
4. The agent's prompt or environment says that large scratch data belongs under $TMPDIR / $SWARM_CACHE_ROOT (the 20 GiB cache volume, never an eviction), not under literal /tmp (3 GiB) or the workspace (5 GiB, checkpointed).
5. PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH points under the cache root when it is not already set (the browser image's /opt/playwright and the live-browser stub are kept).
6. Optional, delivered: the worker warns once in the step log when literal /tmp passes about 2 GiB, before kubelet evicts.
7. A test simulates evicting a volume with known contents and asserts that the report names its largest paths.
8. A test asserts that a step's environment carries the cache-root guidance and PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH under the cache.
9. Volume sizes (GKE_DISK, AUTOPILOT_MAX_EPHEMERAL_GIB) stay unchanged: raising /tmp is the owner's sizing decision, outside this issue.

#### Overlaps with open work
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2450](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/2450) (pull request): Changes apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py (Cloudflare Access token plumbing). Step worker-scratch-sampler adds one small hunk in the same file, in `_heartbeat`/`_usage_reading` and the attempt setup, which #2450 does not touch. Whichever lands second rebases. Nothing else is shared.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2370](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/2370) (pull request): Changes lifecycle.py (the CI-fix round on a red default branch) in different functions from this plan's heartbeat hunk. Whichever lands second rebases.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2288](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/2288) (pull request): Changes lifecycle.py (the CI-fix brief) in different functions from this plan's heartbeat hunk. Whichever lands second rebases.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2145](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/2145) (pull request): Changes lifecycle.py (`_push_through_broker` retry), away from `_heartbeat`. Whichever lands second rebases.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2335](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/2335) (pull request): Changes apps/swarm-ui/src/AgentDetail.tsx, a graph candidate. This plan does not touch the UI: the console already draws last_error, which carries the new report.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2279](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/2279) (pull request): #2279, #2148 and #2147 all edit runners/cliagent.py's platform paragraph. This plan puts its scratch note in runners/claude_code.py, beside RELATED_TESTS_NOTE, and leaves cliagent.py alone. cliagent already passes every AGENT_CACHE_ENV name on, so the new PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH entry needs no edit there.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2253](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/issues/2253) (issue): Related cause: claude-code has no Chromium libraries, which is why the evicted lane unpacked Chromium libs and fonts into /tmp. This plan only steers that data onto the cache volume. Shipping the libraries stays #2253's work.
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2402](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/pull/2402) (pull request): Edits handoff.py, livegate presets and docs/mirrored-values.md. If step scheduler-scratch-env records SWARM_SCRATCH_VOLUMES in docs/mirrored-values.md, whichever lands second rebases that doc. No code is shared.

#### Steps
1. **The GKE worker is told its local scratch volumes and their limits (SWARM_SCRATCH_VOLUMES)** (`scheduler-scratch-env`) — 1.5 agent-hours

   - tests, written first:
     - tests/unit/control_plane/test_dispatch_scratch_volumes.py::test_every_gke_class_names_its_disk_emptydirs_and_their_limits
     - tests/unit/control_plane/test_dispatch_scratch_volumes.py::test_cache_and_dshm_are_not_scratch_volumes
     - tests/unit/control_plane/test_dispatch_scratch_volumes.py::test_cloud_run_carries_no_scratch_volumes

   <details><summary>Instructions</summary>

   Issue #2436. The worker needs to know which of its paths are kubelet-limited local emptyDirs, and how big each limit is, so that it can report what filled one and warn before it evicts. Do NOT change any size: GKE_DISK and AUTOPILOT_MAX_EPHEMERAL_GIB stay as they are (the issue says /tmp sizing is the owner's decision).

   1. In apps/scheduler/scheduler/dispatch.py, add a constant SCRATCH_VOLUMES_ENV = "SWARM_SCRATCH_VOLUMES" next to CACHE_ROOT_ENV (around line 214-221). Use the same mirrored-name comment style: agent_worker's scratch module defines the same name.
   2. Add a pure function scratch_volumes_value(disk: GkeDisk) -> str. It renders the worker container's local disk volumes as `workspace=/workspace:5,tmp=/tmp:3,home=<WORKER_HOME>:2`: the kubelet volume name (the emptyDir's `name`, which is what kubelet's 'Usage of EmptyDir volume "<name>"' message says), its mountPath and its sizeLimit in GiB. Build it from the same constants the manifest uses (WORKSPACE_MOUNT, WORKER_HOME, the GkeDisk fields), so it cannot drift. Leave out the cache volume: it is a network disk and never an eviction. Leave out dshm: it is a memory tmpfs and counts against memory.
   3. Set it on the GKE worker container's env wherever CACHE_ROOT_ENV is set (`env[CACHE_ROOT_ENV] = CACHE_MOUNT`, around line 1657). It is GKE only, for the same reason. If that function does not see the resource class, set it in `GkeJobDispatcher._manifest`, where `gke_disk(rc)` is already in hand, and say why in a comment. Never set it on Cloud Run.
   4. The YAML templates kubernetes/worker-templates/worker-job.yaml, worker-job-v2.yaml and worker-job-browser.yaml each carry SWARM_CACHE_ROOT (around line 185). Add SWARM_SCRATCH_VOLUMES beside it, as a __SCRATCH_VOLUMES__ placeholder. In kubernetes/render.py's render_job, give it a value from the dispatcher's own scratch_volumes_value(gke_disk(rc)), and give it a constrained pattern in the placeholder-pattern table (render.py around line 367 refuses a placeholder without one).
   5. If docs/mirrored-values.md lists values mirrored between the dispatcher and the worker, add this one.

   Tests, written first:
   - tests/unit/control_plane/test_dispatch_scratch_volumes.py. For each resource class in GKE_DISK, the rendered GKE manifest's worker container carries SWARM_SCRATCH_VOLUMES. Its entries name exactly the manifest's own emptyDir volumes that are disk-backed (no medium) and mounted in the worker container, with matching mountPath and sizeLimit. The cache and dshm volumes are absent. A Cloud Run job's env does not carry it.
   - Extend tests/unit/worker/test_kubernetes_manifests.py: a rendered template carries the same value as the dispatcher for the same class.
   Run scripts/related-tests.sh --run for the changed files, then scripts/changed-guards.sh once.

   </details>

2. **The agent's environment and prompt steer big scratch data to $TMPDIR on the cache volume, and PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH goes under the cache** (`worker-scratch-guidance`) — 2 agent-hours
   - files: `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/cachedirs.py`, `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/workspace.py`, `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/runners/claude_code.py`, `tests/unit/worker/test_cache_scratch.py`, `tests/unit/worker/test_scratch_note.py`, `tests/unit/worker/test_image_env_reaches_the_runner.py`
   - tests, written first:
     - tests/unit/worker/test_cache_scratch.py::test_playwright_browsers_path_is_under_the_cache_when_the_image_sets_none
     - tests/unit/worker/test_cache_scratch.py::test_the_browser_images_playwright_path_is_kept

     - tests/unit/worker/test_scratch_note.py::test_the_cloud_run_note_does_not_promise_a_cache_volume

   <details><summary>Instructions</summary>

   Issue #2436, requirement 2. TMPDIR already points at the cache volume (cachedirs.cache_env), but the evicted lane wrote a Postgres data dir (/tmp/pgdata), test logs (/tmp/tr) and Chromium's unpacked libs and fonts to a literal /tmp, which is a 3 GiB emptyDir.

   1. apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/cachedirs.py: cache_env gives PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH = <cache>/ms-playwright, but ONLY when the worker's own environment has no PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH. Add a keyword parameter, for example `browsers_path_set: bool`, that the caller (Workspace.child_env) fills from os.environ. agent-runtime-browser sets it to /opt/playwright (read-only Chromium), and lifecycle's passthrough loop (lifecycle.py around 9125-9160) carries that value. The claude-code runner replaces it with AGENT_BROWSERS_PATH when the live browser exists (runners/claude_code.py around 368). Both must keep winning: read workspace.py's child_env and lifecycle's `_build_child_env` to confirm the order in which the two environments are merged, and test the browser-image case explicitly. Add `ms-playwright` to the directories create() makes if Playwright needs it to exist. Add the name to AGENT_CACHE_ENV, so cliagent's `_PLAIN_PASSTHROUGH` and generic's `_build_env` carry it to the agent without editing those files. Extend the module docstring with WHY: issue #2436, task_73850f24085447368991 evicted twice with `EmptyDir volume "tmp" exceeds 3Gi`.
   2. In cachedirs.py, add SCRATCH_NOTE(own_volume: bool) -> str, the one sentence an agent is told. On GKE (own_volume): 'Put large scratch data -- databases (e.g. a Postgres data directory), test logs, unpacked libraries and fonts, downloads -- under $TMPDIR, which is on the 20 GiB cache volume and never evicts the pod; never write it to a literal /tmp (3 GiB: past it the pod is evicted and the attempt lost) or to the workspace (5 GiB, checkpointed).' Read the sizes from dispatch's mirrored values if the worker has them (SWARM_SCRATCH_VOLUMES, from step scheduler-scratch-env; otherwise state the GKE_DISK standard sizes and CACHE_VOLUME_GIB as mirrored constants, with a comment naming dispatch.py). On Cloud Run, give a shorter sentence: $TMPDIR is inside the workspace tmpfs and counts against the memory limit.
   3. apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/runners/claude_code.py: append the note once after the prompt, in the same place and the same way as related_tests_note (around line 1336). Do it for every repository step on this runner, not only browser steps. Do NOT edit runners/cliagent.py: open PRs #2279, #2148 and #2147 rewrite its platform paragraph. If codex gets its notes from a different path, say so in the PR body rather than editing cliagent.py.

   Tests, written first:
   - tests/unit/worker/test_cache_scratch.py: on GKE, cache_env carries PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH under the cache when the image sets none. With the image's /opt/playwright present, the child env keeps /opt/playwright. AGENT_CACHE_ENV includes the name.
   - tests/unit/worker/test_scratch…

   </details>

3. **The worker samples its scratch volumes' largest paths onto HEARTBEAT events and warns once past two thirds of a limit** (`worker-scratch-sampler`) — 2.5 agent-hours
   - files: `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/scratchusage.py`, `apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py`, `tests/unit/worker/test_scratch_usage.py`, `tests/unit/worker/test_scratch_warning.py`
   - tests, written first:
     - tests/unit/worker/test_scratch_usage.py::test_sample_names_the_largest_paths_of_a_volume_with_known_contents
     - tests/unit/worker/test_scratch_usage.py::test_sample_descends_through_a_single_wrapper_directory
     - tests/unit/worker/test_scratch_usage.py::test_a_bounded_walk_says_it_is_partial
     - tests/unit/worker/test_scratch_usage.py::test_paths_are_cut_and_redacted
     - tests/unit/worker/test_scratch_warning.py::test_heartbeat_event_carries_the_scratch_reading
     - tests/unit/worker/test_scratch_warning.py::test_tmp_past_two_thirds_warns_once_and_emits_a_fresh_reading
     - tests/unit/worker/test_scratch_warning.py::test_nothing_is_sampled_without_scratch_volumes

   <details><summary>Instructions</summary>

   Issue #2436, requirements 1 and 3. kubelet evicts a pod past an emptyDir sizeLimit with no grace period, so the worker cannot report at the moment of eviction. It records the largest paths on every beat instead, and the reconciler reports the newest reading.

   1. New module apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/scratchusage.py. Its docstring records WHY: issue #2436, task_73850f24085447368991, kubelet's zero-grace local-storage eviction.
      - SCRATCH_VOLUMES_ENV = "SWARM_SCRATCH_VOLUMES" (mirrored from scheduler/dispatch.py; step scheduler-scratch-env sets it on GKE only), with parse_volumes(value) -> list of (name, mount Path, limit_bytes). It tolerates an absent or malformed value by returning [], so sampling is off on Cloud Run.
      - sample(volumes, *, top=5, max_entries=..., max_seconds=...) -> dict. For each volume it returns {name: {"used_bytes", "limit_bytes", "top": [[path, bytes], ...], "partial": bool}}. Count bytes as allocated blocks (st_blocks * 512), the way kubelet's du-style accounting does, with lstat and no symlinks followed. Hard links count once. Unreadable entries are skipped. The walk is bounded by an entry count and a wall time, and `partial` says whether it stopped early. To pick `top`, start at the mount. Descend into any directory that holds at least 90% of its parent's bytes (for example the single /workspace/<attempt> wrapper), at most 4 levels. Then list that level's 5 largest children by bytes. Each path is absolute, cut to 120 characters and passed through agent_worker.redact, so a path can never carry a credential onto an event.
      - format_top(entry) -> 'path 2.1 GiB, path 0.7 GiB' (one decimal, GiB/MiB). Keep it pure, because the tests and the step log use it.
      - warn_threshold(limit_bytes) = two thirds of the limit (2 GiB of /tmp's 3 GiB, the issue's 'about 2 GiB').
   2. apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py, kept to one small hunk (open PRs #2450, #2370, #2288 and #2145 edit other functions of this file):
      - Run the walk inside `_heartbeat` (around line 10462), not on another thread, at most once per beat. Read its cost and keep it cheap. Put the newest sample on every HEARTBEAT event as detail["scratch"], in `_usage_reading` or where the event is emitted.
      - The first time a volume's used_bytes passes warn_threshold, log a warning once per volume per attempt: `/tmp is at 2.2 GiB of its 3 GiB limit; past it kubelet evicts this pod. Largest: <format_top>. Move large scratch data under $TMPDIR (the cache volume).` Write it to the step log the console shows. Find how the worker's own lines reach that log (live stdout tail or the worker log) and use the same path. At the same moment, emit one extra HEARTBEAT event outside the every-5th cadence, carrying only {"scratch": ...}, so the reading the reconciler finds is at most one beat older than the eviction. Do the same again whenever a volume grows by another 10% of its limit past the threshold, so a fast fill keeps the reading fresh.
      - Ver…

   </details>

4. **A disk-limit eviction's reason names the evicted volume's largest paths from the attempt's last scratch reading** (`reconciler-eviction-report`) — 2 agent-hours
   - files: `apps/reconciler/reconciler/detect.py`, `apps/reconciler/reconciler/scratchreport.py`, `apps/reconciler/reconciler/repair.py`, `docs/execution-backends.md`, `tests/unit/control_plane/test_eviction_names_largest_paths.py`
   - tests, written first:
     - tests/unit/control_plane/test_eviction_names_largest_paths.py::test_a_tmp_eviction_names_the_largest_paths_of_the_last_reading
     - tests/unit/control_plane/test_eviction_names_largest_paths.py::test_readings_of_another_generation_are_ignored
     - tests/unit/control_plane/test_eviction_names_largest_paths.py::test_no_reading_leaves_the_reason_unchanged
     - tests/unit/control_plane/test_eviction_names_largest_paths.py::test_an_events_read_failure_never_blocks_the_repair
     - tests/unit/control_plane/test_eviction_names_largest_paths.py::test_node_pressure_eviction_gets_no_report
     - tests/unit/control_plane/test_eviction_names_largest_paths.py::test_second_disk_eviction_still_fails_and_names_paths

   <details><summary>Instructions</summary>

   Issue #2436, requirement 1. Today task_73850f24085447368991's last_error read only 'evicted: EmptyDir volume "tmp" exceeds 3Gi; evicted for disk 2 times: not retried again'.

   1. apps/reconciler/reconciler/detect.py: eviction_cause already parses kubelet's message (_LIMIT_EVICTIONS). Make the evicted volume's name (the `volume` group), or 'every volume' for a pod-level or container-level limit, available to the repair. Put it in the WORKER_EVICTED finding's detail (`detect_evicted`, around line 1829) as detail['volume'].
   2. Add a pure function to a reconciler module, for example detect.py or a new apps/reconciler/reconciler/scratchreport.py: scratch_report(events, *, attempt_id, generation, volume) -> str | None. It takes this attempt's events at this generation, filtered the way progress.assess filters them, and finds the newest HEARTBEAT event whose detail carries 'scratch'. It returns `largest at HH:MM:SSZ: /tmp/pgdata 2.1 GiB, /tmp/tr 0.6 GiB, ...` for the named volume, with at most 5 paths, the volume's used/limit bytes, and '(partial)' when the reading was partial. For a pod-level eviction it names the fullest volume's paths. It returns None when there is no reading. Do NOT import agent_worker: restate the event shape (detail['scratch'][name] = {used_bytes, limit_bytes, top: [[path, bytes]], partial}) as data, with a comment naming agent_worker/scratchusage.py, and make the formatting match scratchusage.format_top. Keep the whole result one bounded line, using the reconciler's _one_line/_short helpers.
   3. apps/reconciler/reconciler/repair.py: in the generic repair, around line 2005-2025, where `ended_why` and `_out_of_memory` already grow `finding.reason`, add this. When `finding.kind is FindingKind.WORKER_EVICTED and finding.detail.get('disk_limit')`, read `self._store.attempt_events(task_id, attempt_id)`, guarded by try/except and a logged warning the way `_out_of_memory` does it, and append '; ' + scratch_report(...) to the reason before the repair writes. The reason then reaches the task's last_error, the attempt's error and the events, through the existing writes, so the console and swarm-mcp show it with no UI change. Words only: the state decision, the count_disk_eviction rule, the fence and the release stay exactly as they are (invariants 3 and 5). Do not do this on dry_run.
   4. Docs: in docs/execution-backends.md, where disk evictions are described, add two sentences. One says the eviction reason now names the evicted volume's largest paths from the worker's last reading, which is at most one heartbeat old because kubelet gives no grace period. The other says big scratch data belongs under $TMPDIR on the cache volume.

   Tests, written first:
   - tests/unit/worker/test_worker_evicted.py, or a new tests/unit/control_plane/test_eviction_names_largest_paths.py if that is where the reconciler tests live. Simulate an eviction: build a snapshot whose termination says 'Usage of EmptyDir volume "tmp" exceeds the limit "3Gi"', plus an attempt…

   </details>

title: No release has deployed since 23:32Z: main's per-commit builds queue on GitHub-hosted runners, so every release times out waiting for its image build
body:
### What happened

**Nothing has deployed to SwarmCloud since 2026-10-25 23:32Z.** Release run 40245218405 (248fdf11d) was the last success. Read at 05:24Z on 2026-10-26:
- **Releases:** of the last 30 `release.yml` runs on main, 25 were cancelled, 3 failed and 2 are pending. The 4 failures since 00:23Z (40249148453, 40254486207, 40255378252, 40263856035) all failed in `images and scan (dev)` with `timed out after 2700s waiting for application.yml's 'build images' job for <sha>, which is still …`.
- **Queue:** 71 workflow runs are queued and 4 are in progress. Of the queued, **27 are `application` push runs on main**, the oldest queued since 01:40Z. Two main `application` runs had been in progress since 02:57Z and 03:03Z.
- **Runners:** the self-hosted `bogdan-ci` pool shows 45 runners, all busy. Main push jobs do not use that pool. The `runs-on` expression sends `push`/`workflow_dispatch` on `refs/heads/main` to GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-24.04` (since PR 1720). So main's builds queue behind the hosted concurrency limit.
- **Why it compounds:** `application.yml` runs one concurrency group per main commit, never cancelled (deliberate, see its comment). So every merge adds a full main run of about 25 jobs to the hosted queue. `release.yml` keeps one pending run per group, so each new merge replaces the pending release, and the one in progress waits 2700 s for its own commit's build, which has not reached a runner. With merges every few minutes, no release completes.
- **Knock-on:** the `auto-merge` workflow_run is itself queued, so labelled PRs merge late. The #2413 fix (PR 2421, merged 04:47Z), the curl CVE fix (PR 2410) and every visual QA fix are on main but not deployed.

### Severity

S1. The deploy pipeline is stalled. No guarantee is broken, but nothing merged since 23:32Z reaches SwarmCloud.

### Where you saw it

GitHub Actions: release.yml and application.yml on main.

### Environment

bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud main; SELF_HOSTED_CI=on; read 2026-10-26 05:24Z.

### Steps to reproduce

Merge PRs to main every few minutes for an hour while the self-hosted pool is busy with PR runs.

### What you expected instead

A release completes within about an hour of the newest merge, so main stays deployable during a burst of merges.

### Identifiers

Releases: 40245218405 (last success), 40263856035 (newest failure), 40269875205 (in progress at 05:24Z, waits for 45a7840ca's build). Newest main: 4d1a746c7 (application run 40272121131, queued).

### Does it look like one of these?

No duplicate found. Related decisions: the owner's runner routing (2026-10-14, PR 1720), and application.yml's per-commit group on main (2026-09-24).

### Screenshots, errors, logs

`##[error]timed out after 2700s waiting for application.yml's 'build images' job for 00a69830f86c114a7a1291881a50b34112d5723f, which is still …` (release 40263856035).

### Anything else

**Options (all change workflow files, so they are the owner's):**
1. **Route main's push jobs that hold no cloud identity to the self-hosted pool** (cap 100), keeping only the id-token jobs hosted. This removes main's tests from the hosted queue, and the release waits only on the build.
2. **Build only the newest main commit, then release that:** skip, or cancel when superseded, main runs for commits a newer commit has replaced, and make release.yml promote the newest built commit rather than its own. This has to keep the 2026-09-24 guarantee, that a release never waits for a commit that was never built.
3. **Skip main's test jobs when the identical tree already passed on its PR** (the build-images job already skips them this way). Main then only builds.
4. Short term: cancel the queued intermediate main `application` runs, keeping the newest commit's. CLD tried this at 05:24Z and the auto-mode classifier refused it as interfering with workloads, so it is the owner's to run or allow.

title: Parked merges keep their Claude Code rows polling for hours, outlive a hand-merged PR, and wake on any answer
body:
### What happened

As of 2026-10-26 07:38Z, seven workflows of this session showed in Claude Code as running for 5-7 hours. All of them were on their final step, the merge, and every earlier step had SUCCEEDED between 01:14Z and 04:09Z. Each merge step was PARKED HUMAN_REQUIRED because its review named owner questions that hold the merge (#2070). That much is by design, and the merges hold no capacity (invariant 1). Five things around the design are wrong:

1. **The Claude Code row never ends.** The sc plugin's merge row calls `swarm_follow` with a 30-minute hold for as long as the step stays parked (`stop: false`). It writes a line only on a change, so the panel shows "PARKED · waiting 7s" for hours. Each row ran 27-35 follow calls and 0.32-0.46M tokens. One row's 30-minute holds came back in about 3 s each (119 calls in 2h14m, 2.1M tokens). After it died, the run's result phase attached a duplicate row for the same step. About 4.4M tokens were spent in total.
2. **A merged PR does not end its merge step.** JOIN-UI-ADMIN's PR 2387 was merged by hand at 07:25Z. Its merge step stayed PARKED on an owner question. The owner-question park is spared by the human-wait expiry, so nothing would ever have ended it.
3. ~~The review's list and the hold disagree.~~ **Corrected 08:4xZ: they agree.** FAILURES-1026's review lists implement Q0, Q1, Q3, Q5 and Q6 in `verdict.needs_owner`, exactly the questions the merge parked on. Q2 and Q4 are its `open_questions`, the non-blocking list `merge.py` only posts on the pull request. The operator (CLD) read `open_questions` as the holding list, so F16 (Q6) never reached the owner. That is an operator error, not a platform defect.
4. **The served text is the browser hand-off's.** "Waiting for a person: sign in on its console page, then say it is ready" is shown for an owner-question hold. MERGE-PARK-QUESTIONS (PR 2324) fixes this. It merged at 23:57Z, 25 minutes after the last successful release (#2438).
5. **A woken merge ignores what the answer says.** `merge.py _answered` only checks that `owner_answers` holds the index. An answer that picks an option the PR did not build wakes the merge, and the PR merges as built. VQ-CAPACITY (PR 2414), VQ-CONFIG-B (PR 2411) and BROWSER-POOL-100 (PR 2389) had their workflows cancelled by hand so the picks could be built first.

### Severity

S2

### Where you saw it

Claude Code /workflows panel (sc plugin rows); console agent page of a parked merge step; workflow merge steps.

### Environment

SwarmCloud (eng), deployed release 248fdf11d (2026-10-25 23:32Z); sc plugin 0.5.49.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a five-step lane (implement, review, fix, re-review, merge) whose implement step asks an owner question the review names as needs_owner.
2. Attach it with `/sc attach <wf>` and leave the question unanswered.
3. Watch the merge row in /workflows. Then merge the PR by hand and watch the merge step.

### What you expected instead

1. A row whose step parks for a person ends, with the questions and an answer link. `/sc check` re-attaches it when the step resumes.
2. A parked merge whose PR merged or closed outside the workflow finishes, SUCCEEDED "merged outside the workflow" or CANCELLED.
3. (No platform change: the hold already equals `verdict.needs_owner`.) The operator queues owner questions from the merge step's own hold (`blocked_by[].owner_questions`), never from a review summary.
4. The hold says which questions it waits for (fixed on main; waits on deploy).
5. An answer that picks an option the PR did not build holds the merge and sends a fix round, instead of merging the unbuilt option.

### Identifiers

- Workflow ids: wf_98a86b7bd13e4dc6b55c (VQ-CONFIG-B), wf_205ab892741d479d8371 (VQ-CAPACITY), wf_3daa29296b3e4c91bc77 (VQ-AGENTS), wf_41878a8c91734d84bb10 (QA-FLOWS-CAP), wf_cfafdf7162b64f48af00 (BROWSER-POOL-100), wf_605fdb48d07d4016ba89 (FIX-2253), wf_e34648f9dc7040d78e3e (FAILURES-1026), wf_2c9717e85f1545c0ad50 (JOIN-UI-ADMIN)
- Merge task ids: task_f0451f1448694209b2ee (FAILURES-1026 hold), task_8d5dd6b8827b4dcf8b0e (JOIN-UI-ADMIN)
- Claude Code run with the collapsed holds: wf_dad54c2c-2dd (row agent-a038beebb162ddeb9)

### Screenshots, errors, logs

The VQ-CONFIG-B merge row's progress lines: 02:29Z "PARKED · waits: Waiting on 2 upstream steps"; 03:04Z DISPATCHED; 03:05Z "PARKED · waiting 7s · waits: Waiting for a person: sign in on its console page". After that, `changed: false` on every 30-minute call until 07:35Z.

title: AI Studio's lanes need to render their own branch, pass Cloudflare Access with a service token, and run CodeRabbit
body:
### What are you trying to do?

The AI Studio session (ai-studio-9d) runs visual-conformance lanes on SwarmCloud for sagaxyz/ai-studio. Its lanes need to:
1. see their own UI before they finish;
2. reach the Galatia platform admin, which sits behind Cloudflare Access with 2FA;
3. run the local CodeRabbit review that the repository's rules ask for on risky lanes.

BGD approved all three on 2026-10-26 (08:5xZ). He also approved read-only access to sagaxyz/agents-backend for eng, which CLD granted the same hour. agents-backend is now registered in eng with a read grant and `readable_by_tasks`, no merge policy and no workflow files.

### What would you like to see?

- **IMPLEMENT-RENDER.** A UI lane's implement step, in any repository, renders its own branch on claude-code-browser (desktop 1440 and phone 380/390, light and dark) and compares each render with the repository's frame PNGs (`swarm-handoff compare`) before it finishes. The doc tells lane authors how to serve their app without sign-in.
- **CF-ACCESS-TOKEN.** A Cloudflare Access service token in a workspace secret slot, scoped to a host list, sent by the browser runner as `CF-Access-Client-Id` / `CF-Access-Client-Secret` headers to listed hosts only. The agent never sees the values. BGD creates and stores the token.
- **CODERABBIT-IMAGE.** The coderabbit CLI, pinned and checksummed, in the claude-code image. Its API key comes from a workspace secret slot BGD sets, exposed only to the agent process and redacted.

### Where would this live?

Browser runner and swarm-handoff (images/, apps/agent-worker/), workspace secrets, the claude-code image, docs/.

### How do you do it today?

- **Self-render:** lanes check UI only through rendered-HTML tests. After merge, a staging re-check found 28 of 52 desktop rows and 12 of 34 phone rows still wrong, plus 6 new regressions.
- **Cloudflare Access:** not possible; agents cannot pass 2FA.
- **CodeRabbit:** not possible; the CLI is absent from the runner images.

### How would you know it worked?

- An AI Studio implement step attaches compare scores and diff images for every frame it touched.
- A visual-QA step opens the platform admin with the token while the token appears nowhere in its environment or tool results.
- `coderabbit review` runs in a claude-code step whose workspace has the key set.

### Constraint check

No credential in the repository, tfvars, a Job environment or a log. Tokens live only in Secret Manager slots that BGD sets, and both secret lanes get a security review (invariant 9: per-tenant secrets).

title: A lane step that merges main cannot publish once main has changed a workflow file, because -m lists main's files as the branch's
body:
### What happened

A lane step that merges main into its branch cannot publish once main has changed a workflow file since the branch was cut. The worker's workflow-file guard lists main's own `.github/workflows/*` changes as the branch's, through the merge commit, and routes the push to swarm-api's `git_push_branch`. That call failed both times, so nothing was pushed and the step ended FAILED with its work in `workflow-lines.patch`.

Twice on 2026-10-26, both after PR 2446 (which changed `application.yml` and `release.yml`) merged:

- **task_1297d8f422484ecdac7e** (ci-fix, workflow wf_693d5d7f0053400aa847) on PR 2446's own branch. It made no change of its own.
- **task_f2b7285633584cb4b1c0** (conflict-fix, workflow wf_1def49dabc4943c38926) on PR 2451 (ANSWER-CONTENT-CHECK). Its merge of main resolved two additive conflicts, in `merge.py` and `docs/merge-step.md`. The operator redid the same merge by hand and pushed it as d2634efc8: `git diff --stat origin/main d2634efc8` names no workflow file.

Both refusals read: "refusing to publish: the branch touches .github/workflows/application.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml, which only swarm-api's git_push_branch may push (agent-autonomy.md §3.3), and it answered api_unavailable: the platform did not answer; ask again."

**Cause, read in the code.** `lifecycle._workflow_paths` (agent-worker) and `gittools._workflow_paths` (swarm-api, around line 1356) both run `git log --format= --name-only --no-renames -m <tip> --not <base>`. With `-m`, a merge commit is diffed against EACH parent. Against the branch parent, a merge of main lists every file main changed, workflow files included, though the merge's result equals main's for those files.

### Severity

S3 — broken, but I found a workaround (the operator merges main by hand and pushes)

### Where you saw it

SwarmCloud worker (agent-worker publish), swarm-api gittools

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a lane PR whose branch predates a main commit that changes `.github/workflows/*`.
2. Run a CI-fix or conflict-fix step on it that merges `origin/main` into the branch.
3. The publish lists main's workflow files as touched, routes the push to `git_push_branch`, and fails. The step ends FAILED with `workflow-lines.patch`.

### What you expected instead

A merge of main counts as touching a workflow file only where its result differs from main's for that file: a conflict resolution in it, or a change the branch itself made. `--diff-merges=combined` (`-c`) lists a merge's files only where the result differs from every parent. That gives this rule for merge commits, and non-merge commits keep today's listing. The worker and swarm-api must change together; their docstrings say the two must never disagree about which route a branch takes. A test should hold it: a branch with a main merge that brings in a workflow change publishes through the worker's own push. Separately, `git_push_branch` answering `api_unavailable` on both calls deserves a look: no exception class is in the step's summary.

### Identifiers

- Task id: task_1297d8f422484ecdac7e, task_f2b7285633584cb4b1c0
- Workflow id: wf_693d5d7f0053400aa847, wf_1def49dabc4943c38926
- Attempt id: att_64678a41bda148fc8abb, att_d4eb651149e44ee9a354
- Release or CI run id: PR 2446 merged before both; PR 2451 hand-merged as d2634efc8

### Does it look like one of these?

Two places disagree about one value (a mirrored copy drifted): no. Both copies agree, and both use `-m`.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

The step summaries are quoted above. Read at 2026-10-26T11:38Z.

### SwarmCloud plan for #2452

**Approved** by bogdan at 2026-10-27T00:16:16 UTC.

The push then goes to git_push_branch, which answered api_unavailable both times, and the step ends FAILED with workflow-lines.patch. The fix switches both listings, together, to `--diff-merges=combined` (-c), as the issue asks. A merge then names a workflow file only where its result differs from every parent; non-merge commits list exactly as before. Real-git tests hold the worker and swarm-api to that rule and to each other, and a branch that merges main publishes through the worker's own push. Step two works out why git_push_branch answered api_unavailable (worker gittools.GitToolTools.call maps any retryable ChildApiError to the bare message 'the platform did not answer; ask again'). It fixes the swarm-api side if a merge bundle makes it fail, and puts the HTTP status or code in the refusal so a step summary names it. Step three handles the second comment: merge step task_219f6017 refused PR 2460's head 8a73a93cd as head_moved. So the step must first establish what pushed 8a73a93cd. If swarm-api's git_push_branch pushed it for a task, the merge step must accept a head swarm-api recorded (record_tip) for a task of the same branch, under the same signed-fact checks as _fixer_head. If it was a hand push, that is #2505's subject, and the step records the evidence instead of building a second mechanism. One known consequence of -c: a merge whose result keeps a workflow file version the branch already pushed earlier, where main changed that file, is not listed, so the worker's own push carries it. Step one must pin that behaviour in a test and in docs/runner-git-tools.md. GitHub may refuse such a push for workflow scope; the existing PUBLISH_FAILED path then fails the step without losing the work.

#### Requirements
1. A merge of the default branch counts as touching a workflow or action file only where the merge's result differs from every parent (a conflict resolution in it, or a change of the branch's own), via `--diff-merges=combined`.
2. Non-merge commits keep today's listing (every path they add, change, delete or rename away under .github/workflows/ or .github/actions/).
3. The worker's lifecycle._workflow_paths and swarm-api's gittools._workflow_paths change together and run the same listing, so they never disagree about which route a branch takes; their docstrings and docs/runner-git-tools.md say so.

5. Investigate why git_push_branch answered api_unavailable on both failing calls, fix the cause if it is in swarm-api's handling of a merge bundle, and make the refusal carry its cause (status/code), since no exception class reached the step summary.
6. Find out what pushed 8a73a93cd onto PR 2460. The merge step must count a head that swarm-api's git_push_branch pushed for its own workflow's task as one of its own heads, instead of refusing it head_moved.

title: A runner's duration counts only the agent run after an account swap, and nothing records what the swap cost
body:
### What happened

Two lanes hit the 7,200 s runner timeout on 2026-10-26. In both, the task's runner summary says the agent ran about 4,600 s. That reads as if about 42 minutes of the attempt were spent outside the agent, and the operator reported it to BGD that way. That was wrong. The events show the agent ran the whole attempt:

| task | agent_started | account swap | killed | runner duration_s |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| task_0a5cac0cd0fc45db8c6b (IMPLEMENT-RENDER) | 09:07:00 | 09:49:03, eng:ai-eng-2 exhausted, to eng:ai-eng-1-max | 11:06:52 | 4,657.8 |
| task_952b00e6dc7e4dbb8c6c (GITHUB-ACCESS-S2B) | 09:07:11 | 09:50:13, same swap | 11:07:08 | 4,598.3 |

At about 42 minutes in, the account ran out of quota (`swap_reason: exhausted`). The worker moved to another account, which restarted the agent CLI. `duration_s` counts only the run after the swap (11:07 − 09:50 ≈ 4,615 s).

Two things follow:

1. **The duration misleads.** A reader cannot tell an account swap from idle time.
2. **Nothing records what a swap costs.** Both lanes timed out, but the time and tokens the restarted agent spent re-reading its context are not measured anywhere.

### Severity

S2 — wrong data on screen or in the API (states, counts, capacity, costs, timings) — I can't trust what it says

### Where you saw it

Worker on GKE (apps/agent-worker); the task's result summary, as served by swarm_result and the console's Details

### Environment

dev — https://swarm.saga.xyz

### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a long claude-code step on an account close to its 5-hour quota.
2. When the account is exhausted mid-run, the worker swaps the account (`account_assigned`, `swap_reason: exhausted`) and the agent restarts.
3. Read the task's result: `outputs.duration_s` is the last run only.

### What you expected instead

- The attempt's runner summary counts every agent run: total duration, the number of runs, and each swap (when, from which account, to which, why).
- Each run records its own duration and tokens, so the cost of a swap is measurable.
- The console's Details shows the swap.

BGD decided on 2026-10-26 to fix the duration and to measure what a swap costs. Whether to resume in place, or to swap at a turn boundary, is a later decision, made on those numbers.

### Identifiers

- Task id: task_0a5cac0cd0fc45db8c6b, task_952b00e6dc7e4dbb8c6c
- Attempt id: att_16d7d3e5737d4f94aed1, att_bd0707bad34b4b57a2ab

### Does it look like one of these?

A `0`, `$0` or "real zero" where the true answer is *we don't know*: a near relative. A partial count is shown as the whole.

### Screenshots, errors, logs

Events read through GET /v1/tasks/{id}/events at 2026-10-26T12:49Z.

title: An agent's spend has no limit; a workspace default in tokens or dollars, lowered per step and capped by the platform, should stop it
body:
### What are you trying to do?

Put a hard limit on how much one agent can spend, set in tokens or in dollars, so a runaway step stops instead of burning a pool account. Today nothing stops one. The only limit is the step's timeout, and on 2026-10-26 four steps ran their full 7,200 s. One of them spent two hours with its CPU pegged and $2.34 of model use, and others swapped accounts mid-run on exhausted quota (#2457).

### What would you like to see?

BGD's decisions, 2026-10-26 at about 13:18Z:

- **Where it is set: the workspace default, which a step can only lower.**
  - A **workspace admin** sets a per-agent budget on the workspace's Settings, as a token count or a dollar amount, with the unit chosen per workspace.
  - A **spec step** may set a lower `budget` (`{usd: N}` or `{tokens: N}`), the way it sets `timeout_seconds` today. A step can never raise it.
  - A **platform admin** sets a ceiling that no workspace default can exceed.
  - An attempt's budget is min(step, workspace, ceiling). With mixed units, each limit is checked on its own.
- **At the limit: warn at 80%, then stop and keep the work.**
  - At 80% the agent is told to finish and publish, and the console shows an amber "budget 80%" on the agent.
  - At 100% the worker stops the agent at its next turn boundary, checkpoints, publishes what it has, and ends the step FAILED with the end cause `budget_exceeded`. The work is kept and the step can be resumed.
- **Default: off until a workspace admin sets one.** Nothing changes for running work, or for a workspace that sets nothing.
- **Dollars** are the API-price estimate SwarmCloud already reports as `cost_usd`, since the pool accounts are Claude subscriptions. **Tokens** are counted from the runner's own usage reports: input plus output, with cache reads counted as the runner reports them.
- Every Claude-model profile is covered, plus codex wherever it reports usage.

### Where would this live?

- swarm-api: the workspace setting, the platform ceiling, the spec step's `budget` validation, and the resolution.
- agent-worker: enforcement from the runner's usage stream.
- The console: Settings, platform settings, and the agent's row and Details.

### How do you do it today?

There is no per-agent limit. Schedules carry tripwires (failure review and visual QA `per_run_usd`), and nothing stops a step.

### How would you know it worked?

- A step with `budget: {usd: 1}` in a workspace with no default is warned at $0.80 and stopped at $1.00 at a turn boundary. Its branch is published, and it ends FAILED `budget_exceeded`.
- A workspace default of 15M tokens stops an agent at 15M.
- A step budget above the workspace default is refused at submission.
- A workspace default above the platform ceiling is refused on save.
- With no default and no step budget, nothing changes.

### Constraint check

Invariant 10: a step's `budget` only LOWERS a limit and never chooses resources, as `timeout_seconds` does today. Any new field the frozen contract needs (the step's `budget`, the end cause `budget_exceeded`, or the setting's shape) is a request in docs/contract-change-requests.md for BGD, never a code change. Invariant 1 holds: a stopped step holds no capacity.

title: A step whose MCP credential expired while it waited fails at once, though its caller could supply a fresh one
body:
### What should change

A step whose workflow's MCP credential expired while the step waited (parked or queued) parks CREDENTIAL_MISSING (`detail.credential: "mcp"`, `code: mcp_credential_expired`) instead of failing, and re-storing the credential for that workflow and server promotes it. A park past a limit fails as today. This reverses the 2026-10-18 rule in `apps/scheduler/scheduler/mcp_admission.py` (`McpAnswer.terminal`).

### Why

Product Oracle mints a workflow's MCP credential at submission, sized for the steps (7200 s for a one-step Code map). On 2026-10-26 its 5 Code map runs (tenant u-or-9a0792) waited about 4.7 h parked PROVIDER_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED / account_assign, because the only account lent to the tenant (eng:devops-team) was under its 7-day floor. When BGD lent more accounts at about 22:45Z, all 5 were promoted and FAILED `mcp_credential_expired` at once (credentials lapsed at 20:00Z). Measured from Firestore task records and swarm-scheduler logs.

### Decision

BGD, 2026-10-26 ~22:55Z, picked design (c) over (a) SwarmCloud calls a tenant-registered refresh URL, and (b) Oracle rotates when it sees the step leave PARKED (which races dispatch). Oracle's half: watch for that park and re-store the credential through its existing store call.

### Work

Lane MCP-KEY-PARK, workflow wf_c55587a3316a4f7c9a90.

**Approved** by automatic approval (`plan_approval: auto`) at 2026-10-27T00:04:09 UTC.

The pre-publish gate in apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/prepublish.py marks an outcome timed_out only when the check is GUARDS_CHECK (_run_checks, `timed_out = (check.name == GUARDS_CHECK and ...)`). Any other check that runs into its per-check timeout is a plain FAILED. That includes graph-pytest, whose run_command returns Ran(124, '...[timed out after Ns]', timed_out=True), but the check only hands (status, output) back to _run_checks. So Gate.run opens a fix turn for it, and fix_prompt names no time budget. In task_f5abe2567f79434f9ed4 the agent re-ran the same 59-file pytest selection and the 5400 s runner deadline killed it. The fix: (1) _run_checks marks ANY FAILED check whose output carries the timeout marker as timed_out, with reason 'ran out of time'. That is the '[timed out after Ns]' suffix run_command writes; guards keep their 'ran past N s' form too. Such a check goes in the fix prompt's 'Not yours to fix' line and does not open a fix turn on its own. (2) Gate.run / _second_turn work out guard parts only from a timed-out GUARDS_CHECK outcome. Today `parts = max(guards_parts(o.output) for o in timed_out)` returns GUARDS_MIN_PARTS for any timed-out outcome, so a graph-pytest timeout would wrongly start a sharded guards re-run. (3) fix_prompt states the seconds of the step's budget left (remaining()). It says the guard script is re-run in parts by the worker, and any other check that timed out is not re-run at all, and tells the agent not to run a timed-out check or its test selection itself. Red-first tests drive a real Gate with a fake runner whose graph-pytest returns Ran(124, ..., timed_out=True): record['fix_turn'] is False and resume is never called, as against main, where it is called.

#### Requirements
1. _run_checks marks any check that timed out (not only GUARDS_CHECK) as timed_out=True with reason 'ran out of time', e.g. a graph-pytest killed at CHECK_TIMEOUT_SECONDS.

4. fix_prompt states the step's remaining budget in seconds (remaining()) and tells the agent not to re-run a check that timed out.
5. A timed-out non-guards check does not trigger the sharded guards re-run; guard parts come only from a timed-out GUARDS_CHECK outcome.

<!-- swarmcloud-issue-run:run_c380a95bb80549fda117:plan -->
### SwarmCloud plan for #2506

**Approved** by bogdan at 2026-10-27T00:15:51 UTC.

**Mode:** one agent · **Estimate:** 2.5 agent-hours · **Revision:** 1 · **Digest:** `sha256:a128b1de8bfb872721e811f5b218595ae5c8e3012d4e486eb18be92fab6b8163`

The end-of-agent publish (`Worker._publish_git` in apps/agent-worker/agent_worker/lifecycle.py) decides the workflow route from `_workflow_paths`, whose range excludes only `_workflow_negatives(floor)`: the clone base and the merged default-branch commit. It never reads where origin's publish branch currently stands. In the measured case (ci-fix task_1297d8f4, PR #2446), HEAD was the owner's commit 89507cf, which was already the PR branch's tip. The worker still counted that commit's workflow files as the round's own and sent a no-op push through the broker, whose single call answered api_unavailable. The step ended publish_failed when nothing needed pushing. The fix reads origin's current tip of the publish branch from the forge (`fetch_branch_tip`, token-bearing, run in the worker-owned publish repository). When HEAD equals that tip, or the tip already contains HEAD, the publish ends as the existing `no_change` result (`BASE_MERGE_NO_CHANGE_FIELD`, picked up by `_no_change_after_publish`) and makes no broker call and no token push. Otherwise the tip, when it is an ancestor of HEAD, joins `_workflow_negatives`, so commits origin already has are neither listed as the round's workflow paths nor bundled. They are also sent as `haves`. This follows the shape of `_push_onto_base_merge`'s no_change end (#2179).

#### Requirements

### SwarmCloud plan for #2508

**Approved** by automatic approval (`plan_approval: auto`) at 2026-10-27T00:09:04 UTC.

**Mode:** one agent · **Estimate:** 1.5 agent-hours · **Revision:** 1 · **Digest:** `sha256:f12bf68bbee0ff2fc9c4e5e8dadccfe233de2ca05ce460887b870d07f6cdc8d5`

In an agent container (SWARM_TASK_ID set), apps/swarm-ui/vitest.config.ts caps vitest only through the top-level maxWorkers (agentMaxWorkers sized to the cgroup memory limit: 1 worker at 5 GiB). In vitest 3.2.7 a forks pool takes poolOptions.forks.maxForks ahead of maxWorkers, and CLI options are merged over the config file, so an agent that ran `npx vitest run --pool=forks --poolOptions.forks.maxForks=3` got 3 forks, filled the 5 GiB browser pod and was OOM-killed; its review and fix steps were swept (f-042/043/044). The change makes the agent cap hold whatever the command line says: when SWARM_TASK_ID is set, the effective worker count of every pool (forks maxForks/minForks, threads maxThreads/minThreads, vmForks, vmThreads, and the top-level maxWorkers/minWorkers) is clamped to agentMaxWorkers AFTER vitest has merged CLI options into the config -- by a hook that sees the resolved config (e.g. a plugin's configureVitest hook, available in vitest >= 3.1), not merely by writing poolOptions into the config object, which a CLI --poolOptions flag would override in the same way it overrode maxWorkers. The clamp is a pure exported helper in src/vitestWorkers.ts. A red-first test resolves the real config through vitest's node API with an agent env and maxForks=3 (and --maxWorkers=3) passed as CLI options and asserts the forks stay at agentMaxWorkers; outside an agent container nothing changes (CI and laptops keep vitest's defaults).

#### Requirements
1. With SWARM_TASK_ID set, a command-line --poolOptions.forks.maxForks larger than agentMaxWorkers cannot raise the number of forks vitest runs above agentMaxWorkers.
2. The same clamp holds for poolOptions.threads.maxThreads (and the vmForks/vmThreads equivalents) and for a command-line --maxWorkers.
3. minForks/minThreads (and minWorkers) are pinned so they never exceed the cap, which vitest would otherwise reject or honour above it.
4. Outside an agent container (SWARM_TASK_ID unset or empty: CI, a laptop) vitest's defaults and any CLI pool options are left untouched.
5. A test fails before the fix and passes after it: it resolves vitest.config.ts with an agent env and maxForks=3 on the CLI and asserts the forks stay at agentMaxWorkers (settling vitest 3.2.7's option precedence by measurement, not assumption).
6. agentMaxWorkers stays gated on `if (!env.SWARM_TASK_ID) return undefined` so tests/unit/worker/test_agent_env_carries_task_id.py keeps holding the env name the worker passes.

#### Overlaps with open work
- [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2504](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/issues/2504) (issue): Same incident family (agents filling their pod's memory): #2504 asks run_cli_agent to give the agent a memory/CPU budget in its prompt and env caps such as PYTEST_XDIST_AUTO_NUM_WORKERS. - [bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud#2507](https://github.com/bogdan-alexandrescu/SwarmCloud/issues/2507) (issue): Covers the other half of f-042's cause: the agent's prompt (PUBLISH_PARAGRAPH in cliagent.py) says nothing about the memory limit or parallel/backgrounded test runs, which is why it ran four parallel Bash loops. Different file; this plan does not change the prompt. Even with the clamp, four parallel vitest processes each at the cap could exceed memory -- #2507 is where that is stopped.

title: A review that says NOT_YET ends the workflow, so every further fix round is a new workflow
body:
### What should change

A workflow carries its own review-then-fix loop: a step kind (working name `fix_until_merge`) that names a review step and `max_rounds`. While the review's `verdict.json` says NOT_YET, SwarmCloud runs a fix on the same branch with the findings as input, then the review again, until MERGE or `max_rounds`, and then parks for a person.

### Why

Product Oracle's lanes run build → review. A NOT_YET today means a whole new workflow (a fix lane plus a re-review): Oracle ran 14 workflows on 2026-10-26, 5 of them fix rounds. SwarmCloud's own lanes hit the same wall: implement → review → fix → re-review → merge ends `verdict_not_merge` when the re-review still says NOT_YET, and CLD then sends a new fix lane by hand. Only one review-fix round compiles today: under `integrate` only the integrator may be gated, so a second review needs a gated step that is not the publisher (docs/workflows.md, "What this does not do"; apps/swarm-api/swarm_api/issueruns.py on `fix_rounds`). The platform already appends its own rounds to a running workflow (`mergewake._append_round_step`: ci-fix:N, conflict-fix:N, pick-fix:N).

### Decision

BGD (2026-10-26 ~5:20 PM PDT in Product Oracle's session, confirmed here ~00:10Z): wanted, **design first**. A design lane writes docs/design/fix-loop.md with the owner's questions; build lanes follow BGD's picks.
